50901.m: Santa Claus's village is in Finland.

50902.q: Helsinki is the capital of which country?
50902.e: Helsinki is the largest city in Finland. It lies in the south of the country by the sea.
50902.m: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

50903.e: Helsinki lies on the Gulf of Finland. This is part of the Baltic Sea.
50903.m: Helsinki is on the Baltic Sea.

50904.q: What colour is the famous cathedral of Helsinki?
50904.e: Helsinki Cathedral is white and has green domes. It stands at the top of a big flight of steps above Senate Square.

50905.q: What stands on the islands of Suomenlinna off Helsinki?
50905.e: Suomenlinna is a fortress on islands off Helsinki. It was meant to protect the city from the sea and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
50905.m: Suomenlinna is a sea fortress off Helsinki.

50906.q: Which big sporting event took place in Helsinki in 1952?
50906.e: The 1952 Summer Olympics took place in Helsinki. The Olympic Stadium is still standing today.
50906.m: Helsinki was an Olympic city in 1952.

50907.q: Which capital can you reach from Helsinki by ferry in only about two hours?
50907.e: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia and lies opposite Helsinki. By ferry the journey takes only about two hours.
50907.m: Ferries sail from Helsinki to Tallinn.

50908.q: Which languages are on the street signs in Helsinki?
50908.e: Finland has two official languages. That is why street names in Helsinki are written in Finnish and Swedish.
50908.m: In Helsinki, signs are in Finnish and Swedish.

50909.q: Why is Iceland called a volcanic island?
a: Because it was formed by volcanoes
Because it is made entirely of sand
Because it is in the Mediterranean
50909.e: Iceland grew out of the sea through volcanic eruptions. There are still many active volcanoes there today.

50910.q: What is the capital of Iceland?
50910.e: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of an independent country. A large share of Iceland's people live there.
50910.m: Reykjavík is the capital of Iceland.

50911.q: What do you call a hot spring that shoots water high into the air?
50911.e: The word geyser comes from Iceland. The geyser Strokkur shoots a column of water into the air every few minutes.
50911.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

50912.q: What is Iceland often called because of its volcanoes and glaciers?
a: The land of fire and ice
50912.e: Iceland has hot volcanoes and at the same time big glaciers. That is why people speak of the land of fire and ice.
50912.m: Iceland is the land of fire and ice.

50913.q: What is the largest glacier in Iceland called?
50913.e: Vatnajökull is the largest glacier in Iceland. There are even volcanoes under its ice.

50914.q: Which Icelandic volcano brought air traffic in Europe to a standstill with its ash cloud in 2010?
50914.e: Eyjafjallajökull erupted in 2010. Its ash drifted over Europe, and many aeroplanes had to stay on the ground.

50915.q: What is the special gait of the Icelandic horse called, in which the rider is hardly shaken about?
50915.e: The Icelandic horse can do the tölt. It moves fast and very smoothly, so the rider is hardly shaken about.
50915.m: Icelandic horses can do the tölt.

50916.q: Which bird with a colourful beak nests in large numbers on the cliffs of Iceland?
50916.e: The puffin has a colourful beak. Millions of these birds nest on steep cliffs in Iceland.

50917.q: What do many houses in Iceland use for heating?
50917.e: Under Iceland the earth is very hot. Hot water from the ground is used directly to heat the houses.
50917.m: In Iceland, homes are heated with heat from the earth.

a: In the far north of Europe
50918.e: Lapland is in the north of Norway, Sweden and Finland. A small part also belongs to Russia.
50918.m: Lapland is in the far north of Europe.

50919.q: What are the people who have lived in Lapland for a long time called?
50919.e: The Sámi are the indigenous people of Lapland. Many of them have kept reindeer for centuries.
50919.m: The Sámi are the people of Lapland.

50920.q: What happens to the sun in Lapland in summer?
a: It does not set at night
It does not rise at all
50920.e: In the far north, the midnight sun shines in summer. Then it stays light even at night.
50920.m: In summer the midnight sun shines in Lapland.

50921.q: What is the time in winter when the sun does not rise at all in Lapland called?
50921.e: In winter, the sun stays below the horizon for weeks in the far north. This dark time is called the polar night.
50921.m: During the polar night the sun does not rise.

50922.q: Which coloured lights can you see in the sky over Lapland in winter?
50922.e: The northern lights glow green, sometimes also red or purple. They are caused by particles from the sun.
50922.m: The northern lights glow over Lapland in winter.

50923.q: Which imaginary line on Earth runs through Lapland?
50923.e: The Arctic Circle runs right across Lapland. It goes all the way round the Earth in the far north.
50923.m: The Arctic Circle runs through Lapland.

50924.q: What is the weather in Lapland usually like in winter?
50924.e: In winter there is a lot of snow in Lapland. It is often far below zero degrees.
50924.m: Winter in Lapland is cold and snowy.

50925.q: Which animals pull Santa Claus's sleigh in stories?
50925.e: In many Christmas stories, reindeer pull the sleigh.

50926.q: What do reindeer like to eat most in winter?
50926.e: Reindeer scrape in the snow with their hooves to find lichen. That is why one kind of lichen is even called reindeer lichen.

50927.q: Why do the Sámi in the far north keep reindeer?
50927.e: The Sámi are a people of the far north. Their reindeer provide meat and warm hides. In the past they also pulled sledges.
50927.m: The Sámi keep reindeer for meat and hides.

50928.q: What is the name of the reindeer with the red nose from the Christmas song?
50928.e: Rudolph lights the way through the fog with his red nose. Many children all over the world know the song.
50928.m: Rudolph is the reindeer with the red nose.

50929.q: Which is the largest kind of deer in the world?
50929.e: The moose is the largest deer. A male can be more than 2 metres tall at the shoulder.
50929.m: The moose is the largest deer in the world.

50930.q: What do the antlers of a male moose often look like?
50930.e: Many bull moose have wide, flat antlers. That is why they are called palmate antlers, shaped like a shovel.

50931.q: What do many road signs in Sweden warn about?
50931.e: A great many moose live in Sweden. They often cross roads, so there are special warning signs.
50931.m: In Sweden, signs warn about moose.

a: Plants such as leaves and twigs
50932.e: Moose are herbivores. They eat leaves, twigs, bark and also water plants.

50933.q: What are moose surprisingly good at?
50933.e: Moose are good swimmers. They even swim across wide lakes and rivers.

50934.q: What is a male moose called?
50934.e: Male moose are called bulls, females are called cows. The young are called calves.
50934.m: A male moose is called a bull.

50935.e: The Faroes lie in the North Atlantic between Iceland, Norway and Scotland. It is windy there and often foggy.
50935.m: The Faroes are in the North Atlantic.

50936.q: Which kingdom do the Faroe Islands belong to?
50936.e: The Faroes belong to the Kingdom of Denmark. But they run most things themselves.
50936.m: The Faroes belong to the Kingdom of Denmark.

50937.q: What does the name “Faroe” probably mean?
50937.e: A great many sheep live on the islands. That is why the name is usually explained as “sheep islands”.

50938.q: How many larger islands make up the Faroes?
50938.e: The Faroes are made up of 18 larger islands. All but one are inhabited.
50938.m: The Faroes are made up of 18 islands.

50939.q: What is the capital of the Faroes?
50939.e: Tórshavn is one of the smallest capitals in the world. It has colourful houses with grass roofs.
50939.m: Tórshavn is the capital of the Faroes.

50940.e: Poland has a long coastline on the Baltic Sea in the north. There are many sandy beaches there.
50940.m: Poland is on the Baltic Sea.

50941.q: Which long river flows right across Poland?
50941.e: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland. It flows from the mountains in the south to the Baltic Sea.
50941.m: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland.

50942.q: What colours is the flag of Poland?
50942.e: The Polish flag has two stripes. It is white at the top and red at the bottom.
50942.m: The flag of Poland is white and red.

50943.q: What is the money in Poland called?
50943.e: In Poland you pay with the złoty. Poland has not introduced the euro.
50943.m: In Poland you pay with the złoty.

50944.q: Which neighbouring country does Poland have in the west?
50944.e: In the west, Poland borders Germany. Much of the border runs along the Oder and Neisse rivers.

50945.q: Which famous composer came from Poland?
50945.e: Frédéric Chopin was born in Poland in 1810. He wrote mainly beautiful music for the piano.
50945.m: Frédéric Chopin was a famous composer from Poland.

50946.q: Which beautiful old city in Poland used to be the capital for a long time?
50946.e: Kraków was the capital of Poland for many centuries. Wawel Castle stands there.
50946.m: Kraków used to be the capital of Poland.

50947.q: Which scientist from Poland worked out that the Earth goes round the sun?
50947.e: Nicolaus Copernicus lived in Poland around 500 years ago. He realised that the Earth circles the sun and not the other way round.
50947.m: Copernicus realised that the Earth circles the sun.

50948.e: Warsaw lies on both banks of the Vistula. Many bridges connect the two sides.

50949.q: Which mythical creature is on the coat of arms of Warsaw?
50949.e: The coat of arms of Warsaw shows a mermaid with a sword and shield. A statue of her stands in the old town.
50949.m: A mermaid is the symbol of Warsaw.

50950.q: Which famous scientist was born in Warsaw?
50950.e: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
50950.m: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw.

50951.q: What happened to the old town of Warsaw after the Second World War?
a: It was turned into a park.
It was turned into a lake.
50951.e: In the Second World War the old town was almost completely destroyed. Afterwards it was rebuilt using old pictures.
50951.m: The old town of Warsaw was rebuilt after the war.

50952.q: What special heritage list does the old town of Warsaw belong to?
50952.e: The old town of Warsaw has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980. That is a list of especially valuable places in the world.
50952.m: The old town of Warsaw is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50953.q: What is the very tall building in the centre of Warsaw called?
50953.e: The Palace of Culture is a big tower block in the middle of Warsaw. It has theatres, cinemas and museums inside.
50953.m: The Palace of Culture is a well-known tower block in Warsaw.

50954.q: Which musician is Warsaw's big airport named after?
50954.e: Warsaw's largest airport is called Warsaw Chopin Airport. It bears the name of the famous composer.
50954.m: Warsaw's airport is named after Chopin.

50955.q: Which city is the largest in Poland?
50955.e: Warsaw has more than 1.8 million inhabitants (as of 2020). No other city in Poland is as big.
50955.m: Warsaw is the largest city in Poland.

50956.q: What is the capital of the Czech Republic?
50956.e: The capital of the Czech Republic is Prague. It is in the west of the country.
50956.m: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.

50957.q: What is the money in the Czech Republic called?
50957.e: In the Czech Republic you pay with the Czech koruna. The euro is not the national currency there.
50957.m: In the Czech Republic you pay with koruna.

50958.q: Does the Czech Republic have a coastline on the sea?
a: No, it has no sea coast.
50958.e: The Czech Republic is a landlocked country like Switzerland. It is surrounded by other countries on all sides.
50958.m: Like Switzerland, the Czech Republic has no sea.

50959.q: Which famous cartoon character comes from the Czech Republic?
50959.e: The Little Mole was created by the Czech artist Zdeněk Miler. Children all over the world know his films.
50959.m: The Little Mole comes from the Czech Republic.

50960.q: Which big river has its source in the Czech Republic and flows into Germany?
50960.e: The Elbe rises in the Giant Mountains in the Czech Republic. It flows through Germany to the North Sea.
50960.m: The Elbe has its source in the Czech Republic.

50961.q: Which country did the Czech Republic and Slovakia come from in 1993?
50961.e: Until the end of 1992, the Czech Republic and Slovakia together formed Czechoslovakia. On 1 January 1993 they became two countries.
50961.m: The Czech Republic and Slovakia used to be one country.

50962.q: What is the highest mountain in the Czech Republic called?
50962.e: Sněžka is around 1,600 metres high. It is in the Giant Mountains on the border with Poland.
50962.m: Sněžka is the highest mountain in the Czech Republic.

50963.q: What is the western part of the Czech Republic, where Prague is, called?
50963.e: The Czech Republic is made up mainly of Bohemia and Moravia. Prague is in Bohemia.

50964.q: Which neighbouring country does the Czech Republic have to the south?
50964.e: To the south, the Czech Republic borders Austria. Its other neighbours are Germany, Poland and Slovakia.
50964.m: Austria lies south of the Czech Republic.

50965.q: What is the river that flows through Prague called?
50965.e: The Vltava flows through Prague. Later it flows into the Elbe.

50966.q: What is the famous old stone bridge in Prague called?
50966.e: Charles Bridge is more than 600 years old. Many stone statues stand on it.
50966.m: Charles Bridge is the most famous bridge in Prague.

50967.q: What does the famous old clock on Prague's town hall show on the hour?
50967.e: The Astronomical Clock in Prague is around 600 years old. On the hour, figures of the apostles pass by little windows.
50967.m: Figures move on Prague's town hall clock.

50968.q: Which huge complex on a hill is a landmark of Prague?
50968.e: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world. Today the President of the Czech Republic works there.
50968.m: Prague Castle is a huge castle complex.

50969.q: What nickname does Prague have because of its many towers?
50969.e: Prague has a great many church towers and gate towers. That is why it is called the City of a Hundred Spires.
50969.m: Prague is also called the City of a Hundred Spires.

50970.q: Which famous writer was born in Prague?
50970.e: Franz Kafka was born in Prague in 1883. He wrote his books in German.

50971.q: What is the big, long square in Prague's New Town called?
50971.e: Wenceslas Square is named after Saint Wenceslas. The National Museum stands at its upper end.
50971.m: Wenceslas Square is a big square in Prague.

50972.q: What colour are many roofs in Prague's old town?
50972.e: Many houses in Prague have red tiled roofs. That is why the old town looks red from above.
50972.m: Prague has lots of red roofs.

50973.q: What is the capital of Hungary?
50973.e: The capital of Hungary is Budapest. About one in five people in the country lives there.
50973.m: Budapest is the capital of Hungary.

50974.q: What is the big lake in Hungary called?
50974.e: Lake Balaton is called Plattensee in German. It is the largest lake in Central Europe.
50974.m: The big lake in Hungary is called Balaton.

50975.q: What is the money in Hungary called?
50975.e: In Hungary you pay with the forint. Hungary has not introduced the euro.
50975.m: In Hungary you pay with the forint.

50976.q: Which red spice is typical of Hungary?
50976.e: Hungary is known for its paprika powder. It goes into many dishes, for example goulash.
50976.m: Paprika is a typical spice from Hungary.

50977.q: Which stew with meat and paprika comes from Hungary?
50977.e: Goulash is a dish from Hungary. In the past, cattle herders cooked it in a pot over the fire.
50977.m: Goulash is a dish from Hungary.

50978.q: Which well-known toy did the Hungarian Ernő Rubik invent?
50978.e: Ernő Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube in 1974. You have to twist it so that each side has only one colour.
50978.m: The Rubik's Cube was invented in Hungary.

50979.q: Which language is spoken in Hungary?
50979.e: People in Hungary speak Hungarian. The language is hardly related to German or the Slavic languages.

50980.q: Which neighbouring country does Hungary have in the west?
50980.e: In the west, Hungary borders Austria. Hungary has no coastline on the sea.

50981.q: Which river divides Budapest into two parts?
50981.e: The Danube flows right through the middle of Budapest. Many bridges connect the two banks.
50981.m: The Danube flows through the middle of Budapest.

50982.q: Budapest has one of the oldest underground railways in Europe. In which year did it first run?
50982.e: Budapest's first underground line opened in 1896. It was the first electric underground railway on the European mainland.
50982.m: Budapest's underground has been running since 1896.

50983.q: Which huge building with a dome stands in Budapest right on the Danube?
50983.e: The Hungarian Parliament is one of the largest parliament buildings in the world. It stands on the bank of the Danube.
50983.m: The Parliament in Budapest stands on the Danube.

50984.q: What is the famous bridge with two pairs of lions in Budapest called?
50984.e: The Chain Bridge was the first permanent bridge between Buda and Pest. Stone lions lie at both ends.
50984.m: The Chain Bridge connects Buda and Pest.

50985.q: With its many warm springs, what is Budapest known for?
50985.e: There are many warm springs under Budapest. They supply large thermal baths, for example the Széchenyi Baths.
50985.m: Budapest is known for its thermal baths.

50986.q: What is the green island in the Danube in the middle of Budapest called?
50986.e: Margaret Island lies in the Danube between Buda and Pest. It is a big park without many cars.
50986.m: Margaret Island is a park in the Danube.

50987.q: What is the beautiful viewing terrace with little towers in Buda called?
50987.e: Fisherman's Bastion stands on Castle Hill in Buda. From there you can see far across the Danube and the Parliament.
50987.m: Fisherman's Bastion is a viewpoint in Budapest.

50988.q: Who used to live in the big palace on Castle Hill in Budapest?
50988.e: The big Royal Palace stands on Castle Hill in Budapest. The kings of Hungary used to live there.
50988.m: Kings used to live in Budapest's Royal Palace.

50989.q: What is the capital of Slovakia?
50989.e: The capital of Slovakia is Bratislava. In German it used to be called Pressburg.
50989.m: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia.

50990.q: What money do you pay with in Slovakia?
50990.e: Slovakia introduced the euro in 2009. Before that there was the Slovak koruna.
50990.m: In Slovakia you pay with the euro.

50991.q: What are the high mountains in the north of Slovakia called?
50991.e: The High Tatras are the highest range of the Carpathians. Part of them belongs to Poland.
50991.m: The High Tatras are in the north of Slovakia.

50992.q: Which big river flows through Bratislava?
50992.e: The Danube flows through Bratislava. Ships sail along it as far as Vienna and Budapest.

50993.q: Which language is spoken in Slovakia?
50993.e: People in Slovakia speak Slovak. The language is closely related to Czech.

50994.q: Does Slovakia have a coastline on the sea?
a: No, it has no sea coast.
50994.e: Slovakia is a landlocked country. It has no coast, just like Switzerland.

50995.q: Which capital lies very close to Bratislava, only around 60 kilometres away?
50995.e: Bratislava lies right on the border with Austria. It is only about 60 kilometres to Vienna.
50995.m: Bratislava and Vienna are close to each other.

50996.q: What colours is the flag of Slovakia?
50996.e: The Slovak flag has three stripes in white, blue and red. On the left there is also a coat of arms with a double cross.
50996.m: The flag of Slovakia is white, blue and red.

50997.q: What is the capital of Romania?
50997.e: The capital of Romania is Bucharest. Do not mix it up with Budapest in Hungary.
50997.m: Bucharest is the capital of Romania.

50998.e: In the east, Romania has a coastline on the Black Sea. The port of Constanța is there.
50998.m: Romania is on the Black Sea.

50999.q: Which big mountain range curves through Romania?
50999.e: The Carpathians form a big arc through Romania. Many bears and wolves still live there.

51000.q: Where does the Danube flow into the sea in Romania?
51000.e: Just before the Black Sea, the Danube splits into many branches. This area is called the Danube Delta and is a paradise for birds.
51000.m: The Danube ends in the Danube Delta on the Black Sea.

51001.q: Which well-known spooky character is linked with Romania?
51001.e: The vampire Count Dracula comes from a famous book. In it he lives in a castle in the mountains of Romania. Bran Castle is often called Dracula's Castle.
51001.m: The Dracula story is set in Romania.

51002.q: What is the region in the middle of Romania called?
51002.e: Transylvania is called Siebenbürgen in German. There are many old castles and fortified churches there.
51002.m: Transylvania lies in the middle of Romania.

51003.q: What is the money in Romania called?
51003.e: In Romania you pay with the leu. The word means lion.
51003.m: In Romania you pay with the leu.

51004.q: Which gymnast from Romania was the first to get a perfect 10 at the Olympics in 1976?
51004.e: Nadia Comăneci performed without a single mistake in Montreal in 1976. She was only 14 years old and was the first to get the perfect score of 10.
51004.m: Nadia Comăneci was the first to score a perfect 10.

51005.q: Which big wild animals live in the forests of Romania?
51005.e: A great many brown bears live in the mountain forests of Romania, more than in almost any other country in Europe.
51005.m: Lots of brown bears live in Romania.

51006.q: What is the capital of Bulgaria?
51006.e: The capital of Bulgaria is Sofia. It lies at the foot of Mount Vitosha.
51006.m: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.

51007.e: In the east, Bulgaria has a coast on the Black Sea. Many people go there for beach holidays.
51007.m: Bulgaria is on the Black Sea.

51008.q: Which alphabet is used in Bulgaria?
51008.e: In Bulgaria people write with Cyrillic letters. This alphabet was created more than 1000 years ago in the area of Bulgaria.
51008.m: In Bulgaria people write in Cyrillic.

51009.q: Which flowers is Bulgaria famous for?
51009.e: Huge fields of roses grow in Bulgaria. Their petals are used to make valuable rose oil for perfume.
51009.m: Bulgaria is famous for its roses.

51010.q: What does a nod of the head often mean in Bulgaria?
51010.e: In Bulgaria nodding often means “no” and shaking your head means “yes”. Here it is exactly the other way round.
51010.m: In Bulgaria a nod often means no.

51011.q: Which dairy product is especially well known in Bulgaria?
51011.e: Bulgaria is famous for its yoghurt. One yoghurt bacterium is even named after the country.

51012.q: What is the name of the large church with the golden main dome in Sofia?
51012.e: The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is the landmark of Sofia. Its large main dome is covered in gold.
51012.m: The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is in Sofia.

51013.q: Which famous monastery lies in the mountains of Bulgaria?
51013.e: Rila Monastery lies in the Rila Mountains. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and has colourful paintings on its walls.
51013.m: Rila Monastery is a famous monastery in Bulgaria.

51014.q: What is the capital of Ukraine?
51014.e: The capital of Ukraine is Kyiv. It is the largest city in the country.
51014.m: Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine.

51015.q: Which big river flows through Kyiv?
51015.e: The Dnipro, also called the Dnieper, flows right through Kyiv. It is the longest river in Ukraine.

51016.q: Which sea is on Ukraine’s southern coast?
51016.e: In the south, Ukraine has a coast on the Black Sea. A well-known port city there is Odesa.
51016.m: Ukraine is on the Black Sea.

51017.q: Which yellow flowers grow in huge fields in Ukraine?
51017.e: Ukraine is one of the countries that grow the most sunflowers. Oil is made from the seeds.
51017.m: Lots of sunflowers grow in Ukraine.

51018.q: Which red soup made from beetroot is typical of Ukraine?
51018.e: Borscht is cooked with beetroot, which is why it is red. The soup is very popular in Ukraine.
51018.m: Borscht is a red soup from Ukraine.

51019.q: Which country is the largest by area that lies entirely in Europe?
51019.e: Russia is bigger, but it also lies in Asia. Of the countries that lie entirely in Europe, Ukraine is the largest.
51019.m: Ukraine is the largest country entirely in Europe.

51020.q: What is the money in Ukraine called?
51020.e: In Ukraine people pay with the hryvnia. It is pronounced roughly “HRIV-nya”.
51020.m: In Ukraine people pay with the hryvnia.

51021.q: Moscow is the capital of which country?
51021.e: Moscow is the capital of Russia. Russia is the largest country in the world.
51021.m: Moscow is the capital of Russia.

51022.e: The river through Moscow is called the Moskva. The city takes its name from this river.

51023.q: What is the Moscow underground especially known for?
51023.e: Many stations of the Moscow Metro look like palaces. They have chandeliers, marble and colourful pictures.
51023.m: The Moscow Metro has magnificent stations.

51024.q: What is the name of the famous theatre for ballet and opera in Moscow?
51024.e: The Bolshoi Theatre is one of the best-known theatres in the world. Bolshoi means “big” in Russian.
51024.m: The Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow is famous for ballet.

51025.q: What do the colourful towers of the famous church on Red Square in Moscow look like?
51025.e: St Basil’s Cathedral has colourful domes that look like onions. They are called onion domes.
51025.m: The church on Red Square has colourful onion domes.

51026.q: Which old fortress with red walls stands right next to Red Square?
51026.e: The Kremlin is a fortress with red brick walls and many towers. Today the Russian government works there.
51026.m: The Kremlin is on Red Square.

51027.q: In which big city is Red Square?
51027.e: Red Square is in the middle of Moscow, the capital of Russia. Long ago its name also meant “beautiful square”.

51029.q: Which three countries are called the Baltic States?
51029.e: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania lie next to each other on the Baltic Sea. Together they are called the Baltic States.
51029.m: The Baltic States are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

51030.q: Which sea are the Baltic States on?
51030.e: All three Baltic States have a coast on the Baltic Sea. That is where their name comes from.
51030.m: The Baltic States are on the Baltic Sea.

51031.q: What is the capital of Estonia?
51031.e: The capital of Estonia is Tallinn. Its old town with its town wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
51031.m: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia.

51032.q: What is the capital of Latvia?
51032.e: The capital of Latvia is Riga. It is the largest city in the Baltic States.
51032.m: Riga is the capital of Latvia.

51033.q: What is the capital of Lithuania?
51033.e: The capital of Lithuania is Vilnius. It has a large baroque old town.
51033.m: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania.

51034.q: Which money do people use today in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania?
51034.e: All three Baltic States have introduced the euro. Lithuania was the last to join, in 2015.
51034.m: In the Baltic States people pay with the euro.

51035.q: What did around two million people form across the three Baltic States in 1989?
51035.e: In the Baltic Way, people held hands over about 650 kilometres. In this peaceful way they showed that they wanted to be free.
51035.m: The Baltic Way was a huge human chain.

51036.q: Which of the three Baltic States lies furthest north?
51036.e: Estonia is in the north, Latvia in the middle and Lithuania in the south. From Estonia, Finland is close across the sea.
51036.m: Estonia is the most northern Baltic State.

51037.q: Which money do people use in Greece today?
51037.e: Greece is one of the countries that use the euro. There have been euro coins and notes there since 2002.
51037.m: In Greece people pay with the euro.

51038.q: What colours is the flag of Greece?
51038.e: The Greek flag has blue and white stripes and a white cross on a blue square in the top left corner.
51038.m: The flag of Greece is blue and white.

51039.q: How many stripes does the flag of Greece have?
51039.e: The flag has nine horizontal stripes, five blue and four white.
51039.m: The Greek flag has nine stripes.

51040.q: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
51040.e: The first modern Olympic Games took place in Athens in 1896. This was a way of remembering the Games of ancient Greece.
51040.m: The first modern Olympic Games were in Athens in 1896.

51041.q: Which language is spoken in Greece?
51041.e: In Greece people speak Greek. The language has its own letters.

51042.q: Which tree grows very often in Greece and gives a fine oil?
51042.e: Very many olive trees grow in Greece. Olive oil is pressed from the olives.
51042.m: Lots of olive trees grow in Greece.

51043.q: Which white cheese goes in a Greek salad?
51043.e: Feta is a white, salty cheese from Greece. It is made from sheep’s milk, often with a little goat’s milk.
51043.m: Feta cheese goes in a Greek salad.

51044.q: In which city is the Acropolis?
51044.e: The Acropolis is in the middle of Athens, the capital of Greece.

a: A citadel hill with ancient temples
51045.e: The Acropolis is a high rock on which the ancient Greeks built temples and gateways.
51045.m: The Acropolis is a citadel hill with ancient temples.

51046.q: What is the most famous temple on the Acropolis called?
51046.e: The Parthenon is the largest and best-known temple on the Acropolis.
51046.m: The most famous temple on the Acropolis is the Parthenon.

51047.q: For which goddess was the Parthenon built?
51047.e: The Parthenon was dedicated to the goddess Athena. She was the protector of the city of Athens.
51047.m: The Parthenon is the temple of the goddess Athena.

51048.q: What material is the Parthenon built from?
51048.e: The Parthenon was built from white marble. The stone came from a quarry near Athens.
51048.m: The Parthenon is built from marble.

51049.q: Roughly how old is the Parthenon?
51049.e: The Parthenon was built about 2500 years ago, in the 5th century BC.
51049.m: The Parthenon is about 2500 years old.

51050.q: What holds up the roof of the Parthenon in Athens?
51050.e: Many tall marble columns stand all around the Parthenon. They hold up the roof of the temple.
51050.m: Marble columns hold up the roof of the Parthenon.

51051.q: What do the stone figures of women on a temple on the Acropolis hold up?
51051.e: At the Erechtheion temple, six stone figures of women hold up the roof of a porch. They are called caryatids.
51051.m: At the Erechtheion, stone figures of women hold up a roof.

51052.e: In Greek, “akros” means “high” or “top” and “polis” means “city”. The Acropolis lies high above Athens.

51053.q: What is the sea with many islands between Greece and Turkey called?
51053.e: The Aegean Sea is part of the Mediterranean. Very many Greek islands lie in it.
51053.m: The Aegean Sea lies between Greece and Turkey.

51054.q: What is the group of islands that Santorini and Mykonos belong to called?
51054.e: The Cyclades are a group of islands in the Aegean Sea. Santorini, Mykonos and Naxos belong to them.
51054.m: Santorini and Mykonos belong to the Cyclades.

51055.q: On which Greek island is the ancient palace of Knossos?
51055.e: The palace of Knossos is on Crete. It is very old and is one of the best-known excavations in Greece.
51055.m: The palace of Knossos is on Crete.

51056.q: Which Greek island lies very close to Albania?
51056.e: Corfu lies in the Ionian Sea in north-western Greece. From there you can see the coast of Albania.

51057.q: On which island did the Colossus, one of the Seven Wonders of the World, once stand?
51057.e: The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge statue of the sun god Helios. An earthquake knocked it down a long time ago.
51057.m: The Colossus stood on the island of Rhodes.

51058.q: Which buildings on a hill is the island of Mykonos known for?
51058.e: On Mykonos there are white, round windmills. In the past they were used to grind grain.
51058.m: Mykonos is known for its windmills.

51059.q: How do many people travel from one Greek island to the next?
51059.e: There is sea between the islands. That is why big ships, the ferries, sail from island to island.
51059.m: You travel between the Greek islands by ferry.

51060.q: In an ancient legend, which island is the home of the hero Odysseus?
51060.e: In the ancient legend, Odysseus travels for ten years before he finally gets home to the island of Ithaca.
51060.m: Odysseus came from the island of Ithaca.

51061.q: How was the island of Santorini formed?
51061.e: Santorini was formed by a volcano. In a huge eruption, the middle of the island collapsed into the sea.

51062.q: What colour are most houses on Santorini?
51062.e: The houses on Santorini are painted white. The white paint keeps the houses cooler in the sun.
51062.m: The houses on Santorini are mostly white.

51063.q: What colour are many church domes on Santorini?
51063.e: Many churches on Santorini have blue domes. Together with the white houses, this makes a very famous view.
51063.m: On Santorini many churches have blue domes.

51064.q: What is the huge crater in the sea that Santorini lies around called?
51064.e: A caldera is a large hollow that forms when a volcano collapses in on itself. At Santorini it is filled with seawater.

51065.q: What do many people like to watch on Santorini in the evening?
51065.e: From the village of Oia you can see the sun set into the sea. Many people come every evening to watch it.
51065.m: The sunsets on Santorini are famous.

51066.q: Where is the main town of Santorini?
a: High up on the edge of the crater
In the middle of a forest
51066.e: The main town is called Fira. It lies high up on the edge of the large volcanic crater.
51066.m: The main town of Santorini lies high up on the crater rim.

51067.q: On which animals can you ride up the many steps to the main town of Santorini?
51067.e: Very many steps lead from the old harbour up to Fira. You can walk, take the cable car or ride on donkeys and mules.
51067.m: On Santorini donkeys carry people up the steps.

51068.q: What buried the ancient town of Akrotiri on Santorini about 3600 years ago?
51068.e: In a huge volcanic eruption, Akrotiri was buried under ash. Today researchers are digging out the well-preserved houses.
51068.m: The ancient town of Akrotiri lay under volcanic ash.

51069.q: Roughly how high is Mount Olympus?
51069.e: The highest peak of Mount Olympus is called Mytikas and is about 2918 metres high.
51069.m: Mount Olympus is just under 3000 metres high.

51070.q: According to the ancient legends, who lived on Mount Olympus?
51070.e: The ancient Greeks believed that their most important gods lived on Mount Olympus.
51070.m: According to the legends, the gods lived on Mount Olympus.

51071.q: What is the name of the king of the gods on Mount Olympus?
51071.e: In the Greek legends, Zeus was the most powerful god and ruled over the other gods.
51071.m: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods.

51072.q: In the legends, what does Zeus hurl when he is angry?
51072.e: Zeus was also the god of the sky and the weather. When he was angry, he threw lightning bolts.

51073.q: According to the legends, how many main gods lived on Mount Olympus?
51073.e: The ancient Greeks spoke of twelve Olympian gods, for example Zeus, Hera, Athena and Apollo.
51073.m: Twelve main gods lived on Mount Olympus.

51074.q: Which god from Mount Olympus ruled over the sea?
51074.e: Poseidon was the god of the sea. He carried a trident.
51074.m: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea.

51075.q: Which Swiss mountain is higher than Mount Olympus?
51075.e: The Matterhorn is about 4478 metres high, so it is much higher. The Rigi, Pilatus and the Säntis are all lower than 2600 metres.
51075.m: The Matterhorn is much higher than Mount Olympus.

51076.e: Croatia has a long coast on the Adriatic Sea. The Adriatic is part of the Mediterranean.
51076.m: Croatia is on the Adriatic Sea.

51077.q: Which national park in Croatia is known for its many lakes and waterfalls?
51077.e: In Plitvice Lakes National Park, 16 lakes lie one after another. They are connected by many waterfalls.
51077.m: The Plitvice Lakes have many waterfalls.

51078.q: Which dog breed with black spots is named after a region of Croatia?
51078.e: The Dalmatian is named after Dalmatia. Dalmatia is the coastal region in the south of Croatia.
51078.m: The Dalmatian is named after a region of Croatia.

51079.q: Which item of clothing got its name from Croatian soldiers?
51079.e: About 400 years ago, Croatian soldiers wore knotted neckcloths. This became the cravat, and the word comes from “Croat”.
51079.m: The word cravat comes from the Croats.

51080.q: Which money have people used in Croatia since 2023?
51080.e: Croatia introduced the euro on 1 January 2023. Before that, people paid with the kuna.
51080.m: Croatia has used the euro since 2023.

51081.q: Which pattern can be seen on the coat of arms of Croatia?
51081.e: The coat of arms of Croatia shows red and white squares like a chessboard. You can also see it on the flag.
51081.m: The Croatian coat of arms has a red and white chequerboard.

51082.q: In which Croatian city is there a huge old palace of a Roman emperor?
51082.e: In Split, the Roman emperor Diocletian had a palace built about 1700 years ago. Today people live right inside its walls.
51082.m: Emperor Diocletian’s palace is in Split.

51083.q: In which country is the city of Dubrovnik?
51083.e: Dubrovnik lies in the very south of Croatia on the Adriatic Sea.

51084.q: What surrounds the whole old town of Dubrovnik?
51084.e: A thick town wall with towers runs all around the old town. You can walk all the way round on top of it.
51084.m: The old town of Dubrovnik is surrounded by a wall.

51085.q: Roughly how long is the town wall of Dubrovnik?
51085.e: The town wall is 1940 metres long, so almost 2 kilometres.
51085.m: The wall of Dubrovnik is almost 2 kilometres long.

51086.q: What is the wide main street in Dubrovnik’s old town called?
51086.e: The Stradun is the main street of the old town, about 300 metres long. It is paved with smooth stone.
51086.m: The main street of Dubrovnik is called the Stradun.

51087.e: Dubrovnik lies beautifully by the sea and is therefore often called the “Pearl of the Adriatic”.
51087.m: Dubrovnik is called the Pearl of the Adriatic.

51088.q: How can you get up Mount Srđ above Dubrovnik easily without hiking?
a: By a lift in a tower
51088.e: A cable car goes up Mount Srđ, which is 412 metres high. From the top you can see the whole old town.
51088.m: A cable car goes up Mount Srđ.

51089.q: What was Dubrovnik called in the past, when it was a small republic of its own?
51089.e: For a long time the city was its own republic called Ragusa. It traded by ship all over the Mediterranean.
51089.m: Dubrovnik used to be called Ragusa.

51090.q: Which small island lies just off Dubrovnik and is known for its peacocks?
51090.e: Lokrum is only a short boat ride from the old town. Peacocks roam freely on the island.
51090.m: Peacocks live on the island of Lokrum.

51091.q: Which mythical creature is the symbol of Ljubljana?
51091.e: The dragon is the heraldic animal of Ljubljana. Four metal dragons sit on the Dragon Bridge.
51091.m: The symbol of Ljubljana is a dragon.

51092.q: Which lake in Slovenia has a small island with a church on it?
51092.e: In Lake Bled there is a small island with a church. You get there by wooden boat.
51092.m: In Lake Bled there is an island with a church.

51093.q: What is the highest mountain in Slovenia called?
51093.e: Triglav is 2864 metres high. It is so important that it even appears on Slovenia’s coat of arms.
51093.m: The highest mountain in Slovenia is Triglav.

51094.q: Which country is a neighbour of Slovenia?
51094.e: Slovenia borders Austria, Italy, Hungary and Croatia.
51094.m: Austria is a neighbour of Slovenia.

51095.q: Which pale animal without proper eyes lives in the caves of Slovenia?
51095.e: The olm is an amphibian that lives in the dark. Because it is pale like skin, it is also called the “human fish”.
51095.m: The olm lives in the caves of Slovenia.

51096.q: What is Slovenia’s sea coast like?
51096.e: Slovenia has only a short stretch of coast on the Adriatic Sea, about 47 kilometres long.
51096.m: Slovenia has a very short coast.

51097.q: How do you travel into the big stalactite cave of Postojna?
51097.e: In Postojna Cave, a little train goes several kilometres deep into the mountain.
51097.m: A little train goes into Postojna Cave.

51098.q: In which country is the city of Istanbul?
51098.e: Istanbul is in Turkey. It is the largest city in the country.

51099.q: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey. But which city is the capital?
51099.e: The capital of Turkey is Ankara. The government works there, even though Istanbul is much bigger.
51099.m: The capital of Turkey is Ankara.

51100.q: What is the famous building with a huge dome in Istanbul, which was first a church, called?
51100.e: Hagia Sophia was built as a church about 1500 years ago. Later it became a mosque.
51100.m: Hagia Sophia in Istanbul has a huge dome.

51101.q: Why is the Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul also called the Blue Mosque?
a: Because it stands in the sea
Because it glows blue at night
51101.e: Inside, the mosque is decorated with many thousands of tiles in which blue is an important colour.
51101.m: The Blue Mosque gets its name from blue tiles.

51102.q: What is the huge covered market in Istanbul called?
51102.e: In the Grand Bazaar there are thousands of shops under one roof. It is one of the largest covered markets in the world.

51103.q: What was Istanbul called for a long time in the past?
51103.e: For a long time the city was called Constantinople, after the Roman emperor Constantine.
51103.m: Istanbul used to be called Constantinople.

51104.q: Roughly how many people live in Istanbul (as of 2025)?
51104.e: In 2025 over 15 million people lived in Istanbul. That is clearly more than in the whole of Switzerland.
51104.m: Istanbul has more inhabitants than the whole of Switzerland.

51105.e: The Bosphorus is a narrow waterway between two pieces of land. Something like this is called a strait.

51106.q: Which two seas does the Bosphorus connect?
a: Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
51106.e: The Bosphorus runs from the Black Sea in the north to the Sea of Marmara in the south.
51106.m: The Bosphorus connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara.

51107.q: Which two continents does the Bosphorus separate?
51107.e: On one side of the Bosphorus is Europe, on the other side is Asia.
51107.m: The Bosphorus separates Europe and Asia.

51108.q: How many large bridges cross the Bosphorus (as of 2026)?
51108.e: Three large bridges cross the Bosphorus. They were opened in 1973, 1988 and 2016.

51109.q: How can a train in Istanbul cross the Bosphorus without using a bridge?
a: Through a tunnel under the water
51109.e: Since 2013 the Marmaray railway has run through a tunnel under the Bosphorus.
51109.m: A train runs through a tunnel under the Bosphorus.

51110.q: Roughly how long is the Bosphorus?
51110.e: The Bosphorus is about 30 kilometres long.
51110.m: The Bosphorus is about 30 kilometres long.

51111.q: Roughly how wide is the Bosphorus at its narrowest point?
51111.e: At its narrowest point the Bosphorus is only about 700 metres wide. You can easily see the other side.
51111.m: The Bosphorus is about 700 metres wide at its narrowest point.

51112.q: What is the capital of Albania?
51112.e: Tirana is the capital and the largest city of Albania.
51112.m: The capital of Albania is Tirana.

51113.q: Which animal is on the flag of Albania?
51113.e: The flag of Albania shows an eagle with two heads. That is why Albania is also called the land of eagles.
51113.m: There is a double-headed eagle on the flag of Albania.

51114.q: What colours is the flag of Albania?
51114.e: The background of the flag is red, and the eagle on it is black.
51114.m: The flag of Albania is red and black.

51115.q: What is the name of Albania’s national hero, after whom the big square in Tirana is named?
51115.e: Skanderbeg fought for Albania almost 600 years ago. The main square of Tirana is called Skanderbeg Square.
51115.m: Albania’s national hero is called Skanderbeg.

51116.q: Which small round concrete structures can be seen in many places in Albania?
51116.e: Many years ago the government had a great many bunkers built all over Albania. Many are still standing today.
51116.m: There are a great many old bunkers in Albania.

51117.q: Which two seas is Albania on?
51117.e: In the north Albania is on the Adriatic Sea, in the south on the Ionian Sea.
51117.m: Albania is on the Adriatic Sea and the Ionian Sea.

51118.q: The town of Berat in Albania is called the “town of a thousand windows”. Why?
a: Many old houses with lots of windows stand one above another on the hillside
Windows are made in the town
A palace in the town has exactly a thousand windows
The houses in the town are made entirely of glass
51118.e: In Berat, many old white houses stand one above another on the hillside. Their many windows gave the town its nickname.
51118.m: Berat is the town of a thousand windows.

51119.q: Tirana airport is named after which famous nun with Albanian roots?
51119.e: Mother Teresa had Albanian parents and helped poor people in India. Tirana airport bears her name.
51119.m: Tirana airport is named after Mother Teresa.

51120.q: Belgrade is the capital of which country?
51120.e: Belgrade is the capital and the largest city of Serbia.
51120.m: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia.

51121.q: Which two rivers meet in Belgrade?
51121.e: In Belgrade the Sava flows into the Danube. The old town lies exactly at this spot.
51121.m: In Belgrade the Sava flows into the Danube.

51122.q: What is the big old fortress in Belgrade above the rivers called?
51122.e: Kalemegdan Fortress lies high above the place where the two rivers meet. Today there is a large park there.

51123.q: What does the name Belgrade mean?
51123.e: In Serbian the city is called Beograd. “Beo” means white and “grad” means city.

51124.q: What is the huge church with the big dome in Belgrade called?
51124.e: The Temple of Saint Sava is one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world. It is dedicated to Saint Sava.
51124.m: The huge Temple of Saint Sava is in Belgrade.

51125.q: Which alphabet is used in Serbia alongside the Latin alphabet?
51125.e: In Serbia people often write with Cyrillic letters. This alphabet is also used in Russia, for example.
51125.m: In Serbia people also write with Cyrillic letters.

51126.q: Belgrade airport is named after which famous inventor?
51126.e: Nikola Tesla was an inventor with Serbian parents. There is also a Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade.
51126.m: Belgrade airport is named after Nikola Tesla.

51127.q: What is the money in Serbia called?
51127.e: In Serbia, and so also in Belgrade, people pay with the Serbian dinar.
51127.m: In Belgrade people pay with the dinar.

51128.q: What does the name Montenegro mean?
51128.e: Montenegro is an Italian name and means “black mountain”. In Montenegrin the country is called Crna Gora.

51129.q: What is the capital of Montenegro?
51129.e: Podgorica is the capital and the largest city of Montenegro.
51129.m: The capital of Montenegro is Podgorica.

51130.q: What is the famous bay in Montenegro surrounded by high mountains called?
51130.e: The Bay of Kotor reaches far inland. Steep mountains rise straight out of the water.
51130.m: The Bay of Kotor is in Montenegro.

51131.q: Which money do people use in Montenegro?
51131.e: Montenegro uses the euro, even though it is not a member of the European Union.
51131.m: In Montenegro people pay with the euro.

51132.e: Montenegro has a coast on the Adriatic Sea with many beaches and old little towns.
51132.m: Montenegro is on the Adriatic Sea.

51133.e: Montenegro lies on the Balkan Peninsula on the Adriatic Sea, part of the Mediterranean. The Bay of Kotor is especially well known.
51133.m: Montenegro is on the Adriatic Sea.

51135.q: Since which year has Montenegro been an independent country?
51135.e: In 2006 the people of Montenegro voted for independence. Before that the country was joined with Serbia.
51135.m: Montenegro has been an independent country since 2006.

51136.q: Which sea does the Danube flow into?
51136.e: The Danube flows from west to east right across Europe. In Romania and Ukraine it flows into the Black Sea.
51136.m: The Danube flows into the Black Sea.

51137.q: Which capital city is on the Danube?
51137.e: Vienna, the capital of Austria, is on the Danube. Bratislava and Belgrade are also on this river.

51138.q: Which capital city is divided into two parts by the Danube?
51138.e: The Danube flows right through Budapest. On one side is Buda, on the other Pest.
51138.m: The Danube separates Buda and Pest.

51139.q: Roughly how long is the Danube?
51139.e: The Danube is about 2850 kilometres long. This makes it one of the longest rivers in Europe.
51139.m: The Danube is almost 3000 kilometres long.

51140.q: Which river from the Engadine flows into the Danube?
51140.e: The Inn rises in the Engadine in the Grisons. At Passau in Germany it flows into the Danube.
51140.m: The Inn carries water from the Engadine into the Danube.

51141.q: Which composer wrote the waltz “The Blue Danube”?
51141.e: The waltz “The Blue Danube” was written by Johann Strauss (the son) in 1867. It is very popular in Austria.
51141.m: Johann Strauss wrote a famous Danube waltz.

51142.q: In which country is most of the Danube Delta?
51142.e: At its end the Danube splits into many branches and forms a delta. Most of it is in Romania, a small part in Ukraine.
51142.m: The Danube Delta is mostly in Romania.

51143.q: Which large lake does the Rhine flow through?
51143.e: The Rhine flows into Lake Constance and out again at Stein am Rhein. Lake Constance borders Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
51143.m: The Rhine flows through Lake Constance.

51144.q: What is the big waterfall of the Rhine near Schaffhausen called?
51144.e: At Neuhausen am Rheinfall, the Rhine plunges over rocks. It is one of the largest waterfalls in Europe.
51144.m: The Rhine Falls are near Schaffhausen.

51145.q: Where does the Rhine end in the end?
51145.e: The Rhine flows through Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands. Near Rotterdam it flows into the North Sea.
51145.m: The Rhine flows all the way to the sea.

51146.q: Which Swiss city has Rhine ports for large ships?
51146.e: Basel has the Swiss Rhine Ports. From there ships can sail along the Rhine all the way to the sea.
51146.m: Basel is the Swiss port on the Rhine.

51147.q: Which famous cathedral stands on the Rhine?
51147.e: Cologne Cathedral stands in Cologne, right on the Rhine. It is one of the largest churches in the world.
51147.m: Cologne Cathedral stands on the Rhine.

51148.q: Between Lake Constance and Basel, the Rhine mostly forms the border between Switzerland and which country?
51148.e: On this stretch the river is called the High Rhine. On most sections, Switzerland is on one side and Germany on the other.
51148.m: The High Rhine is the border with Germany.

51149.q: Roughly how long is the Rhine?
51149.e: The Rhine is about 1230 kilometres long. It is one of the most important rivers for shipping in Europe.
51149.m: The Rhine is over 1200 kilometres long.

51150.q: In which country does the Elbe rise?
51150.e: The Elbe begins in the Giant Mountains in Czechia. There it is called the “Labe”.

51151.q: Which large port city is on the Elbe?
51151.e: Hamburg is on the Elbe and has the largest port in Germany. Big ships sail up the Elbe into the city.

51152.q: Which sea does the Elbe flow into?
51152.e: The Elbe flows north-west through Czechia and Germany. Then it flows into the North Sea.
51152.m: The Elbe flows into the North Sea.

51153.q: Which city with the famous Frauenkirche (Church of Our Lady) is on the Elbe?
51153.e: Dresden is on the Elbe. The Frauenkirche was destroyed in the war and later rebuilt.

51154.q: Which river flows through Prague and into the Elbe?
51154.e: The Vltava flows right through Prague. A little further north it flows into the Elbe.
51154.m: The Vltava is a tributary of the Elbe.

51155.q: Roughly how long is the Elbe?
51155.e: The Elbe is about 1100 kilometres long. Most of it flows through Germany.
51155.m: The Elbe is about 1100 kilometres long.

51156.q: Between Czechia and Dresden, the Elbe flows past many tall rock towers. What kind of rock are they made of?
51156.e: The rock towers along the Elbe are made of sandstone. That is why the area is called the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.
51156.m: The Elbe flows through the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.

51157.q: Which two countries does the Elbe flow through?
51157.e: The Elbe rises in Czechia and then flows through Germany to the North Sea.
51157.m: The Elbe flows through Czechia and Germany.

51158.q: Which capital city is on the Seine?
51158.e: The Seine flows right through Paris, the capital of France. Many bridges cross the river.

51159.q: Which sea does the Seine flow into?
51159.e: The Seine flows into the English Channel at Le Havre. The English Channel lies between France and England.
51159.m: The Seine flows into the English Channel.

51160.q: Which famous tower stands close to the Seine?
51160.e: The Eiffel Tower stands in Paris very close to the bank of the Seine. It was built in 1889 for a world fair.
51160.m: The Eiffel Tower stands by the Seine.

51161.q: What is the famous large church on an island in the Seine in Paris called?
51161.e: Notre-Dame stands on an island in the middle of the Seine. The city of Paris began on this island.
51161.m: Notre-Dame stands on an island in the Seine.

51162.q: Where did the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paris Olympic Games take place?
51162.e: In July 2024 the athletes travelled along the Seine on boats. It was the first time the opening of the Summer Olympics did not take place in a stadium.
51162.m: The 2024 Olympic opening ceremony took place on the Seine.

51163.q: What do the bouquinistes on the banks of the Seine sell?
51163.e: The bouquinistes have green boxes on the walls along the Seine in Paris. In them they sell old books and pictures.

51164.q: Roughly how long is the Seine?
51164.e: The Seine is about 780 kilometres long. It flows entirely through France.
51164.m: The Seine is about 780 kilometres long.

51165.q: Which city in Normandy is on the Seine?
51165.e: Rouen is on the Seine between Paris and the sea. The painter Claude Monet often painted Rouen Cathedral.

51166.q: What is the oldest bridge over the Seine in Paris called?
51166.e: The name Pont Neuf means “New Bridge”. Even so, it is the oldest bridge still standing in Paris and was finished in 1607.
51166.m: The Pont Neuf is the oldest bridge in Paris.

51167.q: Which is the longest river in France?
51167.e: The Loire is about 1000 kilometres long. No other river in France is as long.
51167.m: The Loire is the longest river in France.

51168.q: What can be seen especially often in the Loire Valley in France?
51168.e: In the Loire Valley, kings and nobles built many magnificent castles. That is why a great many visitors come every year.
51168.m: The Loire Valley is famous for its castles.

51169.q: Which large castle with a double spiral staircase is in the Loire Valley?
51169.e: King Francis I had the Château de Chambord built. On its double spiral staircase, two people can walk without meeting each other.
51169.m: Chambord has a double spiral staircase.

51170.q: Which castle in the Loire Valley stands like a bridge over the River Cher?
51170.e: The Château de Chenonceau is built on arches over the Cher. The Cher is a tributary of the Loire.
51170.m: Chenonceau stands over the River Cher.

51171.q: Where does the Loire flow in the end?
51171.e: The Loire flows into the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire. Shortly before that, it flows through the city of Nantes.
51171.m: The Loire flows into the Atlantic.

51172.q: Which famous artist spent his last years in Amboise on the Loire?
51172.e: Leonardo da Vinci lived his last years in Amboise. He died there in 1519.
51172.m: Leonardo da Vinci died in Amboise on the Loire.

51173.q: Which city on the Loire did Joan of Arc free in 1429?
51173.e: In 1429 Joan of Arc helped to free the city of Orléans. That is why she is also called “the Maid of Orléans”.

51174.q: Since 2000, the Loire Valley has been on which famous list?
51174.e: UNESCO declared the Loire Valley a World Heritage Site in 2000. The landscape, the towns and the castles are protected.
51174.m: The Loire Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

51175.q: Which is the longest river in Poland?
51175.e: The Vistula is about 1000 kilometres long. It flows from the south to the north of Poland.
51175.m: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland.

51176.q: Which capital city is on the Vistula?
51176.e: The Vistula flows right through Warsaw, the capital of Poland.

51177.q: Which sea does the Vistula flow into?
51177.e: The Vistula flows north. Near Gdańsk it flows into the Baltic Sea.
51177.m: The Vistula flows into the Baltic Sea.

51178.q: Which old Polish royal city in the south is on the Vistula?
51178.e: For a long time Kraków was the capital of the Polish kings. The old town lies right on the Vistula.

51179.q: What is the Vistula called in Polish?
51179.e: In Polish the Vistula is called “Wisła”. It is pronounced roughly “VEES-wa”.
51179.m: The Vistula is called Wisła in Polish.

51180.q: Which port city lies close to the mouth of the Vistula?
51180.e: Gdańsk is in the north of Poland by the sea. A branch of the Vistula flows through the city.
51180.m: Gdańsk lies near the mouth of the Vistula.

51181.q: According to a Polish legend, which mythical creature lived in a cave by the Vistula below Wawel Castle?
51181.e: The legend tells of the Wawel Dragon, who lived in a cave by the river. Today there is a dragon statue there that breathes fire.
51181.m: According to legend, a dragon lived below Wawel Castle.

51182.q: Roughly how long is the Vistula?
51182.e: The Vistula is about 1000 kilometres long. It rises in the Beskids in the south of Poland.
51182.m: The Vistula is about 1000 kilometres long.

51183.q: In which country does the Ebro flow?
51183.e: The Ebro flows in north-eastern Spain. It is one of the longest rivers in the country.

51184.q: Which sea does the Ebro flow into?
51184.e: The Ebro flows south-east. In the province of Tarragona, between Barcelona and Valencia, it flows into the Mediterranean.
51184.m: The Ebro flows into the Mediterranean.

51185.q: Which large city is on the Ebro?
51185.e: Zaragoza is one of the largest cities in Spain. The Ebro flows right through the city.

51186.q: What does the Ebro form at its mouth?
51186.e: The Ebro carries a lot of sand and mud. Over time this has formed a large delta at its mouth.
51186.m: The Ebro forms a delta at its mouth.

51187.q: Which peninsula is named after the Ebro?
51187.e: The Romans called the Ebro “Iberus”. The name of the Iberian Peninsula, with Spain and Portugal, comes from this.
51187.m: The Iberian Peninsula is named after the Ebro.

51188.q: What is grown a lot in the Ebro Delta?
51188.e: In the flat, wet Ebro Delta there are many rice fields. Rice needs a lot of water.
51188.m: A lot of rice grows in the Ebro Delta.

51189.q: Roughly how long is the Ebro?
51189.e: The Ebro is about 900 kilometres long. It flows from the north of Spain to the sea.
51189.m: The Ebro is about 900 kilometres long.

51191.q: Which old tower in Portugal stands on the bank of the Tagus?
51191.e: Belém Tower was built on the bank of the Tagus about 500 years ago. It was meant to protect the entrance to the harbour.
51191.m: Belém Tower stands on the Tagus.

51192.q: Which capital city lies at the mouth of the Tagus?
51192.e: Lisbon, the capital of Portugal, lies where the Tagus flows into the sea. The river is very wide there.
51192.m: Lisbon lies at the mouth of the Tagus.

51194.q: Which ocean does the Tagus flow into?
51194.e: The Tagus flows west. In the end it flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
51194.m: The Tagus flows into the Atlantic.

51195.q: Which old city in Spain is almost completely surrounded by the Tagus?
51195.e: Toledo lies on a hill. The Tagus flows in a big loop almost all the way round the old town.
51195.m: The Tagus flows almost all the way round Toledo.

51196.q: What is the very long bridge over the Tagus, named after a seafarer, called?
51196.e: The Vasco da Gama Bridge is over 17 kilometres long. It was opened in 1998.
51196.m: The Vasco da Gama Bridge crosses the Tagus.

51197.q: In which country does the Tagus rise?
51197.e: The Tagus begins in the mountains of eastern Spain. Only later does it flow into Portugal.

51198.q: Which famous bridge in San Francisco does the red “25 de Abril” bridge over the Tagus look like?
51198.e: The “25 de Abril” bridge is red and hangs from large cables. That is why it looks very like the Golden Gate Bridge.
51198.m: The red Tagus bridge looks like the Golden Gate Bridge.

51199.q: Which capital city is on the Dnieper?
51199.e: Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine, lies on both banks of the Dnieper. Many bridges connect the two parts of the city.

51200.q: Which sea does the Dnieper flow into?
51200.e: The Dnieper flows from north to south. In the end it flows into the Black Sea.
51200.m: The Dnieper flows into the Black Sea.

51201.q: In which country does the Dnieper rise?
51201.e: The Dnieper begins in hilly country west of Moscow. After that it flows through two more countries.

51202.q: Which country north of Ukraine does the Dnieper also flow through?
51202.e: On its way, the Dnieper also flows through Belarus. Belarus used to be called Byelorussia or White Russia.
51202.m: The Dnieper also flows through Belarus.

51203.q: Which capital city does the Dnieper flow through?
51203.e: The Dnieper flows right through Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine.

51204.q: Roughly how long is the Dnieper?
51204.e: The Dnieper is about 2200 kilometres long. It is one of the longest rivers in Europe.
51204.m: The Dnieper is over 2000 kilometres long.

51205.q: The Dnieper is the longest river of which country?
51205.e: More than 1000 kilometres of the Dnieper are in Ukraine. No other river there is as long.
51205.m: The Dnieper is the longest river in Ukraine.

51206.q: What was built in many places along the Dnieper to produce electricity?
51206.e: Several large dams with hydroelectric power stations were built on the Dnieper. Huge reservoirs formed behind them.
51206.m: There are many dams on the Dnieper.

51207.q: Between which two countries does the Oder form part of the border?
51207.e: A long stretch of the Oder separates Germany and Poland. Together with the Neisse it forms the border.
51207.m: The Oder is a border river between Germany and Poland.

51208.q: Which sea does the Oder flow into?
51208.e: The Oder flows north. Through the Szczecin Lagoon it reaches the Baltic Sea.
51208.m: The Oder flows into the Baltic Sea.

51209.q: In which country does the Oder rise?
51209.e: The Oder begins in the Oder Mountains in Czechia. After that it flows through Poland.

51210.q: Which large Polish city is on the Oder?
51210.e: Wrocław, called Breslau in German, is on the Oder. The city has many islands and bridges.

51211.q: Which German town on the Oder has the same name as a city on the Main?
51211.e: There is Frankfurt am Main and Frankfurt an der Oder. Frankfurt (Oder) lies right on the border with Poland.
51211.m: Frankfurt an der Oder lies on the Polish border.

51212.q: Which port city lies near the mouth of the Oder?
51212.e: Szczecin is in north-western Poland on the Oder. Ships sail from its port out to sea.
51212.m: Szczecin lies near the mouth of the Oder.

51213.q: What is the Oder called in Polish?
51213.e: In Polish the Oder is called “Odra”. It has the same name in Czech.
51213.m: The Oder is called Odra in Polish.

51214.q: Roughly how long is the Oder?
51214.e: The Oder is about 860 kilometres long. Most of it is in Poland.
51214.m: The Oder is about 860 kilometres long.

51215.q: Which city in Italy is on the River Tiber?
51215.e: The Tiber flows right through Rome, the capital of Italy. The city grew up on hills by the river.

51216.q: According to a Roman legend, which twins were left as babies by the Tiber?
51216.e: According to the legend, the twins floated on the river in a basket. A she-wolf found them and fed them with her milk. Romulus is said to have founded Rome later.
51216.m: Romulus and Remus were found by the Tiber.

51217.q: What is the Tiber called in Italian?
51217.e: Italians call the river “Tevere”. The name Tiber comes from Latin.
51217.m: The Tiber is called Tevere in Italian.

51218.q: Which sea does the Tiber flow into?
51218.e: The Tiber flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea west of Rome. This is part of the Mediterranean.
51218.m: The Tiber flows into the Mediterranean.

51219.q: Which ancient Roman port lay at the mouth of the Tiber?
51219.e: Ostia was the port of ancient Rome. The name comes from the Latin word for river mouth.
51219.m: Ostia was the port at the mouth of the Tiber.

51220.q: Which round castle on the Tiber was once the tomb of a Roman emperor?
51220.e: Castel Sant’Angelo was built as a tomb for Emperor Hadrian. Later it became a fortress.
51220.m: Castel Sant’Angelo stands on the Tiber.

51221.q: What shape is the small Tiber Island in Rome?
51221.e: Tiber Island is small and long and has the shape of a ship. Two old bridges connect it to the banks.
51221.m: Tiber Island looks like a ship.

51222.q: Roughly how long is the Tiber?
51222.e: The Tiber is about 400 kilometres long. It rises in the Apennine mountains.
51222.m: The Tiber is about 400 kilometres long.

51223.q: Which river is the Volga connected to by a canal?
51223.e: The Volga-Don Canal was opened in 1952. This lets ships travel from the Volga to the Black Sea.
51223.m: A canal connects the Volga with the Don.

51224.q: Which country does the Volga flow through?
51224.e: From its source to its mouth, the Volga flows only through Russia. It is the country’s most important river.

51225.q: Which body of water does the Volga flow into?
51225.e: The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea. The Caspian Sea is actually the largest lake on Earth.
51225.m: The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.

51226.q: Roughly how long is the Volga?
51226.e: The Volga is about 3500 kilometres long. No other river in Europe is as long.
51226.m: At about 3500 kilometres, the Volga is the longest river in Europe.

51227.q: What does the name of the Russian city Volgograd mean?
51227.e: The Russian word “grad” means city. Volgograd stretches for many kilometres along the bank of the Volga.
51227.m: Volgograd is named after the Volga.

51228.q: Which city with a white Kremlin is on the Volga?
51228.e: Kazan is on the Volga. Its Kremlin with white walls is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

51229.q: What do many people in Russia lovingly call the Volga?
51229.e: In songs and poems the Volga is often called “Mother Volga”. This shows how important the river is to the people.
51229.m: The Volga is lovingly called Mother Volga.

51230.q: What does the Volga look like at its source?
51230.e: The Volga rises in hilly country north-west of Moscow. There it starts out as just a small stream.
51230.m: The Volga begins as a small stream.

51231.q: Which sea does the Volga flow into?
51231.e: Near the city of Astrakhan, the Volga splits into many branches and forms a huge delta on the Caspian Sea.
51231.m: The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.

51232.q: Which big mountain range covers a large part of Switzerland?
51232.e: The Alps cover about 60 per cent of the area of Switzerland. They stretch in a large arc through central Europe.
51232.m: The Alps are the largest mountain range in Switzerland.

51233.q: How many countries have a share of the Alps?
51233.e: The Alps lie in France, Monaco, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Germany, Austria and Slovenia. That makes eight countries.

51234.q: Which country is largely covered by the Alps?
51234.e: Almost two thirds of Austria lies in the Alps. Denmark, Belgium and Poland have no Alps.
51234.m: Austria is a real Alpine country.

51235.q: Which well-known Alpine mountain in Valais looks like a pointed pyramid?
51235.e: The Matterhorn stands near Zermatt on the border with Italy. Its pointed shape is known all over the world.
51235.m: The Matterhorn has the shape of a pyramid.

51236.q: What shape do the Alps have on the map?
51236.e: The Alps stretch in an arc from France to Austria and Slovenia. The arc is about 1200 kilometres long.
51236.m: The Alps form a large arc.

51237.q: Which animal with large, curved horns climbs in the Alps?
51237.e: The Alpine ibex lives high up among the rocks. The males have long, curved horns.
51237.m: The ibex is a skilful climber in the Alps.

51238.q: Which animal whistles in the Alps when there is danger?
51238.e: Marmots warn their family with a loud whistle. Then they all quickly disappear into their burrow.
51238.m: The marmot gives a warning whistle.

51239.q: What does the name “Mont Blanc” mean in English?
51239.e: “Mont” is the French word for mountain and “blanc” means white. Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps.

51240.q: Roughly how high is Mont Blanc?
51240.e: Mont Blanc is a little over 4800 metres high. Its exact height changes slightly from year to year.
51240.m: Mont Blanc is about 4800 metres high.

51241.q: Between which two countries is the summit of Mont Blanc?
51241.e: Mont Blanc lies in the border area between France and Italy. The two countries disagree about exactly where the border runs at the summit.
51241.m: Mont Blanc stands on the border between France and Italy.

51242.q: Which French town lies right below Mont Blanc?
51242.e: Chamonix lies in the valley at the foot of Mont Blanc. Many climbers set off from there.
51242.m: Chamonix lies at the foot of Mont Blanc.

51243.e: The Mont Blanc Tunnel is a road tunnel. It connects France with Italy and is about 11.6 kilometres long.
51243.m: The Mont Blanc Tunnel connects France and Italy.

51244.q: In which century was Mont Blanc climbed for the first time?
51244.e: Jacques Balmat and Michel-Gabriel Paccard reached the summit in 1786. That is in the 18th century.
51244.m: Mont Blanc was first climbed in 1786.

51245.q: Which Italian town lies at the foot of Mont Blanc?
51245.e: Courmayeur lies in the Aosta Valley on the Italian side. The Mont Blanc Tunnel ends very close by.
51245.m: Courmayeur is on the Italian side of Mont Blanc.

51246.q: What covers the summit of Mont Blanc all year round?
51246.e: Right at the top of Mont Blanc it is always very cold. That is why the snow on the summit never melts away completely.
51246.m: There is always snow on Mont Blanc.

51247.q: Which Swiss canton does the Mont Blanc massif border?
51247.e: The north-eastern part of the Mont Blanc massif lies in the canton of Valais. The Trient Glacier is there, for example.
51247.m: Part of the Mont Blanc massif borders Valais.

51248.q: Which two big countries do the Pyrenees separate?
51248.e: The Pyrenees form a natural border. To the north is France, to the south is Spain.
51248.m: The Pyrenees lie between France and Spain.

51249.q: Which small country lies in the middle of the Pyrenees?
51249.e: Andorra lies high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain. The whole country is mountainous.
51249.m: Andorra is a small country in the Pyrenees.

51250.q: Between which two seas do the Pyrenees lie?
51250.e: The Pyrenees stretch from the Atlantic in the west to the Mediterranean in the east. They are about 430 kilometres long.
51250.m: The Pyrenees stretch from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean.

51251.q: What is the highest mountain in the Pyrenees called?
51251.e: Aneto is in Spain and is about 3404 metres high. It is the highest peak in the Pyrenees.
51251.m: Aneto is the highest mountain in the Pyrenees.

51252.q: Are the Pyrenees higher or lower than the Alps?
51252.e: The highest mountain in the Pyrenees is about 3404 metres high. In the Alps there are many mountains over 4000 metres.
51252.m: The Pyrenees are lower than the Alps.

51253.q: Which large animal lives in the mountains of the Pyrenees again today?
51253.e: There were almost no bears left in the Pyrenees. So brown bears were brought there from Slovenia.
51253.m: Brown bears live in the Pyrenees again.

51254.q: The Pyrenees form the northern edge of which peninsula?
51254.e: The Pyrenees separate the Iberian Peninsula from the rest of Europe. Spain and Portugal lie on the peninsula.
51254.m: The Pyrenees close off the Iberian Peninsula in the north.

51255.q: Which people with their own language live at the western end of the Pyrenees?
51255.e: The Basques live in Spain and France by the Atlantic. Their language, Basque, is not related to any other language.
51255.m: The Basques live at the western end of the Pyrenees.

51256.q: Which animal climbs over steep rocks in the Pyrenees and also here in the Alps?
51256.e: Chamois live in the Pyrenees, just as in the Alps. They are very good climbers. The Pyrenees lie between Spain and France.

51257.q: What shape do the Carpathians have on the map?
51257.e: The Carpathians stretch in a large arc through eastern Europe. They are about 1300 kilometres long.
51257.m: The Carpathians form a large arc.

51258.q: In which country is the largest part of the Carpathians?
51258.e: About half of the Carpathians lie in Romania. One part is called the Southern Carpathians or Transylvanian Alps.
51258.m: Most of the Carpathians are in Romania.

51259.q: In which part of Europe are the Carpathians?
51259.e: The Carpathians lie in countries such as Romania, Slovakia, Poland and Ukraine. That is east-central and eastern Europe.
51259.m: The Carpathians are a mountain range in eastern Europe.

51260.q: What is the highest part of the Carpathians called?
51260.e: The High Tatras are in Slovakia and Poland. The highest Carpathian mountain, Gerlach Peak, is here.
51260.m: The High Tatras are the highest part of the Carpathians.

51261.q: Which animal lives in especially large numbers in the Carpathians?
51261.e: A great many brown bears live in the Carpathians, especially in Romania. Wolves and lynxes are also found there.
51261.m: Many brown bears live in the Carpathians.

51262.q: Which well-known spooky story is linked to a castle in the Carpathians?
51262.e: Bran Castle in Romania is often called “Dracula’s Castle”. The story of Dracula is set in Transylvania.
51262.m: Dracula’s story is set in the Carpathians.

51263.q: Which big river flows through a gorge in the Carpathians?
51263.e: The Danube breaks through the Carpathians on the border between Serbia and Romania. The narrow stretch is called the Iron Gates.
51263.m: The Danube flows through the Iron Gates in the Carpathians.

51264.q: Roughly how high is the highest mountain in the Carpathians?
51264.e: Gerlach Peak in Slovakia is about 2655 metres high. This makes the Carpathians clearly lower than the Alps.
51264.m: Gerlach Peak is about 2650 metres high.

51265.q: Which of these countries has a share of the Carpathians?
51265.e: Slovakia is a very mountainous country. A large part of it belongs to the Carpathians.
51265.m: Slovakia also has a share of the Carpathians.

51266.q: In which country are the Apennines?
51266.e: The Apennines run through almost the whole of Italy. They begin in the north-west and reach the south of the country.
51266.m: The Apennines are Italy’s mountain range.

51267.q: How do the Apennines run through Italy?
51267.e: The Apennines run like a long back through the Italian boot. That is why they are called the backbone of Italy.
51267.m: The Apennines are the backbone of Italy.

51268.q: Because of its shape, what is the Apennine Peninsula also called?
51268.e: Italy lies on the Apennine Peninsula. On the map it looks like a boot.
51268.m: Italy has the shape of a boot.

51269.q: Which volcano stands in Italy near the city of Naples, close to the Apennines?
51269.e: Vesuvius stands near Naples. Etna is on Sicily, Stromboli on a small island, and Monte Rosa is an Alpine mountain.

51270.q: On which large island do the Apennines continue?
51270.e: The Apennines are about 1500 kilometres long. In the south they continue in the mountains of northern Sicily.

51271.q: Which small country lies on a mountain at the edge of the Apennines?
51271.e: San Marino lies on Monte Titano in northern Italy. The country is completely surrounded by Italy.
51271.m: San Marino lies on a mountain in the Apennines.

51272.q: Which predator survived in the forests of the Apennines?
51272.e: There were always wolves in the Apennines, even when they had almost disappeared elsewhere. From there, wolves have returned as far as the Alps.

51273.q: Which mountain range is higher: the Apennines or the Alps?
51273.e: The highest mountain in the Apennines is about 2912 metres high. In the Alps there are mountains over 4000 metres.
51273.m: The Alps are higher than the Apennines.

51274.q: Which river of Florence rises in the Apennines?
51274.e: The Arno rises in the Apennines in Tuscany. It flows through Florence and Pisa.
51274.m: The Arno flows from the Apennines through Florence.

51275.q: Which two countries do the Scandinavian Mountains mainly run through?
51275.e: The Scandinavian Mountains lie on the Scandinavian Peninsula. A large part belongs to Norway, the eastern edge to Sweden.
51275.m: The Scandinavian Mountains are in Norway and Sweden.

51276.q: Which large animal with antlers like shovels lives in the forests of Scandinavia?
51276.e: The elk, also called the moose, is the largest deer in the world. Its broad antlers look like shovels.

51277.q: What are the long arms of the sea along the coast of Norway?
51277.e: Fjords are long, narrow arms of the sea between steep mountains. They often reach far inland.
51277.m: There are many fjords on Norway’s coast.

51278.q: What shaped the fjords in Norway?
51278.e: In the Ice Age, huge glaciers flowed through the valleys. They scraped the valleys out deeply.

51279.q: Which animal with antlers do the Sami keep in the north of Scandinavia?
51279.e: The Sami keep herds of reindeer in the north of Scandinavia. Reindeer are well adapted to cold and snow.

51280.q: What can you see in the night sky in winter in the far north of Scandinavia?
51280.e: The northern lights glow green and sometimes red in the dark sky. The midnight sun only happens in summer.
51280.m: In winter the northern lights glow in the north.

51281.q: What can you experience in summer in the far north of Scandinavia?
51281.e: North of the Arctic Circle, the sun does not set at all for several weeks in summer. This is called the midnight sun.
51281.m: In northern Scandinavia the midnight sun shines in summer.

51282.q: What is the Jostedalsbreen in Norway?
51282.e: The Jostedalsbreen lies in the Scandinavian Mountains. It is the largest glacier on the European mainland.
51282.m: The Jostedalsbreen is the largest mainland glacier in Europe.

a: A rock plateau above a fjord
51283.e: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) is a flat rock ledge. It lies about 600 metres above the Lysefjord.
51283.m: Preikestolen is a rock ledge above the Lysefjord.
