51638.q: What is the place by Lake Ägeri where a famous battle took place in 1315 called?
51638.e: On 15 November 1315 the Confederates fought a Habsburg army at Morgarten. A monument by Lake Ägeri recalls it.
51638.m: A battle took place at Morgarten by Lake Ägeri in 1315.

51639.q: Which tower with a clock is a landmark of Zug’s old town?
51639.e: The Zytturm is an old clock tower in Zug’s old town. Its roof is blue and white like the Zug coat of arms.
51639.m: The Zytturm is a landmark of Zug.

51640.q: Pilatus is the local mountain of which city?
51640.e: Pilatus stands south-west of Lucerne. You can see it from the whole city.

51641.e: The highest summit of Pilatus is 2128 metres high. That is about 2100 metres.

51642.q: What is special about the Pilatus Railway?
a: It is the steepest cog railway in the world
It is the longest cable car in the world
It is the fastest train in the world
51642.e: At its steepest point, the Pilatus Railway has a gradient of 48 per cent. This makes it the steepest cog railway in the world.
51642.m: The Pilatus Railway is the steepest cog railway in the world.

51643.q: According to old legends, which mythical creature is said to live on Pilatus?
51643.e: In the past people told stories that dragons lived on Pilatus. That is why the dragon is a symbol of the mountain.
51643.m: According to legend, dragons lived on Pilatus.

51644.q: Where does the cog railway up Pilatus start?
51644.e: The Pilatus Railway goes up from Alpnachstad on Lake Alpnach. From there it climbs to Pilatus Kulm.
51644.m: The Pilatus Railway starts in Alpnachstad.

51645.q: In which year was the Pilatus Railway opened?
51645.e: The Pilatus Railway has been running since 1889. So it is more than 130 years old.
51645.m: The Pilatus Railway has run since 1889.

51646.q: Which large lake can you see far below from Pilatus?
51646.e: Pilatus stands right by Lake Lucerne. From the top you can see the lake and the city of Lucerne.
51646.m: From Pilatus you look down on Lake Lucerne.

51647.q: How do you get up Pilatus from Kriens?
51647.e: From Kriens, first a gondola and then an aerial cableway take you up Pilatus. The cog railway runs on the other side, from Alpnachstad.
51647.m: From Kriens you go up Pilatus by cable car.

51648.q: When does the cog railway up Pilatus not run?
51648.e: The Pilatus Railway runs only from about spring to autumn. In winter there is too much snow on the line.
51648.m: The Pilatus Railway does not run in winter.

51649.q: Which lovely nickname does the Rigi have?
51649.e: The Rigi is often called the “Queen of the Mountains”. People once believed its name came from the Latin word for queen.
51649.m: The Rigi is also called the “Queen of the Mountains”.

51650.q: Since which year has a cog railway run up the Rigi?
51650.e: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway has run since 1871. It was the first mountain railway in Europe.
51650.m: A railway has run up the Rigi since 1871.

51651.q: From which village on Lake Lucerne does the oldest Rigi railway go up?
51651.e: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway starts in Vitznau on the lakeshore. From there it runs up to Rigi Kulm.
51651.m: The oldest Rigi railway starts in Vitznau.

51652.q: What is the highest point of the Rigi called?
51652.e: Rigi Kulm is the summit of the Rigi. From there you have a wide view over lakes and mountains.
51652.m: Rigi Kulm is the highest point of the Rigi.

51653.q: About how high is Rigi Kulm?
51653.e: Rigi Kulm is just under 1800 metres high. From there you can see far across lakes and mountains.
51653.m: Rigi Kulm is about 1800 metres high.

51654.q: Which two cantons does the Rigi belong to?
51654.e: Part of the Rigi belongs to the canton of Lucerne, another part to the canton of Schwyz. The summit is in the canton of Schwyz.
51654.m: The Rigi belongs to Lucerne and Schwyz.

51655.q: Which three lakes lie around the Rigi?
a: Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz
Lake Geneva, Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Biel
Lake Thun, Lake Brienz and Lake Sarnen
Lake Zurich, Lake Walen and Lake Greifen
51655.e: The Rigi is almost completely surrounded by lakes. Lake Lucerne lies to the south, Lake Zug to the north and Lake Lauerz to the east.
51655.m: The Rigi is surrounded by three lakes.

51656.q: From which place does the second cog railway run up the Rigi?
51656.e: The Arth-Rigi Railway has run up the Rigi from Arth-Goldau since 1875. So you can go up by train from two sides.
51656.m: A railway also runs up the Rigi from Arth-Goldau.

51657.q: Where does Lake Lucerne’s German name “Vierwaldstättersee” come from?
a: From four old cantons on its shores
From four forests in the water
From four islands in the lake
51657.e: The four “Waldstätten” (forest cantons) were Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne. In the past the lake was called the Lake of Lucerne.
51657.m: Lake Lucerne’s German name comes from four old cantons.

51658.q: What is the part of Lake Lucerne that lies in the canton of Uri called?
51658.e: Lake Uri is the south-eastern arm of the lake. It reaches from Brunnen to the mouth of the Reuss near Flüelen and Seedorf.
51658.m: Lake Uri is part of Lake Lucerne.

51659.q: How many cantons border Lake Lucerne today?
51659.e: Today Uri, Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden and Lucerne border the lake. This is because Unterwalden is divided into two cantons.

51660.q: About how deep is Lake Lucerne at its deepest point?
51660.e: The deepest point is 214 metres deep. It lies between Beckenried and Gersau.
51660.m: Lake Lucerne is over 200 metres deep.

51661.q: What is the rock in the lake that honours the author of “William Tell” called?
51661.e: The Schiller Stone is a tall rock in Lake Uri. Its inscription honours Friedrich Schiller, who wrote the play “William Tell”.
51661.m: The Schiller Stone honours Friedrich Schiller.

51662.q: What shape does Lake Lucerne have when seen from above?
a: It is round like a circle
It is straight like a line
It is shaped like a heart
51662.e: The lake has many arms and bays. Near Lucerne, four arms almost form a cross.

51663.q: At which city does Lake Lucerne end in the west?
51663.e: The city of Lucerne lies at the western end of the lake. The water flows out of the lake there.
51663.m: Lucerne lies at the western end of Lake Lucerne.

51664.q: What were the new islands in Lake Uri built from?
51664.e: Small islands were piled up in Lake Uri near Flüelen. They were built from rock dug out during the construction of the Gotthard Base Tunnel.
51664.m: The islands in Lake Uri are made of tunnel rock.

51665.q: Which river from the Muota valley flows into the lake at Brunnen?
51665.e: The Muota flows through the Muota valley. At Brunnen it flows into Lake Lucerne.
51665.m: The Muota flows into Lake Lucerne at Brunnen.

51666.q: According to legend, what did men from the founding cantons do on the Rütli?
51666.e: According to legend, men from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore on the Rütli to help one another. This is called the Rütli Oath.
51666.m: The Rütli Oath is said to have taken place on the Rütli.

51667.q: What is the easiest way to get to the Rütli?
51667.e: It is best to go by boat, for example from Brunnen. You can also walk down from Seelisberg.
51667.m: The best way to the Rütli is by boat.

51668.q: On which day is there a big celebration on the Rütli every year?
51668.e: Every year on 1 August there is a celebration on the Rütli. 1 August is the Swiss National Day.
51668.m: On 1 August the National Day is celebrated on the Rütli.

51669.q: Which general gathered his officers on the Rütli meadow in 1940?
51669.e: On 25 July 1940, General Henri Guisan spoke to his officers on the Rütli. He explained to them how Switzerland was to be defended.
51669.m: General Guisan held the Rütli Report in 1940.

51670.q: Which legendary hero has a monument in Altdorf?
51670.e: The Tell Monument stands on the town hall square in Altdorf. It was put up in 1895.
51670.m: The monument to William Tell stands in Altdorf.

51671.q: Who stands next to Tell on the Tell Monument in Altdorf?
51671.e: The monument shows Tell together with his son Walter. The son is holding on to his father.
51671.m: The Tell Monument shows Tell with his son.

51672.q: According to the legend, what did Tell have to shoot off his son's head in Altdorf?
51672.e: The bailiff Gessler forced Tell to shoot an apple off his son's head. Tell hit the apple.
51672.m: Tell shot an apple off his son's head.

51673.q: According to the legend, which object on a pole were people in Altdorf supposed to greet?
51673.e: Gessler had his hat put on a pole in Altdorf. Everyone had to greet it, but Tell did not.
51673.m: Tell did not greet Gessler's hat.

51674.q: According to the legend, which weapon did Tell shoot with?
51674.e: Tell was a good shot with the crossbow. The monument in Altdorf also shows him with a crossbow.
51674.m: William Tell shot with a crossbow.

51675.q: Which play is performed in the Tell Theatre in Altdorf?
51675.e: Since 1899, amateur actors from Uri have performed Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell” in Altdorf. Today they perform in the Tell Theatre.
51675.m: The play “William Tell” is performed in Altdorf.

51676.q: What material is the Tell Monument in Altdorf made of?
51676.e: The Tell Monument is cast in bronze. It was created by the sculptor Richard Kissling.
51676.m: The Tell Monument in Altdorf is made of bronze.

51677.q: Which famous monument stands on the village square of Altdorf?
51677.e: The Tell Monument in Altdorf shows William Tell with his son Walter. It was put up in 1895.
51677.m: The Tell Monument stands in Altdorf.

51678.q: Which place with a boat harbour on Lake Uri lies right next to Altdorf?
51678.e: Flüelen borders Altdorf to the north and lies on Lake Uri. The boats of Lake Lucerne stop there.
51678.m: Flüelen is the harbour town next to Altdorf.

51679.q: Which river flows through Lake Zug?
51679.e: The Lorze flows into the lake west of the town of Zug. Shortly afterwards it flows out again.
51679.m: The Lorze flows through Lake Zug.

51680.q: Which fish is a well-known speciality from Lake Zug?
51680.e: The Zug Rötel is a special kind of char. It lives in Lake Zug and is a popular fish to eat.
51680.m: The Zug Rötel is a fish from Lake Zug.

51681.q: Which three cantons border Lake Zug?
51681.e: Most of Lake Zug belongs to the canton of Zug. The south belongs to Schwyz and a small part to Lucerne.
51681.m: Lake Zug borders Zug, Schwyz and Lucerne.

51682.q: Which well-known mountain rises on the southern shore of Lake Zug?
51682.e: At the southern end of Lake Zug, the Rigi rises steeply. You can see the mountain well from the lake.
51682.m: The Rigi stands on the southern shore of Lake Zug.

51683.q: About how long is Lake Zug?
51683.e: Lake Zug is about 13.7 kilometres long. That is about 14 kilometres.
51683.m: Lake Zug is about 14 kilometres long.

51684.q: Which place lies at the southern end of Lake Zug?
51684.e: Arth lies in the canton of Schwyz at the southern end of the lake. The town of Zug, on the other hand, lies on the north-eastern shore.
51684.m: Arth lies at the southern end of Lake Zug.

51685.q: Near which place does the Lorze flow out of Lake Zug?
51685.e: The Lorze leaves Lake Zug near Cham. After that it flows on towards the Reuss.
51685.m: The Lorze flows out of Lake Zug near Cham.

51686.q: About how many kinds of fish live in Lake Zug?
51686.e: 32 kinds of fish live in Lake Zug. Important fish for eating are whitefish, perch and pike.
51686.m: About 30 kinds of fish live in Lake Zug.

51687.q: What are the two councils that debate laws in the Federal Palace called?
a: National Council and Council of States
51687.e: The National Council and the Council of States together form Parliament. They meet in two different halls in the Federal Palace.
51687.m: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Federal Palace.

51688.q: Which bank has its head office right next to the Federal Palace on Federal Square?
51688.e: The Swiss National Bank has a large building on Federal Square. One of its jobs is looking after Switzerland's money.
51688.m: The National Bank stands on Federal Square next to the Federal Palace.

51689.q: How many water jets does the fountain on Federal Square have?
51689.e: On Federal Square, 26 jets of water shoot up out of the ground. Each jet stands for one canton.
51689.m: The 26 water jets on Federal Square stand for the 26 cantons.

51690.q: What takes place on Federal Square every Tuesday and Saturday?
51690.e: There is a market in front of the Federal Palace twice a week. You can buy vegetables, fruit and flowers there, for example.
51690.m: A market takes place in front of the Federal Palace twice a week.

51691.q: Which river flows past at the bottom of the slope behind the Federal Palace?
51691.e: The Federal Palace stands on a hill above the Aare. From the terrace you can look down at the river.
51691.m: The Aare flows past behind the Federal Palace.

51692.q: Which two chambers of Parliament meet in the Federal Palace?
a: National Council and Council of States
Federal Council and Federal Supreme Court
51692.e: The Swiss Parliament is called the Federal Assembly. It is made up of the National Council and the Council of States.
51692.m: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Federal Palace.

51693.q: Which figures stand as a large statue in the domed hall of the Federal Palace?
51693.e: The statue shows the three men of the Rütli Oath. It is a reminder of the founding of the Swiss Confederation.
51693.m: In the domed hall, the three Confederates are a reminder of the Rütli Oath.

51694.q: What can you see in the glass dome inside the Federal Palace?
a: The coats of arms of the cantons
A large map of the world
51694.e: In the glass dome above the domed hall are the colourful coats of arms of the cantons. In the middle is the Swiss coat of arms.
51694.m: The coats of arms of the cantons shine in the glass dome of the Federal Palace.

51695.q: Which kind of bear lives in the Bear Park in Bern?
51695.e: Brown bears live in the Bear Park. These bears used to live in the forests of Switzerland too.
51695.m: Brown bears live in the Bear Park in Bern.

51696.q: What do the brown bears in the Bear Park eat?
51696.e: Brown bears are omnivores. They eat fruit, vegetables, nuts, fish and meat.
51696.m: Brown bears eat plants and meat.

51697.q: Why has the city of Bern kept bears for centuries?
a: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern
Bears protect the city from thieves
Bears are bred and sold there
Bears mow the grass on the banks of the Aare
51697.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of the city and the canton of Bern. Today the bears live in the Bear Park by the Aare.
51697.m: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.

51698.q: Next to which bridge is the old Bear Pit in Bern?
51698.e: The Bear Pit lies at the end of the Old Town, just on the other side of the Nydegg Bridge.
51698.m: The old Bear Pit is near the Nydegg Bridge.

51699.q: Why was the Bear Park built in Bern?
a: To give the bears more space
51699.e: The bears had little space in the old round pit. In the Bear Park on the slope they can climb, dig and bathe.
51699.m: The bears have much more space in the Bear Park than in the old pit.

51700.q: What do the bears in the Bear Park usually do in winter?
51700.e: Brown bears sleep a lot in winter and hardly eat. This is called a winter rest.
51700.m: In winter, the bears have a winter rest.

51701.q: How long has Bern had bear pits?
51701.e: A first bear pit is known from as early as 1441. Since then it has been moved to a new place several times.
51701.m: Bern has kept bears for over 500 years.

51702.q: What does the old Bear Pit in Bern look like?
51702.e: The old Bear Pit is a deep, round pit with stone walls. Visitors look down into it from above.
51702.m: The old Bear Pit is a round pit with walls.

51703.q: Why has the city of Bern kept bears for so long?
a: The bear is its heraldic animal
51703.e: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern. That is why bears have lived in the city for a very long time.
51703.m: Bern keeps bears because the bear is its heraldic animal.

51704.q: Which figure on the Zytglogge rings two small bells?
51704.e: A jester with a jester's cap sits in a niche. Before the hour he rings two small bells above his head.
51704.m: A jester rings two small bells on the Zytglogge.

51705.q: What does the Bernese German word “Zytglogge” mean?
51705.e: In Bernese German, “Zyt” means time and “Glogge” means bell. The bell tells the time with its strokes.
51705.m: Zytglogge is Bernese German and means time bell.

51706.q: Which animal crows on the Zytglogge shortly before the hour?
51706.e: A wooden cockerel crows before every full hour. In this way it announces the show of figures.
51706.m: The cockerel on the Zytglogge crows before the hour.

51707.q: Which animals parade in a circle on the Zytglogge?
51707.e: Before the hour, a procession of little bear figures comes out of the tower. They carry weapons and musical instruments.
51707.m: A procession of bears goes past on the Zytglogge.

51708.q: Who strikes the hour with a hammer on the Zytglogge?
51708.e: Right at the top of the tower stands a gilded knight. He is called Hans von Thann and strikes the big bell with his hammer.
51708.m: A golden knight strikes the hours on the Zytglogge.

51709.q: About how old is the Zytglogge tower?
51709.e: The tower was built around 1218 to 1220. That makes it more than 800 years old.
51709.m: The Zytglogge is over 800 years old.

51710.q: What was the Zytglogge used for at the very beginning?
51710.e: At first the Zytglogge was a defensive tower on the western edge of the young city. It only got a clock later.
51710.m: The Zytglogge was first a tower to protect the city.

51711.q: How many minutes before the hour does the show of figures on the Zytglogge start?
51711.e: About four minutes before the hour, the figures start to move. That is why many tourists wait in front of the tower beforehand.
51711.m: The show of figures on the Zytglogge starts about four minutes before the hour.

51712.q: Which figure on the Zytglogge turns over an hourglass?
51712.e: Chronos is a bearded man and the god of time. He turns the hourglass and counts the strokes of the bell.
51712.m: Chronos, the god of time, turns over the hourglass on the Zytglogge.

51713.q: Which number is especially popular in the town of Solothurn?
51713.e: In Solothurn there are many things in elevens, for example churches, fountains and bells. That is why 11 is seen as the town's lucky number.
51713.m: The number 11 is Solothurn's favourite number.

51714.q: Which large church stands in the town of Solothurn?
51714.e: St Ursus Cathedral is the landmark of Solothurn. A wide staircase leads up to its entrance.
51714.m: St Ursus Cathedral is the large church of Solothurn.

51715.q: Which mountain lies to the north above the town of Solothurn?
51715.e: The Weissenstein is a mountain in the Jura. You can go up by gondola and look far out over the Swiss Plateau.
51715.m: The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.

51716.q: In which year did Solothurn join the Swiss Confederation?
51716.e: Solothurn was admitted to the Confederation in 1481 together with Fribourg. That made it the eleventh member.
51716.m: Solothurn has been part of the Confederation since 1481.

51717.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Solothurn?
51717.e: The coat of arms is red at the top and white at the bottom. It is very simple and has no animal.
51717.m: The Solothurn coat of arms is red and white.

51718.q: Which language do most people in the canton of Solothurn speak?
51718.e: The canton of Solothurn is in German-speaking Switzerland. In everyday life people speak Swiss German.
51718.m: German is spoken in the canton of Solothurn.

51719.q: Which town is also called the “Town of Ambassadors”?
51719.e: For a long time, the ambassadors of the King of France lived in Solothurn. That is how it got its nickname.
51719.m: Solothurn is called the Town of Ambassadors because French ambassadors used to live there.

51720.q: Since which year has Aargau been a canton of its own?
51720.e: The canton of Aargau was founded in 1803. Before that, its lands belonged to various rulers.
51720.m: Aargau has been a canton since 1803.

51721.q: Why is Aargau also called the “canton of castles”?
a: It lies high in the mountains
51721.e: There are many castles in Aargau, for example Lenzburg, Hallwyl and Wildegg.
51721.m: Aargau is the canton of castles.

51722.q: Which castle in Aargau gave its name to a famous ruling family?
51722.e: The Habsburg family comes from Habsburg Castle near Brugg. Later they became emperors in Austria.
51722.m: The Habsburgs got their name from Habsburg Castle in Aargau.

51723.q: What was the large Roman camp near Windisch in Aargau called?
51723.e: Around 2000 years ago, there was a large camp of Roman soldiers near Windisch. It was called Vindonissa.
51723.m: The Roman camp of Vindonissa was near Windisch in Aargau.

51724.q: Which canton borders Aargau to the east?
51724.e: The canton of Zurich lies to the east of Aargau. Solothurn and Basel-Landschaft border it to the west.
51724.m: The canton of Zurich is Aargau's eastern neighbour.

51725.q: Which vegetable is in Aargau's nickname “Rüebliland”?
51725.e: In the past, a particularly large number of carrots were grown in Aargau. In Switzerland, carrots are also called Rüebli.
51725.m: Aargau is also called Rüebliland because of its carrots.

51726.q: Which large river forms the border between Aargau and Germany in the north?
51726.e: The Rhine flows along the north of Aargau. Germany lies on the other side.
51726.m: The Rhine separates Aargau from Germany.

51727.q: Which lake lies mostly in the canton of Aargau?
51727.e: Lake Hallwil lies in the south of Aargau. A small part belongs to the canton of Lucerne.
51727.m: Lake Hallwil is the largest lake in Aargau.

51728.q: Aarau is the capital of which canton?
51728.e: The government and the parliament of the canton of Aargau are based in Aarau.
51728.m: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau.

51729.q: Aarau is also called the “town of beautiful ...”. How does the name go on?
51729.e: Many houses in Aarau's Old Town have brightly painted undersides to their roofs. That is why Aarau is called the town of beautiful gables.
51729.m: Aarau is the town of beautiful gables.

51730.q: Which famous physicist took his school-leaving exams in Aarau?
51730.e: Albert Einstein went to the cantonal school in Aarau. In 1896 he passed his school-leaving exams (Matura) there.
51730.m: Albert Einstein went to school in Aarau.

51731.q: In 1798, Aarau was briefly the capital of what?
51731.e: The Helvetic Republic was created in 1798. For a few months, Aarau was its first capital.
51731.m: Aarau was briefly the capital of Switzerland in 1798.

51732.q: What has been made in a foundry in Aarau for many hundreds of years?
51732.e: Aarau has a bell foundry with a tradition more than 600 years old. Its bells hang in many churches.
51732.m: Bells have been cast in Aarau for centuries.

51733.q: Roughly between which two large cities does Aarau lie?
51733.e: Aarau lies on the Swiss Plateau on the railway line between Zurich and Bern. By train you can get to both cities quickly.
51733.m: Aarau lies between Zurich and Bern.

51734.q: What is the old tower in Aarau that now houses the town museum called?
51734.e: The Schlössli is an old residential tower from the 13th century. It is thought to be the oldest building in Aarau.
51734.m: The town museum is in the Schlössli in Aarau.

51735.q: Which neighbouring canton begins just a few kilometres west of Aarau?
51735.e: Aarau lies close to the border of Aargau. The canton of Solothurn begins just to the west.
51735.m: The canton of Solothurn begins west of Aarau.

51736.q: Roughly how many people live in the town of Aarau (as of 2023)?
51736.e: Aarau is a smaller town. At the end of 2023, about 22,000 people lived there.

51737.q: Which baked treat is a well-known speciality from Basel?
51737.e: Basler Läckerli are small, hard gingerbread biscuits with honey and spices. People often buy them as a present.
51737.m: Läckerli are a typical baked treat from Basel.

51738.q: Which large river flows right through Basel?
51738.e: The Rhine divides Basel into Grossbasel and Kleinbasel. Several bridges cross the river.
51738.m: The Rhine flows right through Basel.

51739.q: Which city has the oldest university in Switzerland?
51739.e: The University of Basel was founded in 1460. It is the oldest university in Switzerland.
51739.m: Basel has the oldest university in Switzerland.

51740.q: Which mythical creature is a symbol of Basel?
51740.e: The basilisk is a mythical creature, half cockerel and half dragon. In Basel it stands on many fountains.
51740.m: The basilisk is a symbol of Basel.

51741.q: What colour is the town hall on the market square in Basel?
51741.e: Basel's town hall is painted bright red. It is one of the best-known buildings in the city.
51741.m: Basel's town hall is bright red.

51742.q: How do the ferries in Basel cross the Rhine without an engine?
51742.e: The ferries hang from a cable above the river. The current of the Rhine pushes them from one bank to the other.
51742.m: Basel's Rhine ferries are powered only by the current.

51743.q: In which year did Basel-Landschaft separate from Basel-Stadt?
51743.e: After a quarrel between the city and the countryside, the canton of Basel was divided in 1833.
51743.m: Basel-Landschaft has been separate from Basel-Stadt since 1833.

51744.q: What is the canton of Basel-Landschaft also called for short?
51744.e: People in the canton often say Baselbiet. There is even a song called the Baselbieterlied.

51745.q: Which old Roman town can you visit in Augst?
51745.e: A Roman town stood in Augst around 2000 years ago. You can still see a theatre and many walls.
51745.m: You can visit the Roman town of Augusta Raurica in Augst.

51746.q: What do people carry through the town during the Chienbäse parade in Liestal?
51746.e: At the Chienbäse during carnival, people carry burning bundles of wood. Carts carrying fires also pass through the town gate.
51746.m: Large bundles of wood burn at the Chienbäse in Liestal.

51747.q: Which fruit is the canton of Basel-Landschaft especially known for?
51747.e: There are a great many cherry trees in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. The cherries are called Chriesi there.
51747.m: Basel-Landschaft is known for its cherries.

51748.q: Which mountain range lies in the south of the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
51748.e: The south of Basel-Landschaft is hilly. These hills and mountains are part of the Jura.
51748.m: The Jura lies in the south of Basel-Landschaft.

51749.q: Which river flows through the Laufen valley towards Basel?
51749.e: The Birs comes from the Jura and flows through the Laufen valley. Near Basel it flows into the Rhine.
51749.m: The Birs flows through the Laufen valley to the Rhine.

51750.q: Up to which Swiss city can large cargo ships travel up the Rhine?
51750.e: Large cargo ships travel from the North Sea up the Rhine as far as Basel. Further upstream, rapids and the Rhine Falls stop them.
51750.m: Cargo ships travel up the Rhine as far as Basel.

51751.q: At which large port in the Netherlands do many Rhine ships from Basel arrive?
51751.e: Rotterdam lies at the mouth of the Rhine. It is one of the largest ports in the world.
51751.m: Many Rhine ships from Basel travel as far as Rotterdam.

51752.q: What are containers lifted off the ship with at the port?
51752.e: Large cranes grab the containers from above and lift them onto land. Then they go onto lorries or trains.
51752.m: At the port, large cranes lift the containers off the ship.

51753.q: What are the large steel boxes that goods travel in on ships called?
51753.e: Containers are standard-sized steel boxes. They fit on ships, lorries and trains.
51753.m: Many goods travel on the Rhine in containers.

51754.q: What is brought into Switzerland in especially large amounts through the Rhine ports?
51754.e: A large part of Switzerland's heating oil and fuel comes to Basel by ship. There it is stored in big tanks.
51754.m: A lot of heating oil and fuel comes to Switzerland by ship.

51755.q: What is stored in the tall silos at the port of Basel?
51755.e: Silos are tall towers for loose goods. At the port they are mainly used to store grain.
51755.m: Grain is stored in the port silos.

51756.q: What is the large port on the Kleinbasel side of the Rhine called?
51756.e: The port of Kleinhüningen lies on the right bank of the Rhine in the north of Basel. It has two large harbour basins.
51756.m: The port of Kleinhüningen is on the Kleinbasel side.

51757.q: What is at the very top of the Bernoulli Silo at the port of Basel?
51757.e: From the old silo you can look far out over the port and the point where three countries meet.
51757.m: There is a viewing platform on the Bernoulli Silo.

51758.q: Why are the Rhine ports so important for Switzerland?
a: Switzerland has too few railway lines
The Rhine is Switzerland's only river
Lorries are not allowed into Switzerland
51758.e: Switzerland does not border the sea. But via the Rhine it is still connected to the sea by ship.
51758.m: The Rhine ports give Switzerland a route to the sea.

51759.q: In which canton is the town of Olten?
51759.e: Olten is the largest town in the canton of Solothurn. It lies close to the border with Aargau.
51759.m: Olten is in the canton of Solothurn.

51760.q: Why is Olten railway station especially important?
a: It is the largest station in Switzerland
51760.e: The railway lines from Basel to Lucerne and from Bern to Zurich meet in Olten. That is why many travellers change trains there.
51760.m: Olten is an important railway junction.

51761.q: What does a special stone near Olten station mark?
51761.e: In the past, distances across the whole Swiss railway network were measured from Olten. A stone shows this zero point.
51761.m: Kilometre zero of the Swiss railway is in Olten.

51762.q: What is the old covered bridge over the Aare in Olten made of?
51762.e: The old bridge in Olten was built by a carpenter in 1803. It is made of wood and has a roof.
51762.m: The old bridge in Olten is a wooden bridge.

51763.q: At the foot of which mountain range does Olten lie?
51763.e: Just north of Olten, the hills of the Jura rise up. The town lies in the valley in front of them.
51763.m: Olten lies at the foot of the Jura.

51764.q: Roughly how many people live in Olten (as of 2022)?
51764.e: Olten is a medium-sized Swiss town. In 2022, a little more than 19,000 people lived there.

51765.q: When do especially many trains arrive in Olten at the same time?
a: On the hour and half hour
51765.e: Trains arrive in Olten on the hour and on the half hour. That way you can quickly change to another train.
51765.m: In Olten, trains meet on the hour and on the half hour.

51766.q: From Olten you can quickly get to Basel, Bern, Zurich and which other city?
51766.e: Olten lies almost in the middle between Basel, Bern, Zurich and Lucerne. You can reach all four cities in about an hour.
51766.m: Basel, Bern, Zurich and Lucerne are close to Olten.

51767.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the town of Olten?
51767.e: The Olten coat of arms shows three green fir trees on green hills. The background is white.
51767.m: There are three fir trees on the coat of arms of Olten.

51768.q: Which is the second-largest canton in Switzerland by area?
51768.e: Only the Grisons is larger than the canton of Bern. Bern stretches from the Jura to the Alps.
51768.m: The canton of Bern is the second-largest canton in Switzerland.

51769.q: What colours does the Bernese coat of arms have besides the black bear?
51769.e: The Bernese coat of arms is red. On it is a yellow stripe, along which the black bear walks.
51769.m: The Bernese coat of arms is red and yellow with a black bear.

51770.q: Since which year has Bern been part of the Swiss Confederation?
51770.e: In 1353, Bern made an alliance with Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. This made it part of the Confederation.
51770.m: Bern has been part of the Confederation since 1353.

51771.q: Which large dog breed with black, white and brown fur is named after Bern?
51771.e: The Bernese Mountain Dog comes from the canton of Bern. In the past it helped farmers and pulled small milk carts.
51771.m: The Bernese Mountain Dog has a three-coloured coat.

51772.q: What stands on many old fountains in Bern's Old Town?
51772.e: Many fountains in Bern's Old Town are over 450 years old. Brightly painted figures stand on their columns.
51772.m: The old fountains in Bern have colourful figures on them.

51773.q: Which dish with different kinds of meat and sauerkraut is typical of Bern?
51773.e: A Berner Platte has many kinds of meat and sausage on it. It is served with sauerkraut, beans and potatoes.
51773.m: The Berner Platte is a typical Bernese dish.

51774.q: Which painter has his own museum with wave-shaped roofs in Bern?
51774.e: The Zentrum Paul Klee stands on the edge of Bern. Its roofs look like three rolling hills.
51774.m: The Zentrum Paul Klee in Bern has wave-shaped roofs.

51775.q: What is the local mountain of the city of Bern called?
51775.e: The Gurten lies on the southern edge of Bern. You can go up by funicular railway.
51775.m: The Gurten is Bern's local mountain.

51776.q: What do many people in Bern do in the Aare in summer?
51776.e: In summer, many people in Bern jump into the Aare. They let the current carry them downstream.
51776.m: In summer, people in Bern love drifting down the Aare.

51777.q: According to an old legend, which animal helped the monk Gallus?
51777.e: According to the legend, a bear brought wood for Gallus's fire. As a reward it was given a piece of bread.
51777.m: In the legend of Gallus, a bear helps carry wood.

51778.q: What is the big fair for farming and food in St Gallen called?
51778.e: The Olma takes place in St Gallen every October. There are animals to see and specialities to try.
51778.m: The Olma is a big fair in St Gallen every autumn.

51779.q: Which sausage is a famous speciality from St Gallen?
51779.e: The St Gallen bratwurst is made from veal. Traditionally it is eaten without mustard.
51779.m: The St Gallen bratwurst is traditionally eaten without mustard.

51780.q: What was St Gallen known for all over the world around 1900?
51780.e: Around 1900, St Gallen was a centre of embroidery. Fine St Gallen lace was sold to many countries.
51780.m: Embroidery from St Gallen used to be in demand all over the world.

51781.q: What do visitors put on over their shoes in the Baroque Hall of the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
51781.e: The felt slippers protect the valuable wooden floor in the Baroque Hall. That way it does not get scratched when people walk on it.
51781.m: In the Abbey Library you wear felt slippers over your shoes.

51782.q: What do you mainly find in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
51782.e: The Abbey Library is one of the oldest libraries in the world. It owns very old manuscripts from the Middle Ages.
51782.m: The Abbey Library of St Gallen keeps very old books.

51783.q: Who wrote the books in the monastery of St Gallen in the Middle Ages?
51783.e: In the Middle Ages there were no printing presses yet. The monks carefully copied the books by hand.
51783.m: In the monastery of St Gallen, monks wrote the books by hand.

51784.q: What has the Abbey District of St Gallen with its library been since 1983?
51784.e: The Abbey District with its cathedral and library was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is considered especially valuable for the whole world.
51784.m: The Abbey District of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

51785.q: Which unusual treasure is kept in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
51785.e: The Abbey Library holds the mummy of a woman from Egypt called Shepenese. It is over 2600 years old.
51785.m: There is a mummy from Egypt in the Abbey Library of St Gallen.

51786.q: What is the nickname of the canton of Thurgau?
51786.e: A great many apple trees grow in Thurgau, and their fruit is made into cider (Most). That is why the canton is jokingly called Mostindien, “Cider India”.
51786.m: Thurgau is also called Mostindien because of its many apple trees.

51787.q: Which river gave the canton of Thurgau its name?
51787.e: The Thur flows right across the canton. The name Thurgau roughly means land on the Thur.
51787.m: Thurgau is named after the River Thur.

51788.q: Which lake does the canton of Thurgau lie on in the north?
51788.e: Thurgau has a long shore on Lake Constance. Places such as Arbon and Romanshorn lie right on the water.
51788.m: In the north, Thurgau borders Lake Constance.

51789.q: What was the Ittingen Charterhouse in Thurgau in the past?
51789.e: The Ittingen Charterhouse near Frauenfeld used to be a monastery of monks. Today it has museums, a hotel and a farm estate.
51789.m: The Ittingen Charterhouse is a former monastery in Thurgau.

51790.q: Where does the car ferry from Romanshorn go across Lake Constance?
51790.e: The ferry connects Romanshorn in Thurgau with Friedrichshafen in Germany. Cars and bikes can travel on it too.
51790.m: A ferry goes from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen.

51791.q: Which country lies opposite Thurgau on the other side of Lake Constance?
51791.e: From the Thurgau shore you can look across the lake to Germany. The German state of Baden-Württemberg lies there.
51791.m: Germany lies on the other side of the lake from Thurgau.

51792.q: In which place is the government of Appenzell Ausserrhoden based?
51792.e: Herisau is the largest place in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The government and the cantonal parliament meet there.
51792.m: The government of Appenzell Ausserrhoden is based in Herisau.

51793.q: Which old custom takes place in Urnäsch on New Year's Eve?
51793.e: The Silvesterchläuse go from house to house with big bells and costumes. They come on 31 December and on 13 January, the old New Year's Eve.
51793.m: In Urnäsch, the Silvesterchläuse go round on New Year's Eve.

51794.q: Which well-known children's village is in Trogen?
51794.e: The Pestalozzi Children's Village was founded in 1946 for children who had lost their homes in the war. Today it supports children all over the world.
51794.m: The Pestalozzi Children's Village is in Trogen.

51795.q: Why was the land of Appenzell divided into two parts in 1597?
51795.e: The Protestants and the Catholics could not agree. The Protestants formed Ausserrhoden, the Catholics Innerrhoden.
51795.m: Appenzell was divided in 1597 because of religion.

51796.q: What did Appenzell Ausserrhoden abolish in 1997?
51796.e: Until 1997, the voters met every year for the Landsgemeinde in the open air. Since then they have voted at the ballot box.
51796.m: Appenzell Ausserrhoden abolished the Landsgemeinde in 1997.

51797.q: Which high mountain lies on the border between the two Appenzells and St Gallen?
51797.e: The Säntis is 2502 metres high and the highest mountain in the Alpstein. Three cantons meet on its summit.
51797.m: Three cantons meet on the Säntis.

51798.q: Which animal can be seen on the coats of arms of both Appenzells?
51798.e: Both Appenzell coats of arms show a black bear standing upright. The Ausserrhoden coat of arms also has the letters V and R.
51798.m: A black bear stands on the coats of arms of both Appenzells.

51799.q: Which tangy cheese comes from the Appenzell region?
51799.e: Appenzeller cheese is rubbed with a herbal brine. The exact recipe for this brine is a secret.
51799.m: Appenzeller cheese is cared for with a secret herbal brine.

51800.q: What is the capital of Appenzell Innerrhoden called?
51800.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Appenzell. It has a colourful main street with painted houses.
51800.m: The capital of Appenzell Innerrhoden is called Appenzell.

51801.q: Which canton has the fewest inhabitants?
51801.e: Only about 16,000 people live in Appenzell Innerrhoden (as of 2023). No other canton has so few inhabitants.
51801.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the canton with the fewest inhabitants.

51802.q: When does the Landsgemeinde (open-air assembly) take place in Appenzell?
a: On the last Sunday in April
On the first Sunday in July
51802.e: On this Sunday, the voters gather on the Landsgemeinde square in Appenzell. They vote there by raising their hands.
51802.m: The Innerrhoden Landsgemeinde is on the last Sunday in April.

51803.q: What is the mountain inn that clings to a rock face in the Alpstein called?
51803.e: The Äscher mountain inn stands below the Ebenalp, built tight against a steep rock face. It became famous all over the world through photos.
51803.m: The Äscher mountain inn clings to a rock face in the Alpstein.

51804.q: What is the Wildkirchli in the Alpstein?
51804.e: The Wildkirchli is made up of caves below the Ebenalp. There is a small chapel inside, and bones of cave bears were found there.
51804.m: The Wildkirchli are caves with a chapel in the Alpstein.

51805.q: What is the sweet gingerbread with an almond filling from Appenzell called?
51805.e: The Appenzeller Biber is a gingerbread with a filling made of almonds. Often a picture is pressed into the dough.
51805.m: The Biber is a filled gingerbread from Appenzell.

51806.q: What colour are the trousers of the Appenzell herdsmen in their festive costume?
51806.e: The herdsmen's costume includes yellow leather trousers and a red waistcoat. You can see the herdsmen dressed like this when the cows go up to the alpine pastures, for example.
51806.m: Appenzell herdsmen wear yellow trousers with their costume.

51807.q: Which instrument is typical of Appenzell string music?
51807.e: The hammered dulcimer is played by striking the strings with small hammers. Together with violins and a bass, it sounds typical of Appenzell.
51807.m: The hammered dulcimer plays in Appenzell string music.

51808.q: What takes place on the Zaunplatz in the canton of Glarus on the first Sunday in May?
51808.e: At the Glarus Landsgemeinde, people vote in the open air by raising their hands. It takes place in the capital, Glarus.
51808.m: The Glarus Landsgemeinde is on the first Sunday in May.

51809.q: Who is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Glarus?
51809.e: The Glarus coat of arms shows Saint Fridolin as a pilgrim with a staff and a Bible. He is the patron saint of the canton.
51809.m: Saint Fridolin can be seen on the Glarus coat of arms.

51810.q: Which green cheese comes from the Glarus region?
51810.e: Schabziger gets its green colour and strong taste from blue fenugreek. It is often shaped like a small cone.
51810.m: Green Schabziger is a Glarus speciality.

51811.q: What shines through the Martinsloch onto the church of Elm in spring and autumn?
51811.e: The Martinsloch is a hole in the rock of the Tschingelhörner. On a few days in March and in autumn, the sun shines right through it onto the church tower of Elm.
51811.m: Twice a year, the sun shines through the Martinsloch onto the church of Elm.

51812.q: Which pass connects the canton of Glarus with the canton of Uri?
51812.e: The Klausen Pass leads from Linthal in Glarus over into the Schächen valley in Uri. The pass road is closed in winter.
51812.m: You get from Glarus to Uri over the Klausen Pass.

51813.q: What destroyed a large part of the town of Glarus in 1861?
51813.e: In 1861 a fire broke out during a strong Föhn wind and spread quickly. Afterwards Glarus was rebuilt with wide, straight streets.
51813.m: A great fire destroyed part of Glarus in 1861.

51814.q: Which famous ski racer comes from Elm in the Glarus region?
51814.e: Vreni Schneider grew up in Elm and won three Olympic gold medals. She is one of Switzerland's most successful ski racers.
51814.m: The ski racer Vreni Schneider comes from Elm.

51815.q: What is the Klettgau in the canton of Schaffhausen known for?
51815.e: In the Klettgau, for example in Hallau, many vines grow on sunny slopes. The red Pinot Noir is especially well known.
51815.m: A lot of wine is grown in the Klettgau in Schaffhausen.

51816.q: At what time does the Munot bell ring in Schaffhausen every evening?
51816.e: The little bell in the tower of the Munot rings every evening at 9 pm. In the past it signalled that the town gates were being closed.
51816.m: The Munot bell rings every evening at 9 pm.

51817.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of Schaffhausen?
51817.e: A black ram leaps on the Schaffhausen coat of arms. It fits the name Schaffhausen, which contains the German word for sheep.
51817.m: A black ram leaps on the Schaffhausen coat of arms.

51818.q: Which country borders the canton of Schaffhausen almost everywhere?
51818.e: The canton of Schaffhausen lies mostly north of the Rhine. It is almost completely surrounded by Germany.
51818.m: The canton of Schaffhausen is almost completely surrounded by Germany.

51819.q: What is the Old Town of Schaffhausen known for?
51819.e: An oriel is a small structure with windows that sticks out from the wall of a house. Schaffhausen has over 170 of them, and many are richly decorated.
51819.m: Schaffhausen is known for its many oriel windows.

51820.q: Which animals live in the moat around the Munot in Schaffhausen?
51820.e: Fallow deer have lived in the old moat of the Munot fortress for a long time. Visitors can watch them from above.
51820.m: Fallow deer live in the Munot moat.

51821.q: On which river is the town of Schaffhausen?
51821.e: The town of Schaffhausen lies right on the bank of the Rhine. In the past, ships had to unload their goods here.
51821.m: The town of Schaffhausen lies on the Rhine.

51822.e: At the Rhine Falls, the water of the Rhine plunges down over rocks. It is one of the best-known sights in Switzerland.
51822.m: The Rhine Falls is a large waterfall.

51823.q: Which sentence about the Rhine Falls is true?
a: It is one of the largest waterfalls in Europe
It is the highest waterfall in the world
It lies in the middle of the Alps
It freezes over completely every winter
51823.e: The Rhine Falls is one of the most powerful waterfalls in Europe. But it is not very high.
51823.m: The Rhine Falls is one of the largest waterfalls in Europe.

51824.q: What is the municipality on the Schaffhausen side of the Rhine Falls called?
51824.e: The municipality even has the waterfall in its name. On the other side of the river lies the Zurich municipality of Laufen-Uhwiesen.
51824.m: Neuhausen am Rheinfall lies on the Schaffhausen side of the waterfall.

51825.q: About how high is the Rhine Falls?
51825.e: The water falls about 23 metres. That is roughly as high as a house with seven floors.
51825.m: The Rhine Falls is about 23 metres high.

51826.q: About how wide is the Rhine Falls?
51826.e: The Rhine Falls is about 150 metres wide. That is longer than a football pitch.
51826.m: The Rhine Falls is about 150 metres wide.

51827.q: Which castle stands right above the Rhine Falls?
51827.e: Laufen Castle stands on a rock on the Zurich bank. From there, paths and platforms lead very close to the water.
51827.m: Laufen Castle towers above the Rhine Falls.

51828.q: How do you get onto the rock in the middle of the Rhine Falls?
51828.e: Small boats take visitors to the middle rock. Then you can climb up a staircase.
51828.m: You can only reach the rock in the Rhine Falls by boat.

51829.q: What travels over the bridge just above the Rhine Falls?
51829.e: A railway bridge crosses the Rhine above the waterfall. It was built as early as 1855 and 1856.
51829.m: The railway crosses a bridge at the Rhine Falls.

51830.q: Roughly when did the Rhine Falls form?
51830.e: The Rhine Falls formed about 14,000 to 17,000 years ago. At that time, after the Ice Age, the Rhine had to find a new bed.
51830.m: The Rhine Falls formed after the last Ice Age.

51831.q: Which two cantons border each other at the Rhine Falls?
51831.e: The Rhine forms the border at the waterfall. The right bank belongs to Schaffhausen, the left to Zurich.
51831.m: The cantons of Schaffhausen and Zurich meet at the Rhine Falls.

51832.q: Which island in Lake Constance is known for growing vegetables?
51832.e: On the island of Reichenau in the Untersee, lettuce, tomatoes and other vegetables grow in many fields and greenhouses. The island belongs to Germany.
51832.m: Reichenau is the vegetable island in Lake Constance.

51833.q: Which island in Lake Constance is known for its many flowers?
51833.e: The island of Mainau belongs to Germany. It is also called the flower island because thousands of flowers bloom there.
51833.m: Mainau is the flower island in Lake Constance.

51834.q: What is the nickname of Lake Constance?
51834.e: Lake Constance is so big that sometimes you can hardly see the other shore. That is why it is jokingly called the Swabian Sea.
51834.m: Lake Constance is also called the Swabian Sea.

51835.q: What happened to Lake Constance in the winter of 1963?
51835.e: In the cold winter of 1963, the whole lake froze over. The ice was so thick that people walked across it.
51835.m: In the winter of 1963, Lake Constance froze over completely.

51836.q: Which airships were built in Friedrichshafen on Lake Constance?
51836.e: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin built large airships on Lake Constance. They were named Zeppelins after him.
51836.m: The first Zeppelins were built on Lake Constance.

51837.q: Which is the largest town on Lake Constance?
51837.e: Konstanz is in Germany and has over 80,000 inhabitants. It borders directly on Kreuzlingen in Thurgau.
51837.m: Konstanz is the largest town on Lake Constance.

51838.q: What is the famous high railway bridge near Filisur in the Grisons called?
51838.e: The Landwasser Viaduct is about 65 metres high and leads straight into a tunnel in the rock face. The trains of the Albula line run over it.
51838.m: The Landwasser Viaduct near Filisur is a famous railway bridge.

51839.q: Which dish from the Grisons is wrapped in chard leaves?
51839.e: For capuns, a dough with small pieces of meat is wrapped in chard leaves. Then the little parcels are cooked in milk and stock.
51839.m: Capuns are dough parcels wrapped in chard from the Grisons.

51840.e: Bündnerfleisch is beef that is salted and then dried in the dry mountain air for weeks. It is eaten in thin slices.

51841.q: Which wild animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the Grisons?
51841.e: The coat of arms of the Grisons has three parts, and one of them shows a black ibex. The ibex is the best-known symbol of the canton.
51841.m: The ibex is the heraldic animal of the Grisons.

51842.q: How many countries does the canton of the Grisons border?
51842.e: The Grisons borders Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein. These borders mostly run through high mountains.

51843.q: What is the railway with the red trains in the Grisons called?
51843.e: The Rhaetian Railway runs over many bridges and through many tunnels. The Albula and Bernina lines are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
51843.m: The red trains in the Grisons belong to the Rhaetian Railway.

51844.q: Which sweet speciality comes from the Engadine?
51844.e: The Grisons nut tart is filled with walnuts and caramel. Confectioners from the Engadine made it famous.
51844.m: The nut tart is a well-known speciality from the Grisons.

51845.q: In which area of the Grisons is the story of Heidi set?
51845.e: Johanna Spyri had Heidi live with her grandfather on the alpine pasture above Maienfeld. That is why the area is now also called Heidiland.
51845.m: The story of Heidi is set near Maienfeld in the Grisons.

51846.q: Which pass connects the Grisons with Ticino?
51846.e: The A13 motorway runs over the San Bernardino Pass and through the tunnel beneath it. It connects Chur with Bellinzona.
51846.m: The San Bernardino connects the Grisons with Ticino.

51847.q: What is the deep gorge of the Hinterrhein near Thusis called?
51847.e: The Viamala is a narrow, deep rocky gorge. In the past the path through it was very dangerous, hence the name “bad road”.
51847.m: The Viamala is a gorge of the Hinterrhein.

51848.q: Which big meeting takes place in Davos every January?
51848.e: At the World Economic Forum, politicians and business people from all over the world meet. It is also called the WEF.
51848.m: The World Economic Forum takes place in Davos every January.

51849.q: Chur is the capital of which canton?
51849.e: Chur is the largest town and the capital of the canton. The government and the Great Council work there.
51849.m: Chur is the capital of the Grisons.

51850.e: People lived in the area around Chur more than 10,000 years ago. That is why Chur is often called the oldest town in Switzerland.
51850.m: Chur is often called the oldest town in Switzerland.

51851.q: Which river flows right through Chur?
51851.e: The Plessur comes from the Schanfigg valley and flows through the town. On the edge of town it flows into a larger river.

51852.q: Who has been based in Chur for many centuries?
51852.e: The Diocese of Chur is thought to be the oldest diocese north of the Alps. The bishop lives in the court district above the Old Town.
51852.m: A bishop is based in Chur.

51853.q: Which local mountain can you reach by cable car straight from Chur's Old Town?
51853.e: The cable car starts in the middle of the town of Chur. Up on Brambrüesch you can go hiking, and skiing in winter.
51853.m: A cable car goes from Chur up to Brambrüesch.

51854.q: Which railway runs right through the streets of Chur?
51854.e: The Arosa line starts at Chur station and first rolls through the town like a tram. Then it climbs up to Arosa.
51854.m: The Arosa line runs through the streets of Chur.

51855.q: What did the Romans call the town of Chur?
51855.e: The Romans had a base in Chur called Curia. This name later became Chur.

51856.q: On which large river is Chur?
51856.e: Chur lies in the Rhine valley of the Grisons. From there the Rhine flows on towards Lake Constance.

51857.q: Who is based next to the large cathedral in Chur?
51857.e: Chur is a bishop's town. The cathedral is the bishop's church, and he lives right next to it in the court.
51857.m: A bishop is based in Chur.

51858.q: What does the Romansh greeting “Allegra” mean?
51858.e: People in the Romansh-speaking Grisons greet each other with “Allegra”. The word originally means “be happy”.

51859.q: What does the Romansh word “aua” mean?
51859.e: “Aua” means water in Romansh. The word comes from the Latin “aqua”.

51860.q: Which ancient language did Romansh develop from?
51860.e: The Romans brought their language to the Alps. Over time, Romansh developed from it.
51860.m: Romansh comes from the Latin of the Romans.

51861.q: Into how many regional written forms is Romansh divided?
51861.e: There are five idioms: Sursilvan, Sutsilvan, Surmiran, Puter and Vallader. Each valley writes a little differently.
51861.m: Romansh has five regional written forms.

51862.q: What is the shared written language of Romansh speakers called?
51862.e: Rumantsch Grischun was created in 1982 as a shared written language. The federal government and the canton use it in official texts.
51862.m: Rumantsch Grischun is the shared written language of Romansh speakers.

51863.q: What does “bun di” mean in Romansh?
51863.e: “Bun” means good and “di” means day. Together they make a friendly greeting.

51864.q: What is the number “three” in Romansh?
51864.e: In Romansh you count “in, dus, trais”. “Tre” is Italian and “trois” is French.
51864.m: In Romansh, the number three is “trais”.

51865.q: What is the large art museum on Heimplatz in Zurich called?
51865.e: The Kunsthaus Zurich shows paintings and sculptures from many centuries. It is one of the largest art museums in Switzerland.
51865.m: The Kunsthaus is Zurich's large art museum.

51866.q: Which world football federation has its head office in Zurich?
51866.e: FIFA organises the Football World Cup. Its head office is in Zurich.

51867.q: Which figure is burnt at Zurich's spring festival, Sechseläuten?
51867.e: The snowman is called the Böögg and stands on a big pile of wood. The faster his head explodes, the better the summer is supposed to be.
51867.m: At Sechseläuten, Zurich burns the snowman Böögg.

51868.q: Which church in Zurich has the largest church clock face in Europe?
51868.e: The tower clock of St Peter's Church has huge clock faces. They are almost nine metres wide.
51868.m: St Peter's Church has the largest church clock face in Europe.

51869.q: What is the famous shopping street in Zurich called?
51869.e: The Bahnhofstrasse runs from the station to the lake. There are many shops and banks there.
51869.m: Zurich's best-known shopping street is the Bahnhofstrasse.

51870.q: Which artist made the colourful church windows in the Fraumünster in Zurich?
51870.e: Marc Chagall designed the five choir windows in the Fraumünster. They glow in blue, green, red and yellow.
51870.m: The windows in the Fraumünster are by Marc Chagall.

51871.q: Which country does the rainforest shown in the Masoala Hall at Zurich Zoo come from?
51871.e: Masoala is a peninsula on Madagascar. The hall at Zurich Zoo shows plants and animals from there.
51871.m: The Masoala Hall at Zurich Zoo shows rainforest from Madagascar.

51872.q: Into how many districts is the city of Zurich divided?
51872.e: Zurich is divided into districts 1 to 12. District 1 is the Old Town.
51872.m: The city of Zurich has twelve districts.

51873.q: What is the hill with lime trees in the middle of Zurich's Old Town called?
51873.e: The Lindenhof is a small hill with trees. The Romans already had a fort there.
51873.m: The Lindenhof is a lovely viewpoint in Zurich's Old Town.

51874.q: Which three cantons border Lake Zurich?
51874.e: Most of the lake belongs to the canton of Zurich. Smaller parts belong to Schwyz and St Gallen.
51874.m: Lake Zurich lies in the cantons of Zurich, Schwyz and St Gallen.

51875.q: On which island in Lake Zurich are there an old church and a chapel?
51875.e: On Ufenau stand the Church of St Peter and Paul and the Chapel of St Martin. The island belongs to Einsiedeln Abbey.
51875.m: There is an old church on the island of Ufenau in Lake Zurich.

51876.q: Which town on Lake Zurich is called the “Town of Roses”?
51876.e: Thousands of roses bloom in several gardens in Rapperswil. That is why the town is called the “Town of Roses”.
51876.m: Rapperswil on Lake Zurich is the Town of Roses.

51877.q: What is the sunny shore of Lake Zurich between Zollikon and Meilen called?
51877.e: The northern shore gets a lot of sun and has expensive houses. That is why it is called the Gold Coast.
51877.m: The sunny northern shore of Lake Zurich is called the Gold Coast.

51878.q: What is the left shore of Lake Zurich jokingly called?
51878.e: The left shore gets less sun than the shore opposite. That is why it is jokingly called the Pfnüselküste, because “Pfnüsel” is Swiss German for a runny nose.
51878.m: The left shore of Lake Zurich is jokingly called the Sniffle Coast.

51879.q: What do trains and cars travel over from Rapperswil to Pfäffikon SZ?
a: Through a tunnel under the lake
51879.e: The causeway separates two parts of the lake. Trains and cars have travelled over it since 1878.
51879.m: The causeway connects Rapperswil with Pfäffikon SZ.

51880.q: What is the upper part of Lake Zurich, east of Rapperswil, called?
51880.e: The Obersee (Upper Lake) lies above Rapperswil. The Linth flows into the lake there.
51880.m: The eastern part of Lake Zurich is called the Obersee.

51881.q: How deep is Lake Zurich at its deepest point?
51881.e: The deepest point lies between Herrliberg and Oberrieden. There the lake is about 136 metres deep.
51881.m: Lake Zurich is up to about 136 metres deep.

51882.q: How many towers does the Grossmünster in Zurich have?
51882.e: The Grossmünster has two identical towers. They are a landmark of Zurich.

51883.q: Which reformer preached in the Grossmünster from 1519?
51883.e: Huldrych Zwingli came to the Grossmünster as its priest in 1519. From here he changed the Church in Zurich.
51883.m: Huldrych Zwingli preached in the Grossmünster.

51884.q: According to a legend, which ruler founded the Grossmünster?
51884.e: According to the legend, the emperor followed a stag all the way to Zurich. There he had the graves of saints found.
51884.m: According to legend, Charlemagne founded the Grossmünster.

51885.q: Which patron saints of Zurich are honoured in the Grossmünster?
51885.e: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich. The Grossmünster stands over their graves.
51885.m: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich.

51886.q: Roughly how many steps lead up the tower of the Grossmünster that you can climb?
51886.e: 187 steps lead up the south tower, the Karlsturm. At the top there is a lovely view over Zurich.
51886.m: About 190 steps lead up the tower of the Grossmünster.

51887.q: How can you recognise the Grossmünster in Zurich from far away?
51887.e: The two towers of the Grossmünster are a landmark of Zurich. They stand by the Limmat in the Old Town.

51888.q: Which Church does the Grossmünster belong to today?
51888.e: Since the Reformation, the Grossmünster has been a Reformed church. It belongs to the Reformed Church of the canton of Zurich.
51888.m: The Grossmünster is a Reformed church.

51889.q: Which metal are the large doors of the Grossmünster made of?
51889.e: In 1950, Otto Münch created a door made of bronze. It shows pictures from the Bible.
51889.m: The doors of the Grossmünster are made of bronze.

51890.e: Building began around 1100. Around 1220 the church was finished.
51890.m: The Grossmünster was built in the Middle Ages.

51891.q: What is Zurich's local mountain called?
51891.e: The Uetliberg lies right on the edge of the city of Zurich. Many people go hiking there.
51891.m: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain.

51892.q: About how high is the Uetliberg?
51892.e: The summit of the Uetliberg is about 870 metres above sea level. So it is not a high mountain.
51892.m: The Uetliberg is about 870 metres high.

51893.q: Which S-Bahn line takes you from Zurich main station up the Uetliberg?
51893.e: The S10 runs from the main station to Uetliberg station. From there it is about a ten-minute walk to the summit.
51893.m: The S10 goes up the Uetliberg.

51894.q: What stands on the summit of the Uetliberg?
51894.e: From the observation tower you can see over Zurich, the lake and as far as the Alps. The present tower has stood since 1990.
51894.m: There is an observation tower on the Uetliberg.

51895.q: What can you see on the Planet Trail from the Uetliberg to the Felsenegg?
a: Models of the sun and planets
51895.e: On the Planet Trail, the planets are placed at the correct distances from each other, only greatly scaled down. That way you notice how huge the solar system is.
51895.m: The Planet Trail runs from the Uetliberg to the Felsenegg.

51896.q: Which chain of hills does the Uetliberg belong to?
51896.e: The Uetliberg is the northern end of the Albis chain. It runs along the left shore of Lake Zurich.
51896.m: The Uetliberg belongs to the Albis chain.

51897.q: The Uetliberg railway is said to be the ... standard-gauge railway without a cogwheel in Europe. What is missing?
51897.e: The Uetliberg railway climbs very steeply without a cogwheel. That makes it something special in Europe.
51897.m: The Uetliberg railway is the steepest standard-gauge railway without a cogwheel in Europe.

51898.q: Above which city does the Uetliberg rise?
51898.e: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain. The Uetliberg railway has run up it since 1875.
51898.m: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain.

51899.q: Which place does the cable car from the Felsenegg go down to?
51899.e: The cable car connects the Felsenegg with Adliswil in the Sihl valley. That way you can ride down comfortably after your hike.
51899.m: A cable car goes from the Felsenegg to Adliswil.

51900.q: In which year was the great hall of Zurich main station finished?
51900.e: The architect Jakob Friedrich Wanner built the station building. It was finished in 1871.
51900.m: The great hall of Zurich main station has stood since 1871.

51901.q: Where did the first railway line from Zurich go in 1847?
51901.e: The first railway line lying entirely within Switzerland ran from Zurich into Aargau. It opened in 1847.
51901.m: The first Swiss railway ran from Zurich to Baden in 1847.

51902.q: What was the nickname of Switzerland's first railway from 1847?
51902.e: The name comes from a fine pastry, the “Spanisch Brötli”. The railway made it possible to bring it fresh to Zurich.
51902.m: The first Swiss railway was called the Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn.

51903.q: Which colourful figure floats in the great hall of Zurich main station?
51903.e: The artist Niki de Saint Phalle created the colourful angel. It hangs high up in the hall.
51903.m: A colourful guardian angel floats in Zurich main station.

51904.q: Roughly how many travellers use Zurich main station on a weekday (as of 2023)?
51904.e: On a weekday, about 400,000 people come through the station. That is almost as many as live in the city of Zurich.
51904.m: About 400,000 people use Zurich main station every weekday.

51905.q: What is the shopping area under Zurich main station called?
51905.e: Shopville lies under the station and the station square. There are many shops there.
51905.m: The shopping area Shopville lies under Zurich main station.

51906.q: Whose monument stands in front of Zurich main station?
51906.e: Alfred Escher helped build railways in Switzerland and founded the North Eastern Railway. His monument has stood on the station square since 1889.
51906.m: The monument to Alfred Escher stands in front of Zurich main station.

51907.q: Which museum stands right next to Zurich main station?
51907.e: The National Museum looks like a castle. It shows the history of Switzerland.
51907.m: The National Museum stands next to Zurich main station.

51908.q: How many tracks for passenger trains does Zurich main station have?
51908.e: 16 tracks are above ground and another 10 are underground. Together that makes 26 tracks.
51908.m: Zurich main station has 26 tracks for passenger trains.

51909.q: What is the underground part of the station that opened in 2014 called?
51909.e: Löwenstrasse station lies deep below the tracks. Trains run through it right under the city.

51910.q: In terms of size, where does Winterthur rank among Swiss cities (as of 2023)?
51910.e: Winterthur has about 120,000 inhabitants. Only five Swiss cities are larger.
51910.m: Winterthur is the sixth-largest city in Switzerland.

51911.q: Which is the second-largest town in the canton of Zurich?
51911.e: After the city of Zurich, Winterthur has the most inhabitants in the canton. It lies in the north-east of the canton.
51911.m: Winterthur is the second-largest town in the canton of Zurich.

51912.q: What do many people call Winterthur for short?
51912.e: “Winti” is the short name for Winterthur. You hear it a lot in everyday life.

51913.q: What is the science centre in Winterthur where you can try out lots of things called?
51913.e: At the Technorama you can do your own experiments at many stations. It is the Swiss Science Center.
51913.m: At the Technorama in Winterthur you can do your own experiments.

51914.q: Which river flows through the town of Winterthur?
51914.e: The Eulach flows right through Winterthur. Today it flows in a channel in many places.

51915.q: Which counts are considered the founders of the town of Winterthur?
51915.e: The Counts of Kyburg had their castle nearby. They are considered the founders of Winterthur.
51915.m: The Kyburgs are considered the founders of Winterthur.

51916.q: Which company used to build large machines and ship engines in Winterthur?
51916.e: Sulzer was a huge factory in Winterthur for a long time. The Sulzer tower block was the tallest building in Switzerland from 1966 to 1978.
51916.m: The Sulzer company made Winterthur an industrial town.

51917.q: Winterthur's Old Town is the largest continuous ... in Switzerland. What is missing?
51917.e: Almost no cars drive in Winterthur's Old Town. You can walk everywhere.
51917.m: Winterthur's Old Town is a large pedestrian zone.

51918.q: Which nickname does Winterthur have because of its many gardens and green spaces?
51918.e: Winterthur has many parks and small allotment gardens. That is why it is called the Garden City.
51918.m: Winterthur is known as the Garden City.

51919.q: At the foot of which mountain range does Biel/Bienne lie?
51919.e: Behind Biel, the hills of the Jura rise steeply. In front of the town lies the flatter Swiss Plateau.
51919.m: Biel/Bienne lies at the foot of the Jura.

51920.q: Which two languages are spoken in Biel/Bienne?
51920.e: Many people in Biel speak German, and many others speak French. That is why the town is called Biel and Bienne.
51920.m: German and French are spoken in Biel/Bienne.

51921.q: What is special about the street signs in Biel/Bienne?
a: They are written in two languages.
They are all made of wood.
51921.e: Many people with different mother tongues live together in Biel/Bienne. That is why the street names are on the signs in both of the town's languages.
51921.m: The street signs in Biel/Bienne are bilingual.

51922.q: What is Biel/Bienne especially known for?
51922.e: Many companies in Biel make watches. The town is a centre of the Swiss watch industry.
51922.m: Biel/Bienne is an important watch town.

51923.q: On which lake is the town of Biel/Bienne?
51923.e: Biel/Bienne lies at the north-eastern end of Lake Biel. The lake is named after the town.

51924.q: What is the place above Biel with a large sports university called?
51924.e: The Federal Office of Sport is in Magglingen. Many athletes train there too.
51924.m: Switzerland's sports university is in Magglingen above Biel.

51925.q: What took place in Biel, among other places, in 2002?
51925.e: Expo.02 took place in Biel, Neuchâtel, Murten and Yverdon-les-Bains. Each town had its own exhibition site.
51925.m: The national exhibition Expo.02 also took place in Biel.

51926.q: Which river flows through the town of Biel/Bienne?
51926.e: The Schüss comes from the Jura. It flows through Biel into Lake Biel.

51927.q: What is Biel called in French?
51927.e: Biel is bilingual. That is why the town's official name is the double name Biel/Bienne.
51927.m: Biel is called Bienne in French.

51928.q: What is the covered wooden bridge with a sluice in Thun called?
51928.e: The Obere Schleuse (Upper Sluice) is an old covered bridge. It can be used to control the water level.
51928.m: The covered wooden bridge Obere Schleuse is in Thun.

51929.q: How many small corner turrets does the big tower of Thun Castle have?
51929.e: The big tower has a turret at each corner. That is why you can see it from far away.
51929.m: The tower of Thun Castle has four corner turrets.

51930.q: What does the Thun Panorama, one of the oldest circular paintings in the world, show?
51930.e: The circular painting shows Thun and the mountains around 1810. You stand in the middle and see it all around you.
51930.m: The Thun Panorama shows the town of Thun more than 200 years ago.

51931.q: Which dukes built the big tower of Thun Castle?
51931.e: The Dukes of Zähringen built the tower before 1200. The castle stands on a hill above the Old Town.

51932.e: From Thun you head into the mountains of the Bernese Oberland. That is why Thun is called this.
51932.m: Thun is the gateway to the Bernese Oberland.

51933.q: What is special about the Old Town of Thun?
a: Pavements on top of the shops
51933.e: These raised pavements are called Hochtrottoirs. You walk on the roofs of the lower shops and reach more shops that way.
51933.m: Thun has raised pavements above the shops.

51934.q: Roughly how many people live in the town of Thun (as of 2024)?
51934.e: About 44,000 people live in Thun. In the canton of Bern, only the cities of Bern and Biel are larger.

51935.q: What is Thun known for in the Swiss Army?
51935.e: The army trains many soldiers in Thun. Thun has the largest military training ground in Switzerland.
51935.m: Thun has the largest military training ground in Switzerland.

51936.q: What is the castle in a park on the lakeshore in Thun called?
51936.e: Schadau Castle stands in Schadau Park right on Lake Thun. The park is a popular place for a walk.
51936.m: Schadau Castle stands on the lakeshore in Thun.

51937.q: Which city is the second-largest in Switzerland?
51937.e: Geneva has over 200,000 inhabitants. Only Zurich is larger.
51937.m: Geneva is the second-largest city in Switzerland.

51938.q: Which city is the third-largest in Switzerland?
51938.e: Basel has about 176,000 inhabitants (as of 2023). The city lies on the Rhine.
51938.m: Basel is the third-largest city in Switzerland.

51939.q: Which city was the fifth-largest in Switzerland at the end of 2023?
51939.e: At the end of 2023, Bern had about 137,000 inhabitants. Only four Swiss cities were larger.
51939.m: Bern is one of the five largest cities in Switzerland.

51940.q: Which of these towns has the fewest inhabitants?
51940.e: Chur has about 40,000 inhabitants (as of 2024). Lucerne, St Gallen and Lugano all have over 60,000.
51940.m: Chur is smaller than Lucerne, St Gallen and Lugano.

51941.q: From how many inhabitants does a municipality in Switzerland count as a town in statistics?
51941.e: In statistics, a municipality with more than 10,000 inhabitants counts as a town. Whether it calls itself a town is up to the municipality.
51941.m: A Swiss municipality with over 10,000 inhabitants counts as a town.

51942.q: Which is the largest city in Central Switzerland?
51942.e: Lucerne lies on Lake Lucerne and has over 80,000 inhabitants. It is the seventh-largest city in Switzerland.
51942.m: Lucerne is the largest city in Central Switzerland.

51943.q: Which city on Lake Geneva was the fourth-largest in Switzerland at the end of 2023?
51943.e: At the end of 2023, Lausanne had about 144,000 inhabitants. It is the capital of the canton of Vaud.
51943.m: Lausanne is the fourth-largest city in Switzerland.

51944.q: Which is the largest town in the canton of the Grisons?
51944.e: Chur is the capital of the Grisons. The town is also considered one of the oldest in Switzerland.
51944.m: Chur is the largest town in the Grisons.

51945.q: Roughly how many municipalities in Switzerland count as towns (as of 2020)?
51945.e: About 170 municipalities have over 10,000 inhabitants. Most municipalities in Switzerland are smaller.

51946.q: Which Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
51946.e: The Old Town of Bern has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. It lies in a loop of the Aare.
51946.m: Bern's Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

51947.q: Which town has the old Musegg Wall with nine towers?
51947.e: The Musegg Wall used to protect the Old Town of Lucerne. You can climb some of its towers.
51947.m: The Musegg Wall with its towers is in Lucerne.

51948.q: Which little town with a castle gave its name to a well-known cheese?
51948.e: Gruyères lies on a hill in the canton of Fribourg. Gruyère cheese is named after this area.
51948.m: The little town of Gruyères gave Gruyère cheese its name.

51949.q: In which Old Town is the famous wooden Chapel Bridge?
51949.e: The Chapel Bridge with its water tower crosses the Reuss in Lucerne. It is one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe.
51949.m: The Chapel Bridge is in Lucerne's Old Town.

51950.q: Which town is called the “town of beautiful gables” because of the painted roofs on its houses?
51950.e: In Aarau's Old Town, the undersides of the roofs are brightly painted. That is why Aarau is called the “town of beautiful gables”.
51950.m: Aarau is the town of beautiful gables.

51951.q: In which Old Town is the Abbey District with a famous old library?
51951.e: The Abbey District of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its library is over 1000 years old.
51951.m: The famous Abbey Library is in St Gallen.

51952.q: Which town with a beautiful Baroque Old Town especially loves the number 11?
51952.e: Solothurn has, for example, 11 churches and chapels and 11 fountains. The number 11 can be found everywhere there.
51952.m: Solothurn is the town of the number 11.

51953.q: Which bilingual town has a large Old Town on the Saane?
51953.e: The Old Town of Fribourg lies on a rock above the Saane. It has many bridges and houses from the Middle Ages.
51953.m: Fribourg has a large Old Town on the Saane.

51954.q: What is the well-known part of Zurich's Old Town with many narrow lanes and pubs called?
51954.e: The Niederdorf is in Zurich's Old Town. People in Zurich also call it the “Dörfli” (little village).
51954.m: The Niederdorf is a lively part of Zurich's Old Town.

51955.q: Roughly how many municipalities does the canton of Zurich have (as of 2023)?
51955.e: The canton of Zurich has 160 municipalities. The largest is the city of Zurich.
51955.m: The canton of Zurich has about 160 municipalities.

51956.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Zurich?
51956.e: Every canton has a two-letter abbreviation. You can see it on number plates, for example.
51956.m: The abbreviation for the canton of Zurich is ZH.

51957.q: Roughly how many people live in the canton of Zurich (as of 2023)?
51957.e: About 1.6 million people live in the canton of Zurich. That is almost one in five people in Switzerland.
51957.m: About 1.6 million people live in the canton of Zurich.

51958.q: What is the highest mountain in the canton of Zurich called?
51958.e: The Schnebelhorn is about 1290 metres high. It lies in the Töss valley on the border with St Gallen.
51958.m: The Schnebelhorn is the highest mountain in the canton of Zurich.

51959.q: In which municipality is the largest airport in Switzerland?
51959.e: Zurich Airport lies in Kloten and other municipalities. It is the largest airport in Switzerland.

51960.q: Which lake lies entirely in the canton of Zurich?
51960.e: Lake Greifen lies between Uster and Zurich. It belongs entirely to the canton of Zurich.
51960.m: Lake Greifen lies entirely in the canton of Zurich.

51961.q: Which country does the canton of Zurich border?
51961.e: In the north, the Rhine forms the border with Germany. No other countries border the canton.
51961.m: The canton of Zurich borders Germany.

51962.q: Which typical Ticino dish is made from cornmeal?
51962.e: Polenta is a porridge made from cornmeal. In Ticino it is often eaten with meat, mushrooms or cheese.
51962.m: Polenta is a typical Ticino dish.

51963.q: What is the capital of the canton of Ticino called?
51963.e: Bellinzona is the capital of the canton of Ticino. The cantonal government works there.
51963.m: The capital of Ticino is Bellinzona.

51964.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Ticino border?
51964.e: Ticino lies in the south of Switzerland. It borders Italy to the west, south and east.

51965.q: On which side of the Alps is Ticino?
a: In the middle of the Swiss Plateau
51965.e: Ticino lies south of the Alps. That is why it is often warmer there than in the north of Switzerland.
51965.m: Ticino lies on the south side of the Alps.

51966.q: What is the number plate code of the canton of Ticino?
51966.e: The code TI stands for Ticino, the Italian name of the canton.
51966.m: Cars from Ticino have the code TI.

51967.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Ticino?
51967.e: The Ticino flag is divided in two: red on the left, blue on the right.
51967.m: The Ticino flag is red and blue.

51968.q: Since which year has Ticino been a canton of its own in Switzerland?
51968.e: Ticino became an independent canton in 1803. Before that, it was governed by other members of the Confederation.
