51968.m: Ticino has been a canton since 1803.

51969.q: What is a simple Ticino inn where people often eat outside under the trees called?
51969.e: A grotto is a simple Ticino inn. In the past these were cool cellars where wine and cheese were stored.
51969.m: In Ticino, people love eating in a grotto.

51970.q: What is the southernmost town in Switzerland, right on the border with Italy, called?
51970.e: Chiasso lies in the far south of Ticino. There is an important border crossing into Italy there.
51970.m: Chiasso is the southernmost town in Switzerland.

51971.q: How many famous castles stand in Bellinzona?
51971.e: The three castles of Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro stand in Bellinzona.

51972.q: What is the largest castle in Bellinzona called?
51972.e: Castelgrande means “big castle”. It stands on a rocky hill in the middle of the town.
51972.m: Castelgrande is the largest castle in Bellinzona.

51973.q: Which of Bellinzona's castles lies highest?
51973.e: Sasso Corbaro stands high above the town on the slope. From there you can see far down the valley.
51973.m: Sasso Corbaro is the highest of the three castles.

51974.q: Which famous list do the castles of Bellinzona belong to?
a: The Seven Wonders of the World
51974.e: Since 2000, the three castles and the town walls have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
51974.m: The castles of Bellinzona are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

51975.q: What were the castles of Bellinzona used for in the past?
a: They blocked the route through the valley
51975.e: Bellinzona lies at a narrow point in the valley. With castles and walls, the route to the Alpine passes could be blocked.
51975.m: The castles protected the route over the Alps.

51976.q: What connects Castelgrande castle with the River Ticino?
51976.e: From Castelgrande, a long wall called the Murata runs across the valley to the River Ticino.
51976.m: A long wall blocked the valley at Bellinzona.

51977.q: Which rulers from Italy had the castles of Bellinzona greatly extended?
51977.e: In the Middle Ages, Bellinzona belonged to Milan for a long time. The Dukes of Milan made the castles much bigger and stronger.
51977.m: The Dukes of Milan extended the castles of Bellinzona.

51978.q: What is the middle one of Bellinzona's three castles called?
51978.e: Montebello lies between Castelgrande below and Sasso Corbaro higher up the slope.
51978.m: Montebello is in the middle of the three castles.

51979.q: How can you easily get from the town centre up to the castle rock of Castelgrande today?
51979.e: There is a lift inside the rock of Castelgrande. It takes visitors up from the Old Town.
51979.m: A lift goes up through the rock to Castelgrande.

51980.q: On which lake is the town of Lugano?
51980.e: Lugano lies on the shore of Lake Lugano, which is named after the town.

51981.q: Which mountain right next to Lugano does a funicular run up from Paradiso?
51981.e: Monte San Salvatore stands by Lake Lugano. A funicular runs up it from Paradiso.
51981.m: A funicular runs up Monte San Salvatore.

51982.q: What is a second well-known viewpoint mountain near Lugano, on the other side of the bay, called?
51982.e: Monte Brè lies east of Lugano. A funicular runs up it too.
51982.m: Monte Brè is a viewpoint mountain near Lugano.

51983.q: In which city did the very first Eurovision Song Contest take place in 1956?
51983.e: The first Eurovision Song Contest was held in Lugano in 1956. Switzerland won it with Lys Assia.
51983.m: The first Eurovision Song Contest was in Lugano in 1956.

51984.q: What is the large park on the lakeshore in Lugano called?
51984.e: Parco Ciani is a beautiful city park right on Lake Lugano with old trees and flowers.
51984.m: Parco Ciani lies on the lakeshore in Lugano.

51985.q: In which village near Lugano does the “Swissminiatur” park show Switzerland in miniature?
51985.e: Swissminiatur is in Melide on Lake Lugano. You can see many Swiss buildings there in a very small size.

51986.q: Which sport does the well-known club HC Lugano play?
51986.e: HC stands for Hockey Club. HC Lugano plays in the top Swiss ice hockey league.
51986.m: HC Lugano is an ice hockey club.

51987.q: What is the cultural centre with a concert hall and art museum by the lake in Lugano called?
51987.e: LAC stands for Lugano Arte e Cultura. The building with a concert hall and a museum opened in 2015.
51987.m: At the LAC in Lugano there is art and music.

51988.e: Locarno lies on the northern shore of Lake Maggiore. Most of the lake belongs to Italy.

51989.q: Which animal is the symbol of the Locarno Film Festival?
51989.e: The festival's main prize is called the “Pardo d'oro”, which means Golden Leopard.
51989.m: The leopard is the symbol of the Locarno Film Festival.

51990.q: Where do thousands of people watch films together in the evening during the Locarno Film Festival?
51990.e: A huge screen is put up on the Piazza Grande. Many people watch films there in the open air.
51990.m: On the Piazza Grande in Locarno there is cinema under the stars.

51991.q: How do you get from Locarno up to the church of Madonna del Sasso?
51991.e: The church of Madonna del Sasso stands on a rock above the town. A funicular runs up from Locarno.
51991.m: The church of Madonna del Sasso stands above Locarno.

51992.q: What is Locarno known for when it comes to weather?
51992.e: Locarno is one of the sunniest places in Switzerland. The climate is mild.
51992.m: The sun often shines in Locarno.

51993.q: Which river flows into Lake Maggiore between Locarno and Ascona?
51993.e: The Maggia comes from the Maggia valley. It flows into the lake between the two towns.
51993.m: The Maggia flows into Lake Maggiore near Locarno.

51994.q: Which mountain above Locarno does a cable car go up?
51994.e: A cable car goes from Orselina above Locarno up to Cardada. From there you can see far across the lake.
51994.m: A cable car goes from Locarno up to Cardada.

51995.q: Since when has the Locarno Film Festival existed?
51995.e: The Locarno Film Festival took place for the first time in 1946. It is one of the oldest film festivals in the world.
51995.m: The Locarno Film Festival has existed since 1946.

51996.q: In which month does the Locarno Film Festival take place each year?
51996.e: The festival takes place every year in summer, usually in August.
51996.m: The Locarno Film Festival is in August.

51997.q: Which country does Switzerland share Lake Lugano with?
51997.e: Part of Lake Lugano lies in Switzerland and another part in Italy.
51997.m: Lake Lugano belongs to Switzerland and Italy.

51998.q: Which larger lake lies west of Lake Lugano?
51998.e: Lake Maggiore lies west of Lake Lugano. Lake Como lies to the east of it in Italy.
51998.m: Lake Maggiore lies west of Lake Lugano.

51999.q: What crosses Lake Lugano at Melide?
a: A causeway for road and rail
51999.e: At Melide, a causeway crosses the lake. Cars and trains travel south on it.
51999.m: At Melide, a causeway crosses Lake Lugano.

52000.q: Which Italian village on Lake Lugano is completely surrounded by Swiss territory?
52000.e: Campione d'Italia belongs to Italy but is completely surrounded by Swiss territory. It lies on Lake Lugano.
52000.m: Campione d'Italia is an Italian village on Lake Lugano.

52001.q: Which pretty village with lots of steps lies at the southern end of Lake Lugano?
52001.e: Morcote lies at the foot of Monte Arbostora right by the lake. It is known for its lanes and steps.
52001.m: Morcote is a beautiful village on Lake Lugano.

52002.q: Which village with old houses on the slope lies east of Lugano right by the lake?
52002.e: Gandria is an old fishing village on Lake Lugano. It lies close to the border with Italy.
52002.m: Gandria is an old village on Lake Lugano.

52003.q: How can you travel from place to place on Lake Lugano?
52003.e: Passenger boats run on Lake Lugano. They connect Lugano with villages such as Morcote and Gandria.

52004.e: Lake Lugano is narrow and has several arms between the mountains.
52004.m: Lake Lugano has several long arms.

52005.q: In which canton is the Swiss part of Lake Lugano?
52005.e: The Swiss part of Lake Lugano lies entirely in the canton of Ticino.
52005.m: The Swiss part of Lake Lugano lies in Ticino.

52006.q: Which trees, which usually grow further south, can often be seen in Ticino?
52006.e: Many palm trees grow in Ticino. They give the lakeside towns a southern look.
52006.m: Many palm trees grow in Ticino.

52007.q: Why can palm trees grow in Ticino?
52007.e: The winters in Ticino are mild. The Alps keep cold north winds away and the lakes store warmth.
52007.m: The mild climate lets palm trees grow in Ticino.

52008.q: What is the most common palm tree in Ticino called?
52008.e: The Chinese windmill palm can even cope with a little frost. That is why it is the most common palm in Ticino.
52008.m: The Chinese windmill palm is the most common palm in Ticino.

52009.q: Which continent does the Chinese windmill palm originally come from?
52009.e: The Chinese windmill palm originally comes from China in Asia. Later it was planted in gardens in Ticino.
52009.m: The Chinese windmill palm comes from Asia.

52010.q: What do the leaves of the Chinese windmill palm look like?
52010.e: The leaves of the Chinese windmill palm are large and round and divided into many strips, like an open fan.
52010.m: The Chinese windmill palm has fan-shaped leaves.

52011.q: What problem do Chinese windmill palms cause in Ticino's forests today?
a: They poison the water in streams
52011.e: Chinese windmill palms spread from gardens into the forest. There they take light and space away from native plants.
52011.m: Wild windmill palms crowd out native plants.

52012.q: On which islands in Lake Maggiore is there a garden with plants from all over the world?
52012.e: There is a botanical garden on the Brissago Islands. Plants from warm countries all over the world thrive there.
52012.m: There is a special garden on the Brissago Islands.

52013.q: Where in Ticino are there especially many palm trees?
52013.e: It is mildest by the lakes in winter. That is why palm trees mainly stand on the shores, for example in Lugano or Locarno.
52013.m: In Ticino, palm trees grow mainly by the lakes.

52014.q: What is special about the trunk of the Chinese windmill palm?
52014.e: The trunk of the windmill palm is wrapped in brown fibres. In the past, such fibres were used to make ropes, which is why its German name means “hemp palm”.
52014.m: The Chinese windmill palm has a trunk covered in fibres.

52016.q: Near which town does the Maggia valley begin?
52016.e: The Maggia valley branches off north of Locarno and leads far into the mountains.
52016.m: The Maggia valley begins near Locarno.

52017.q: What are the old houses in the Maggia valley usually built of?
52017.e: The old houses, called rustici, are built of stone. Even the roofs are often covered with stone slabs.
52017.m: The old houses in the Maggia valley are made of stone.

52018.q: What are the old stone houses in Ticino called?
52018.e: A rustico is a simple farmhouse made of stone. Many are now used as holiday homes.
52018.m: An old Ticino stone house is called a rustico.

52019.q: In which canton is the Maggia valley?
52019.e: The Maggia valley stretches north from Locarno into the mountains of Ticino. It is known for its stone houses and waterfalls.
52019.m: The Maggia valley is in Ticino.

52020.q: What is Mario Botta, who designed the round stone church in the Maggia valley?
52020.e: Mario Botta is a well-known architect from Ticino. He designed the round stone church in Mogno in the Maggia valley.
52020.m: Mario Botta is a famous Ticino architect.

52021.q: What can you find in many places in the bed of the River Maggia?
52021.e: Over a long time, the Maggia has worn the rocks smooth. In summer many people swim between the stones.
52021.m: The Maggia has shaped smooth rocks.

52022.q: Why was the church in Mogno in the Maggia valley rebuilt?
a: An avalanche had destroyed the old one
A fire had destroyed the old one
An earthquake had destroyed the old one
A flood had destroyed the old one
52022.e: An avalanche destroyed the old church of Mogno. Afterwards a modern round church was built of light and dark stone.
52022.m: The round stone church in the Maggia valley is in Mogno.

52023.q: Which language do people speak in the Maggia valley?
52023.e: The Maggia valley is in Ticino. Italian is spoken there.
52023.m: Italian is spoken in the Maggia valley.

52024.q: What is the water of the Verzasca famous for?
a: It is very clear and green
It is as cloudy as milk
It is as warm as an outdoor pool in summer
52024.e: The Verzasca has very clean, clear water. It shimmers green between the rocks.
52024.m: The Verzasca has clear, green water.

52025.q: What is the old stone bridge with two arches near Lavertezzo called?
52025.e: The Ponte dei Salti has two stone arches and crosses the Verzasca near Lavertezzo.
52025.m: The Ponte dei Salti is an old bridge in the Verzasca valley.

52026.q: What stands at the entrance to the Verzasca valley?
52026.e: The Contra dam stands at the entrance to the valley. Behind it lies the reservoir Lago di Vogorno.
52026.m: A dam stands at the entrance to the Verzasca valley.

52027.q: What brave thing can you do at the Verzasca dam?
52027.e: Brave people jump off the dam on an elastic rope. The jump became famous through a James Bond film.
52027.m: You can go bungee jumping at the Verzasca dam.

52028.q: About how high is the dam in the Verzasca valley?
52028.e: The Contra dam is about 220 metres high. It is one of the highest dams in Switzerland.
52028.m: The Verzasca dam is about 220 metres high.

52029.q: What is the last village at the far end of the Verzasca valley called?
52029.e: Sonogno lies right at the end of the Verzasca valley. Beyond it you can only go on foot.
52029.m: Sonogno is the last village in the Verzasca valley.

52030.q: What is the reservoir in the Verzasca valley called?
52030.e: Lago di Vogorno lies behind the dam. It was formed by damming the Verzasca.
52030.m: The reservoir in the Verzasca valley is called Lago di Vogorno.

52031.q: Why is swimming in the Verzasca dangerous?
a: The water can suddenly rise a lot
Dangerous fish live in the river
The river is only knee-deep everywhere
52031.e: After rain, or when water is let out of the reservoir, the river can quickly swell. The water is also very cold.
52031.m: You have to be very careful when swimming in the Verzasca.

52032.q: Which small stone village on the slope in the Verzasca valley used to be the smallest municipality in Switzerland?
52032.e: Corippo had only a few inhabitants and was the smallest municipality in Switzerland. Since 2020 it has been part of the municipality of Verzasca.
52032.m: Corippo was the smallest municipality in Switzerland.

52033.q: What does the Italian word “Grazie” mean?
52033.e: In Italian, you say “Grazie” when you want to thank someone.

52034.q: What does the Italian word “Buongiorno” mean?
52034.e: “Buongiorno” is a greeting for the morning and the day. “Buono” means good, “giorno” means day.

52035.q: Apart from Ticino, in which canton is Italian also spoken in some valleys?
52035.e: In southern valleys of the Grisons such as the Bregaglia and the Val Poschiavo, people speak Italian.
52035.m: Italian is also spoken in parts of the Grisons.

52036.q: What is the number “three” in Italian?
52036.e: In Italian you count: uno, due, tre. So “tre” is three.

52037.q: Where in Switzerland can you find Italian written outside Ticino too?
52037.e: All four national languages are on Swiss banknotes. That is why you find Italian there too.
52037.m: Italian is also written on Swiss banknotes.

52038.q: What does the Italian word “Ciao” mean?
52038.e: “Ciao” is a casual greeting. You say it when you arrive and when you leave.
52038.m: You say Ciao to say hello and goodbye.

52039.q: Which national language of Switzerland is spoken by the fewest people?
52039.e: Most people speak German, then French, then Italian. Romansh is spoken by the fewest.
52039.m: Romansh is spoken by the fewest people.

52040.e: Ascona lies on Lake Maggiore, right next to Locarno.

52041.q: Which town lies right next to Ascona?
52041.e: Ascona and Locarno lie next to each other on Lake Maggiore. You can go across on foot or by bike.
52041.m: Ascona lies right next to Locarno.

52043.q: Which music is at the heart of a well-known festival in Ascona?
52043.e: The JazzAscona festival takes place in Ascona every summer. Bands then play in the lanes and by the lake.

52044.q: Which trees grow on Ascona's lakeside promenade because it is so warm there?
52044.e: It is mild in Ticino. That is why even palm trees grow on Ascona's lakeside promenade.
52044.m: Palm trees grow by the lake in Ascona.

52045.q: Why do many people come to Ascona?
a: To go on holiday by the lake
52045.e: Ascona lies on warm Lake Maggiore. Many people go on holiday there.
52045.m: Ascona is a popular holiday resort.

52046.q: What are the lanes in Ascona's Old Town like?
52046.e: Ascona's Old Town has narrow, winding lanes with old houses.
52046.m: Ascona has an Old Town with narrow lanes.

52047.e: Ascona lies in the district of Locarno in the canton of Ticino.

52048.q: What does the River Maggia carry into the lake near Ascona?
52048.e: The Maggia brings a lot of sand and gravel down from the mountains. This is how flat land formed in the lake next to Ascona.
52048.m: The Maggia carries sand and stones into the lake.

52049.q: Which canton does the Misox belong to?
52049.e: The Misox is Italian-speaking but belongs to the canton of the Grisons.
52049.m: The Misox belongs to the Grisons.

52050.q: Which language is spoken in the Misox?
52050.e: The Misox lies south of the Alps. Italian is spoken there, even though it belongs to the Grisons.
52050.m: Italian is spoken in the Misox.

52051.q: Which Alpine pass leads through the Misox?
52051.e: The road over the San Bernardino runs through the Misox. There is also a road tunnel.
52051.m: The San Bernardino leads into the Misox.

52052.q: Which pass connects the Misox with the north of the Grisons?
52052.e: From the Misox, the road leads north over the San Bernardino Pass or through the tunnel into the Rheinwald.
52052.m: The San Bernardino connects the Misox with the north.

52053.q: What is the Misox called in Italian?
52053.e: In Italian, the valley is called Mesolcina.
52053.m: The Misox is called Mesolcina in Italian.

52054.q: What stands as a ruin on a rock near Mesocco in the Misox?
52054.e: The ruin of Mesocco Castle stands near Mesocco. It is one of the largest castle ruins in Switzerland.
52054.m: There is a large castle ruin near Mesocco.

52055.q: Which town does the Misox lead to in the south?
52055.e: In the south, the Misox ends near Bellinzona in Ticino.
52055.m: The Misox leads down to Bellinzona.

52056.q: Which canton does the Italian-speaking Misox belong to?
52056.e: The Misox is Italian-speaking but belongs to the canton of the Grisons. It borders Ticino.
52056.m: The Misox belongs to the Grisons.

52057.q: Which small side valley branches off the Misox?
52057.e: The Calanca valley is a side valley of the Misox. Together they form the Moesa region.
52057.m: The Calanca valley is a side valley of the Misox.

52058.q: Which country does the Matterhorn border?
52058.e: The border between Switzerland and Italy runs over the summit of the Matterhorn.
52058.m: The Matterhorn stands on the border with Italy.

52059.q: In which year did people first stand on top of the Matterhorn?
52059.e: In 1865, a roped team of Englishmen and mountain guides became the first to reach the summit. Four of them died on the way down.
52059.m: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865.

52060.q: What is the Matterhorn called in Italian?
52060.e: On the Italian side, the mountain is called Monte Cervino or simply Cervino.
52060.m: In Italian, the Matterhorn is called Monte Cervino.

52061.q: Which goat with a black front half is typical of the area around Zermatt?
52061.e: The Valais Blackneck goat is black at the front and white at the back. You often see it in Zermatt below the Matterhorn.
52061.m: The Blackneck goat lives in Valais.

52062.q: What is the well-known mountain hut on the ridge below the Matterhorn, where many climbers start from, called?
52062.e: The Hörnli Hut stands on the Hörnli Ridge above Zermatt. The usual climb up the Matterhorn starts from there.
52062.m: Climbers set off up the Matterhorn from the Hörnli Hut.

52063.q: Which mountain is the highest mountain in Switzerland?
52063.e: The Dufourspitze in Valais is higher than any other peak in Switzerland.
52063.m: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

52064.e: The Dufourspitze is 4634 metres high. No peak in Switzerland is higher.

52065.q: In which canton is the Dufourspitze?
52065.e: The Dufourspitze lies in the canton of Valais, not far from Zermatt.

52066.q: Which mountain group does the Dufourspitze belong to?
52066.e: The Dufourspitze is the highest peak of the large Monte Rosa massif.
52066.m: The Dufourspitze belongs to Monte Rosa.

52067.q: Who is the Dufourspitze named after?
52067.e: The mountain bears the name of General Guillaume-Henri Dufour from Geneva. He was an important officer and engineer.
52067.m: The Dufourspitze is named after General Dufour.

52068.q: What did General Dufour have made, which many people still know him for today?
52068.e: General Dufour led the work on the first accurate national map of Switzerland, the Dufour Map.
52068.m: General Dufour had an accurate map of Switzerland drawn.

52069.q: Which neighbouring country does the mountain massif of the Dufourspitze border?
52069.e: The Monte Rosa massif lies on the border between Switzerland and Italy.
52069.m: Monte Rosa lies on the border with Italy.

52070.q: Which famous mountain stands near Zermatt, not far from the Dufourspitze?
52070.e: The Dufourspitze and the Matterhorn both stand near Zermatt in Valais.
52070.m: The Matterhorn and the Dufourspitze stand near Zermatt.

52272.q: In which city does the Rhône leave Lake Geneva?
52272.e: In Geneva the Rhône flows out of the lake. Shortly afterwards it flows into France.
52272.m: The Rhône leaves Lake Geneva in Geneva.

52273.q: Which capital of the canton of Valais lies on the Rhône?
52273.e: Sion is called Sitten in German and is the capital of Valais. The town lies in the Rhône valley.

52274.q: In which direction does the Rhône flow through Valais?
52274.e: The Rhône begins in the east of Valais near the Furka Pass. It then flows west to Lake Geneva.
52274.m: In Valais the Rhône flows from east to west.

52275.q: What is the Rhône called in Upper Valais in the local Swiss German dialect?
52275.e: In German-speaking Upper Valais the Rhône is traditionally called Rotten. In French it is called Rhône.
52275.m: In Upper Valais the Rhône is called Rotten.

52276.q: Why are parts of the Rhône Glacier covered with white sheets in summer?
a: So that hikers can find the way
So that the ice stays clean
So that it gets warmer there
52276.e: The white sheets reflect the sunlight. This makes the ice near the ice grotto melt more slowly.
52276.m: White sheets protect the glacier ice from the sun.

52277.q: Roughly how long is the Inn?
52277.e: The Inn is about 517 kilometres long. Most of it lies in Austria and Germany.
52277.m: The Inn is about 500 kilometres long.

52278.q: Which sea does the water of the Inn end up in?
52278.e: The water of the Inn flows on east through Austria and Germany. Via a great river it finally reaches the Black Sea.
52278.m: The water of the Inn flows into the Black Sea.

52279.q: Which big river does the Inn flow into?
52279.e: The Inn flows through Austria and joins the Danube at Passau. Passau is in Germany.
52279.m: The Inn flows into the Danube.

52280.q: What is the Inn called in Romansh?
52280.e: In Romansh the Inn is called “En”. This is also where the name Engadine comes from.
52280.m: In Romansh the Inn is called En.

52281.q: In which canton does the Inn have its source?
52281.e: The Inn rises at Lake Lunghin high above Maloja in the Upper Engadine. That is in the canton of the Grisons.
52281.m: The Inn has its source in the Grisons.

52282.q: Which of these lakes does the Inn flow through?
52282.e: In the Upper Engadine the Inn flows through Lake Sils, Lake Silvaplana and Lake St Moritz. These lakes lie very high up.
52282.m: The Inn flows through Lake Sils.

52283.q: Which neighbouring country does the Inn flow into when it leaves Switzerland?
52283.e: The Inn leaves Switzerland in the Lower Engadine. After that it flows through Tyrol in Austria.
52283.m: The Inn flows from Switzerland into Austria.

52284.q: Which city in Austria has the Inn in its name?
52284.e: Innsbruck means “bridge over the Inn”. The city is the capital of Tyrol.

52285.q: Which famous holiday resort in the Engadine lies on a lake of the Inn?
52285.e: St Moritz lies on Lake St Moritz. The Inn flows through this lake.
52285.m: St Moritz lies on the Inn.

52286.q: Which valley does the Ticino flow through just after its source?
52286.e: The Bedretto Valley lies at the very top of Ticino. The young Ticino flows through this valley as far as Airolo.
52286.m: The young Ticino flows through the Bedretto Valley.

52287.q: Which language is spoken along the River Ticino in Switzerland?
52287.e: The Ticino flows through the canton of Ticino. Italian is spoken there.
52287.m: Italian is spoken along the Ticino.

52288.q: Which big lake does the Ticino flow into?
52288.e: The Ticino flows into Lake Maggiore on the Magadino plain near Locarno. The lake belongs to Switzerland and Italy.
52288.m: The Ticino flows into Lake Maggiore.

52289.q: Near which pass does the Ticino have its source?
52289.e: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass. The pass lies between Valais and Ticino.
52289.m: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass.

52290.q: Which town with three castles lies on the Ticino?
52290.e: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino. Its three castles are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52290.m: Bellinzona with its three castles lies on the Ticino.

52291.q: Which valley does the Ticino flow through after Airolo?
52291.e: From Airolo the Ticino flows south through the Leventina. The Gotthard road and railway also run through this valley.
52291.m: The Ticino flows through the Leventina.

52292.q: In which direction does the Ticino flow?
52292.e: The Ticino comes from the Alps and flows south. That is how it reaches Italy.

52293.q: Which famous wooden bridge in Lucerne crosses the Reuss?
52293.e: The Chapel Bridge is an old covered wooden bridge. It crosses the Reuss in Lucerne and has a water tower.
52293.m: The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne crosses the Reuss.

52294.q: In which canton does the Reuss have its source?
52294.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area in the canton of Uri. It flows through Andermatt and the Reuss valley of Uri.
52294.m: The Reuss rises in the canton of Uri.

52295.q: Which lake does the Reuss flow through?
52295.e: The Reuss flows into Lake Lucerne at Flüelen. In Lucerne it flows out again.
52295.m: The Reuss flows through Lake Lucerne.

52296.q: In which town does the Reuss leave Lake Lucerne?
52296.e: Lucerne lies at the western end of the lake. There the Reuss flows out of the lake and right through the old town.
52296.m: The Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne in Lucerne.

52297.q: What is the famous bridge over the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge called?
52297.e: The Devil's Bridge crosses the wild Reuss near Andermatt. An old legend says the Devil built it.
52297.m: The Devil's Bridge crosses the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge.

52298.q: Which second old wooden bridge with paintings crosses the Reuss in Lucerne?
52298.e: The Spreuer Bridge is a covered wooden bridge with old paintings. The Lake Bridge and the Reuss Bridge are newer bridges, and the Devil's Bridge is in the Schöllenen Gorge.
52298.m: The Spreuer Bridge crosses the Reuss in Lucerne.

52299.q: Roughly how long is the Reuss?
52299.e: The Reuss is about 164 kilometres long. It is one of the biggest rivers in Switzerland.
52299.m: The Reuss is about 160 kilometres long.

52300.q: Which village on the Gotthard lies on the Reuss?
52300.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren Valley. The Reuss flows right through this valley.

52301.q: In which direction does the Reuss flow from the Gotthard?
52301.e: The Reuss flows north from the Gotthard to Lake Lucerne. After that it carries on north to the Aare.
52301.m: The Reuss flows north from the Gotthard.

52302.q: Which big city does the Limmat flow through?
52302.e: The Limmat flows right through the old town of Zurich. The Grossmünster and the Fraumünster stand on its banks.

52303.q: Which lake does the Limmat flow out of?
52303.e: The Limmat begins at the lower end of Lake Zurich in Zurich. From there it flows north-west.
52303.m: The Limmat flows out of Lake Zurich.

52304.q: Roughly how long is the Limmat?
52304.e: The Limmat is about 36 kilometres long. It is a rather short river, but it carries a lot of water.
52304.m: The Limmat is a short river of about 35 kilometres.

52305.q: What is the river called that flows into Lake Walen and Lake Zurich before it becomes the Limmat?
52305.e: The Linth comes from the canton of Glarus. The water flows through Lake Walen and Lake Zurich and is then called the Limmat.
52305.m: After Lake Zurich the Linth becomes the Limmat.

52306.q: Which spa town in Aargau lies on the Limmat?
52306.e: The town of Baden lies on the Limmat. It has been known for its warm springs since Roman times.
52306.m: The spa town of Baden lies on the Limmat.

52307.q: Which big church with two towers stands in Zurich close to the Limmat?
52307.e: The Grossmünster stands in Zurich's old town close to the Limmat. Its two towers are a landmark of Zurich.
52307.m: The Grossmünster stands on the Limmat in Zurich.

52308.q: Which smaller river flows into the Limmat in Zurich?
52308.e: The Sihl comes from Lake Sihl. It joins the Limmat at the Platzspitz in Zurich.
52308.m: The Sihl flows into the Limmat in Zurich.

52309.q: Which bigger river does the Limmat flow into?
52309.e: The Limmat flows into the Aare near Brugg. The Reuss and the Aare also meet there.
52309.m: The Limmat flows into the Aare.

52310.q: Which town lies in the Limmat valley between Zurich and Baden?
52310.e: The Limmat flows from Zurich through the Limmat valley to Baden. Places such as Dietikon and Schlieren lie in this valley.
52310.m: Dietikon lies in the Limmat valley.

52311.q: What is the Saane called in French?
52311.e: In the French-speaking part of Switzerland the Saane is called “Sarine”. It flows through areas where German and French are spoken.
52311.m: In French the Saane is called the Sarine.

52312.q: Which bilingual cantonal capital lies on the Saane?
52312.e: Fribourg is called Freiburg in German. Its old town lies in a loop of the Saane.

52313.q: Which language border partly runs along the Saane?
52313.e: In the canton of Fribourg the Saane separates German-speaking and French-speaking areas in some places. In the town of Fribourg both languages are spoken.
52313.m: German and French meet on the Saane.

52314.q: What is the language border often linked with the Saane jokingly called?
52314.e: The “Röstigraben” (rösti ditch) means the border between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. The Saane is seen as a picture of this border.
52314.m: The Röstigraben separates German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland.

52315.q: Which river does the Saane flow into?
52315.e: The Saane flows north. In the canton of Bern it flows into the Aare.
52315.m: The Saane flows into the Aare.

52316.q: Which reservoir in the Gruyère region does the Saane flow through?
52316.e: The Saane is dammed at Rossens to form Lake Gruyère. In French it is called Lac de la Gruyère.
52316.m: The Saane flows through Lake Gruyère.

52317.q: Which village near Gstaad has almost the same name as the Saane?
52317.e: The Saane flows through Saanen near Gstaad. The village got its name from the river.
52317.m: The village of Saanen is named after the Saane.

52318.q: In which canton does the Saane have its source?
52318.e: The Saane rises at the Sanetschhorn in the canton of Valais. Then it flows north into the Bernese Oberland.

52319.q: Which of these cantons does the Saane not flow through?
52319.e: The Saane flows through Valais, Bern, Vaud and Fribourg. The Grisons lie far to the east.
52319.m: The Saane flows through western Switzerland and Bern.

52320.q: Which canton is named after the Thur?
52320.e: The name Thurgau means “land on the Thur”. The Thur flows right through the canton.
52320.m: Thurgau is named after the Thur.

52321.q: Which valley in the canton of St Gallen does the Thur flow through?
52321.e: The Thur rises in the upper Toggenburg. It flows through places such as Wattwil and Lichtensteig.
52321.m: The Thur flows through the Toggenburg.

52322.q: Which river does the Thur flow into?
52322.e: The Thur flows into the Rhine near Flaach. It is one of the big tributaries of the Rhine.
52322.m: The Thur flows into the Rhine.

52323.q: Near which mountain does the Thur have its source?
52323.e: The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg south of the Säntis. One of its source streams is called the Säntisthur.
52323.m: The Thur rises near the Säntis.

52324.q: Why can the Thur rise very quickly when it rains?
a: Because no lake catches the water
Because it comes from the sea
52324.e: The Thur does not flow through any big lake. That is why its water rises quickly when there is a lot of rain.
52324.m: Without a lake, the Thur rises quickly when it rains.

52325.q: Which town in Thurgau lies on the Thur?
52325.e: The Thur flows past Weinfelden. Arbon, Kreuzlingen and Romanshorn lie on Lake Constance.

52326.q: Which town in the canton of St Gallen lies on the Thur?
52326.e: The Thur flows past Wil before it reaches Thurgau. Rorschach lies on Lake Constance.

52327.q: Which three cantons does the Thur flow through?
52327.e: The Thur begins in St Gallen and flows through Thurgau. Finally, in the canton of Zurich, it flows into the Rhine.
52327.m: The Thur flows through St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich.

52328.q: Roughly how long is the Thur?
52328.e: The Thur is about 135 kilometres long. It flows from the Toggenburg to the Rhine.
52328.m: The Thur is about 135 kilometres long.

52329.e: The Emme is a river in the canton of Bern. It flows through the Emmental.

52330.q: Which cheese with big holes is named after the valley of the Emme?
52330.e: Emmental cheese originally comes from the Emmental. It is known for its big holes.
52330.m: Emmental cheese comes from the valley of the Emme.

52331.q: Which river does the Emme flow into?
52331.e: The Emme flows into the Aare near Solothurn. The mouth lies between Zuchwil and Luterbach.
52331.m: The Emme flows into the Aare.

52332.q: In which canton does the Emme have its source?
52332.e: The Emme rises in the Bernese Prealps. After that it flows through the Emmental.
52332.m: The Emme rises in the canton of Bern.

52333.q: Which town in the canton of Bern with a big castle lies on the Emme?
52333.e: Burgdorf lies on the Emme at the entrance to the Emmental. Burgdorf Castle stands above the old town.

52334.q: What was the Emme especially feared for in the past?
52334.e: In a heavy thunderstorm the Emme can rise very quickly. Jeremias Gotthelf described the great flood of 1837 in “The Flood in the Emmental”.
52334.m: The Emme used to be feared for its floods.

52335.q: What is another river with a similar name in the canton of Lucerne called?
52335.e: The Kleine Emme (Little Emme) is a separate river in the canton of Lucerne. It flows into the Reuss at Emmenbrücke.
52335.m: The Kleine Emme is a different river from the Emme.

52336.q: Roughly how long is the Emme?
52336.e: The Emme is about 82 kilometres long. That makes it much shorter than the Aare.
52336.m: The Emme is about 80 kilometres long.

52337.q: In which direction does the Emme flow through the Emmental?
52337.e: The Emme comes from the Prealps in the south. It flows north to the Aare near Solothurn.
52337.m: The Emme flows north to the Aare.

52338.q: Why is Switzerland called the “water tower of Europe”?
a: Because many big rivers have their source here
Because it lies by the sea
Because there are many castles here
52338.e: Big rivers such as the Rhine, the Rhône and the Inn rise in the Swiss Alps. Their water flows into many countries in Europe.
52338.m: Switzerland is the water tower of Europe because big rivers rise here.

52339.q: In which mountains do the big Swiss rivers mostly have their source?
52339.e: The Rhine, the Rhône, the Inn and the Ticino all rise in the Alps. There is a lot of snow and there are many glaciers there.
52339.m: The big Swiss rivers rise in the Alps.

a: A line where water flows away in different directions
A dam that separates two lakes
A bridge that crosses a river
A filter that makes water clean
52340.e: On each side of a watershed rainwater flows into different rivers. There are many such lines in the Swiss Alps.
52340.m: At a watershed, water flows away in different directions.

52341.q: Which mountain massif is seen as the centre of the water tower, because several rivers flow from there in all directions?
52341.e: The Rhine, the Rhône, the Reuss and the Ticino all rise around the Gotthard. They flow north, south, east and west.
52341.m: Several big rivers rise around the Gotthard.

52342.q: What stores a lot of water as ice in the Alps?
52342.e: Glaciers are huge masses of ice. When they melt in summer, they release water into the rivers.

52343.q: Roughly how many lakes are there in Switzerland?
52343.e: There are about 1500 lakes in Switzerland. Many of them are small mountain lakes.

52344.q: What does Switzerland use the water of its rivers and reservoirs for especially often?
52344.e: With hydroelectric power stations Switzerland turns flowing water into electricity. More than half of the electricity produced in Switzerland comes from hydropower (as of 2024).
52344.m: Switzerland makes a lot of electricity from hydropower.

52345.q: At which pass in the Engadine does the water divide towards three different seas?
52345.e: Three big river basins meet at the Lunghin Pass. Depending on the side, a raindrop ends up in the North Sea, the Black Sea or the Adriatic.
52345.m: At the Lunghin Pass the ways to three seas divide.

52346.q: Where does most of the water from Switzerland flow to?
a: Into a big lake in the mountains
52346.e: Almost all of Switzerland's rivers flow across the border. That is how many countries in Europe get water from the Swiss Alps.
52346.m: Swiss water flows into the neighbouring countries.

52347.q: Which two cantons does the Gotthard Pass connect?
52347.e: The road over the Gotthard leads from Andermatt in the canton of Uri to Airolo in the canton of Ticino.
52347.m: The Gotthard Pass connects Uri with Ticino.

52348.q: Roughly how high is the Gotthard Pass?
52348.e: The top of the Gotthard Pass lies at about 2107 metres above sea level.
52348.m: The Gotthard Pass is just over 2100 metres high.

52349.q: What does the old Tremola road on the Gotthard have a lot of?
52349.e: The Tremola winds down with many bends from the top of the pass to Airolo. It is paved with stones.
52349.m: The Tremola is the winding cobbled road on the Gotthard.

52350.q: What is the famous bridge in the Schöllenen Gorge on the way to the Gotthard called?
52350.e: The Devil's Bridge crosses the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge near Andermatt. There is a well-known legend about it.
52350.m: The Devil's Bridge is in the Schöllenen Gorge.

52351.q: Which river flows through the Schöllenen Gorge on the Gotthard?
52351.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area and flows down through the Schöllenen towards Lake Uri.
52351.m: The Reuss rushes through the Schöllenen Gorge.

52352.q: What has been a house for travellers at the top of the Gotthard Pass for centuries?
52352.e: There has been a hospice on the Gotthard since the Middle Ages. Travellers could spend the night and warm up there.
52352.m: Travellers found shelter in the hospice on the pass.

52353.q: Why is the Gotthard Pass road closed in winter?
a: Because of fog by the sea
Because of building work by the lake
52353.e: In winter there is a lot of snow on the pass and there is a danger of avalanches. That is why the road is closed for several months.
52353.m: In winter the Gotthard Pass is closed because of snow.

52354.q: In which year was the Gotthard road tunnel opened?
52354.e: The Gotthard road tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo was opened on 5 September 1980.
52354.m: Cars have driven through the Gotthard road tunnel since 1980.

52355.q: Which village lies at the northern foot of the Gotthard Pass in the canton of Uri?
52355.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren Valley on the north side of the Gotthard. Airolo lies on the south side in Ticino.
52355.m: Andermatt lies on the Uri side of the Gotthard.

52356.q: What travels through the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
52356.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel. That is why only trains travel through it.
52356.m: Only trains travel through the Gotthard Base Tunnel.

52357.q: Which record does the Gotthard Base Tunnel hold (as of 2025)?
a: Longest railway tunnel in the world
52357.e: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2025).
52357.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

52358.q: Which canton do you reach when you travel from the north through the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
52358.e: The tunnel begins at Erstfeld in the canton of Uri and ends at Bodio in Ticino.
52358.m: The Base Tunnel takes you to Ticino.

52359.q: How many tubes does the Gotthard Base Tunnel have for the trains?
52359.e: The tunnel consists of two tubes. In each tube the trains travel in one direction only.
52359.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel has two tubes.

52360.q: Why is the Gotthard Base Tunnel called a “base tunnel”?
a: It lies deep down at the foot of the mountain
It is the first tunnel in Switzerland
It leads to a military base
It has a station in the middle
52360.e: A base tunnel lies deep down, roughly at the level of the valleys. This means the trains hardly have to go uphill.
52360.m: A base tunnel runs flat through the foot of the mountain.

52361.q: What is an advantage of the Gotthard Base Tunnel for travellers?
a: The journey to Ticino is shorter
52361.e: Because the tunnel runs flat and straight through the mountain, trains reach Ticino faster than on the old mountain line.
52361.m: With the Base Tunnel you get to Ticino faster.

52362.q: Which country do you reach over the Great St Bernard from Valais?
52362.e: The Great St Bernard connects Valais with the Aosta Valley in Italy.
52362.m: Over the Great St Bernard you get to Italy.

52363.q: In which canton is the Swiss side of the Great St Bernard?
52363.e: The Great St Bernard lies in Lower Valais on the border with Italy.
52363.m: The Great St Bernard is in Valais.

52364.q: Roughly how high is the Great St Bernard?
52364.e: The top of the Great St Bernard Pass lies at about 2469 metres above sea level.
52364.m: The Great St Bernard is almost 2500 metres high.

52365.q: Who has looked after the hospice on the Great St Bernard for almost 1000 years?
52365.e: The hospice was founded in the 11th century. Canons live there, a kind of monk, who take in travellers.
52365.m: On the Great St Bernard, monks help travellers.

52366.q: Which famous dog is named after the Great St Bernard?
52366.e: The monks in the hospice on the Great St Bernard kept big dogs. They helped to find people in the snow. That is why they are called St Bernards.
52366.m: The St Bernard dog is named after the Great St Bernard.

52367.q: Which famous military leader crossed the Great St Bernard with his army in 1800?
52367.e: Napoleon Bonaparte crossed the Great St Bernard with many soldiers in May 1800 to march into Italy.
52367.m: Napoleon crossed the Great St Bernard in 1800.

52368.q: What lies right next to the hospice on the Great St Bernard?
52368.e: There is a small lake at the top of the pass. The border with Italy runs very close by.
52368.m: There is a small lake on the Great St Bernard.

52369.q: In winter, how do you get by car from Valais to Italy when the pass is closed?
52369.e: Since 1964 there has been a road tunnel under the Great St Bernard. It is open all year round.
52369.m: The tunnel under the Great St Bernard is open in winter too.

52370.q: Where does the St Bernard dog get its name from?
52370.e: These dogs were bred in the hospice on the Great St Bernard. That is why they are called St Bernards.
52370.m: The St Bernard dog is named after the Great St Bernard.

52371.q: What was the name of the most famous St Bernard rescue dog?
52371.e: Barry lived from 1800 to 1814 and worked for many years at the hospice on the Great St Bernard. He became famous as a lifesaver.
52371.m: Barry is the most famous St Bernard.

52372.q: How many people is the dog Barry said to have rescued?
52372.e: According to tradition, Barry rescued more than 40 people from the snow and cold. The exact number differs from source to source.

52373.q: Where can you see the stuffed dog Barry today?
a: In the Natural History Museum in Bern
In the Swiss National Museum in Zurich
In the Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne
52373.e: After his death Barry was preserved. Today he stands in the Natural History Museum in Bern.
52373.m: Barry stands in the Natural History Museum in Bern.

52374.q: What colours is a St Bernard's coat usually?
52374.e: St Bernards have a white coat with reddish-brown spots or patches.
52374.m: St Bernards are white with reddish-brown spots.

52375.q: How big are St Bernards compared with other dogs?
52375.e: St Bernards are among the biggest and heaviest dog breeds. They can weigh more than 60 kilograms.
52375.m: The St Bernard is a very big dog.

52376.q: What did St Bernards help the people in the hospice on the pass with in the past?
a: Finding people lost in the snow
52376.e: The dogs went with the helpers from the hospice and, with their good noses, found people who had got lost in the fog and snow.
52376.m: St Bernards searched for people lost in the snow.

52377.q: The St Bernard is seen as the national dog of which country?
52377.e: The St Bernard comes from Switzerland and is seen as the Swiss national dog.
52377.m: The St Bernard is the national dog of Switzerland.

52378.q: In which town in Valais can you visit St Bernards at the Barry Foundation today?
52378.e: The Fondation Barry in Martigny breeds St Bernards. You can visit the dogs at Barryland.
52378.m: You can visit St Bernards in Martigny.

52379.q: Which two countries does the Simplon Pass connect?
52379.e: The Simplon Pass leads from Brig in Valais to Domodossola in Italy.
52379.m: The Simplon Pass leads from Switzerland to Italy.

52380.q: At which town in Valais does the road over the Simplon Pass begin?
52380.e: The Simplon road starts in Brig in Upper Valais and then climbs up to the top of the pass.
52380.m: The Simplon road begins in Brig.

52381.q: Roughly how high is the Simplon Pass?
52381.e: At the top of the pass the Simplon road reaches about 2000 metres above sea level.
52381.m: The Simplon Pass is about 2000 metres high.

52382.q: Who had the first road for vehicles built over the Simplon around 1800?
52382.e: Napoleon wanted to get his cannons over the Alps. That is why he had the Simplon road built from 1801 to 1805.
52382.m: Napoleon had the Simplon road built.

52383.q: Which big stone animal stands on the Simplon Pass?
52383.e: A big stone eagle stands at the top of the pass. It is a reminder of the soldiers who guarded the border in the Second World War.
52383.m: A stone eagle stands on the Simplon Pass.

52384.q: What is the railway tunnel that runs under the Simplon Pass called?
52384.e: The Simplon Tunnel connects Brig with Iselle in Italy. It was opened in 1906.
52384.m: Under the Simplon, trains run through the Simplon Tunnel.

52385.q: Which rich merchant from Valais had a big palace built in Brig and used the Simplon for trade?
52385.e: In the 17th century Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper traded salt over the Simplon. His Stockalper Palace stands in Brig.
52385.m: Stockalper traded over the Simplon and built a palace in Brig.

52386.q: What is there for travellers on the Simplon Pass, similar to the Great St Bernard?
52386.e: A big hospice stands on the Simplon Pass. It is looked after by the same canons as the hospice on the Great St Bernard.
52386.m: There is a hospice on the Simplon Pass too.

52387.q: Which two cantons does the Furka Pass connect?
52387.e: The Furka Pass leads from Realp in the canton of Uri over to Goms in the canton of Valais.
52387.m: The Furka Pass connects Uri with Valais.

52388.q: Which big glacier lies right next to the Furka Pass?
52388.e: On the western side of the Furka there is a big glacier that reaches close to the pass road. Many people visit an ice grotto there.
52388.m: The Rhône Glacier lies near the Furka Pass.

52389.q: Which big lake does the Rhône, which rises at the Rhône Glacier, flow into?
52389.e: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier near the Furka. It flows through Valais into Lake Geneva.
52389.m: The Rhône flows from the Rhône Glacier into Lake Geneva.

52390.q: Roughly how high is the Furka Pass?
52390.e: The top of the Furka Pass lies at about 2429 metres above sea level.
52390.m: The Furka Pass is about 2400 metres high.

52391.q: Which famous film agent drove over the Furka Pass in a film?
52391.e: In the 1964 James Bond film “Goldfinger” there is a car chase on the Furka road.
52391.m: James Bond drove over the Furka in the film “Goldfinger”.

52392.q: What can you visit at the Rhône Glacier on the Furka road?
a: An ice grotto in the glacier
52392.e: Every year an ice grotto is cut into the Rhône Glacier. You can walk through the blue ice inside it.
52392.m: There is an ice grotto in the Rhône Glacier.

52393.q: What kind of train runs over the old mountain line on the Furka in summer?
52393.e: The Furka Cogwheel Steam Railway runs in summer with old steam locomotives between Realp and Oberwald.
52393.m: A steam railway runs on the Furka in summer.

52394.q: How can cars be taken under the Furka in winter?
a: On a car train through the tunnel
52394.e: Car trains run through the Furka Base Tunnel between Realp and Oberwald. That way you can get to Valais in winter too.
52394.m: In winter cars go through the Furka Tunnel on the train.

52395.q: Which two cantons does the Grimsel Pass connect?
52395.e: The Grimsel Pass leads from Innertkirchen in the Bernese Oberland over to Upper Valais.
52395.m: The Grimsel Pass connects Bern with Valais.

52396.q: Roughly how high is the Grimsel Pass?
52396.e: The top of the Grimsel Pass lies at about 2164 metres above sea level.
52396.m: The Grimsel Pass is just over 2100 metres high.

52397.q: What do you see a lot of at the Grimsel?
52397.e: At the Grimsel several valleys were blocked with high walls. That is how big artificial lakes were created.
52397.m: There are many reservoirs at the Grimsel.

52398.q: What is the water of the reservoirs at the Grimsel used for?
52398.e: The water flows through pipes to power stations. There it drives turbines that produce electricity.

52399.q: What lies right next to the road at the top of the Grimsel Pass?
a: A farm with cows in the shed
52399.e: At the top of the Grimsel Pass the small Totensee lies right next to the road.
52399.m: There is a small lake on the Grimsel.

52400.q: What is the valley on the Bern side of the Grimsel Pass called?
52400.e: The Grimsel road climbs up through the Haslital. Meiringen and Innertkirchen lie there.
52400.m: The Haslital lies on the Bern side of the Grimsel.

52401.q: Which small place lies on the Valais side below the Grimsel and the Furka?
52401.e: Gletsch lies on the valley floor between the Grimsel Pass and the Furka Pass. From there you can drive over both passes.
52401.m: Gletsch lies between the Grimsel and the Furka.

52402.q: Which big reservoir lies near the top of the Grimsel Pass on the Bern side?
52402.e: Lake Grimsel is a reservoir behind a high dam. It lies near the top of the pass.
52402.m: Lake Grimsel is a reservoir at the Grimsel.

52403.q: Which two cantons does the Susten Pass connect?
52403.e: The Susten Pass leads from Innertkirchen in the canton of Bern into the Reuss valley of Uri.
52403.m: The Susten Pass connects Bern with Uri.

52404.q: Roughly how high is the Susten Pass?
52404.e: The top of the Susten Pass lies at about 2260 metres above sea level.
52404.m: The Susten Pass is just over 2200 metres high.

52405.q: Which glacier lies right next to the Susten road?
52405.e: Below the top of the pass on the Bern side lies the Stein Glacier. The Hotel Steingletscher stands next to it.
52405.m: The Stein Glacier lies on the Susten road.

52407.q: How does the Susten road get through the top of the pass?
52407.e: Right at the top the road goes through a short summit tunnel. After that it goes back down on the other side.
52407.m: At the top of the Susten you drive through a short tunnel.

52408.q: Which village in Uri lies at the end of the Susten road on the eastern side?
52408.e: On the Uri side the Susten road ends in Wassen in the Reuss valley. There it meets the Gotthard road.
52408.m: The Susten road ends in Wassen.

52409.q: Is the Susten Pass open to cars in winter?
52409.e: Because of snow and avalanches, the Susten Pass is closed for several months in winter.
52409.m: In winter the Susten Pass is closed.

52410.q: Which small lake lies by the Stein Glacier on the Susten?
52410.e: The Steinsee formed in front of the Stein Glacier when the ice melted.
52410.m: The Steinsee lies by the Stein Glacier.

52411.q: In which canton is the Julier Pass?
52411.e: The Julier Pass lies entirely in the canton of the Grisons in the east of Switzerland.
52411.m: The Julier Pass is in the Grisons.

52412.q: Which valley do you reach over the Julier Pass?
52412.e: The Julier road leads from the Oberhalbstein over the pass into a long high valley through which the Inn flows.
52412.m: Over the Julier Pass you drive into the Engadine.

52413.q: Roughly how high is the Julier Pass?
52413.e: The top of the Julier Pass lies at 2284 metres above sea level.
52413.m: The Julier Pass is almost 2300 metres high.

52414.q: Which old stone remains stand on the Julier Pass?
a: Boundary stones from the Middle Ages
52414.e: In Roman times there was a shrine on the Julier. The columns next to the road are remains of it.
52414.m: Columns from Roman times stand on the Julier.

52415.q: What do cars sometimes need in winter on snowy pass roads like the Julier?
52415.e: Snow chains are put around the wheels. This means cars slip less on snow and ice.
52415.m: Snow chains help cars on snowy roads.

52416.q: Which village at the Engadine end of the Julier Pass lies on a lake?
52416.e: Silvaplana lies on Lake Silvaplana in the Upper Engadine. This is where the Julier road ends.
52416.m: The Julier road ends in Silvaplana.

52417.q: Is the Julier Pass usually open in winter?
52417.e: The Julier Pass is cleared of snow in winter, so it can usually be driven on all year round.
52417.m: The Julier Pass is usually open in winter too.

52419.q: Which two cantons does the Lötschberg Tunnel connect?
52419.e: The old Lötschberg Tunnel leads from the Bernese Oberland under the mountain into Valais.
52419.m: The Lötschberg Tunnel connects Bern with Valais.

52420.q: At which village in the canton of Bern does the old Lötschberg Tunnel begin?
52420.e: The northern entrance of the old Lötschberg Tunnel is in Kandersteg. The southern entrance is in Goppenstein.
52420.m: The old Lötschberg Tunnel begins in Kandersteg.

52421.q: How can you travel by car through the old Lötschberg Tunnel?
a: On a road in the tunnel
52421.e: There is no road in the old Lötschberg Tunnel. Cars are carried on trains between Kandersteg and Goppenstein.
52421.m: Cars go through the Lötschberg on the train.

52422.q: In which year was the Lötschberg Base Tunnel opened?
52422.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel was opened in 2007. It lies much deeper than the old Lötschberg Tunnel.
52422.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel has been in use since 2007.

52423.q: Roughly how long is the Lötschberg Base Tunnel?
52423.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 34.6 kilometres long. In the south you come out near Raron in Valais.
52423.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 35 kilometres long.

52424.q: At which place does the Lötschberg Base Tunnel begin in the north?
52424.e: The northern entrance of the base tunnel is near Frutigen in the Kander valley. In the south you come out near Raron in Valais.
52424.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel begins near Frutigen.

52425.q: In which year was the old Lötschberg Tunnel opened?
52425.e: The old Lötschberg Tunnel is a railway tunnel and was opened in 1913.
52425.m: The old Lötschberg Tunnel has been open since 1913.

52426.q: Where do travellers from Bern get to faster thanks to the Lötschberg Tunnel?
52426.e: Trains run through the Lötschberg from Bern directly to Visp and Brig in Valais.
52426.m: Thanks to the Lötschberg you are soon in Valais.

52427.q: What sound does the horn of the PostBus make on mountain roads?
52427.e: The post horn plays three notes one after the other, which sound like “Tü-ta-to”.

52428.q: Why does the PostBus sound its horn before tight bends on pass roads?
a: So that others hear it coming
52428.e: On tight bends you cannot see the oncoming traffic. The horn warns others that a big bus is coming.
52428.m: The PostBus sounds its horn as a warning before tight bends.

52429.q: Who has right of way on roads with the blue “mountain postal road” sign?
52429.e: On a mountain postal road the other vehicles must make way for the PostBus and follow the driver's instructions.
52429.m: On mountain postal roads the PostBus has right of way.

52430.q: What is shown on the sign for a mountain postal road?
52430.e: The sign is blue and shows a yellow post horn. It shows that the PostBus has right of way here.
52430.m: A yellow post horn marks a mountain postal road.

52431.q: When do PostBuses drive over most of the high Alpine passes?
52431.e: Most passes are closed in winter because of snow. That is why the pass PostBuses run mainly in summer.
52431.m: The PostBus goes over the high passes in summer.

52432.q: Apart from travellers, what did the PostBus carry in the past?
52432.e: The PostBus replaced the mail coach. It brought people, but also letters and parcels, to the villages.
52432.m: In the past the PostBus also brought letters and parcels.

52433.q: What travelled over the passes before there were PostBuses?
52433.e: In the past horses pulled the mail coaches over the passes. Later the PostBuses replaced the coaches.
52433.m: Before the PostBus, the mail coach went over the passes.

52434.q: Why is a very tight bend called a “hairpin bend”?
a: It is as thin as a hair
It was built by a hairdresser
52434.e: The road turns almost completely back on itself. From above this looks like a bent hairpin.
52434.m: A hairpin bend has the shape of a hairpin.

52435.q: Why do pass roads have lots of hairpin bends?
a: So that the road is not too steep
So that the road is shorter
So that you can drive faster
So that you see more trees
52435.e: The road zigzags up the mountain. That makes it less steep than if it went straight up.
52435.m: Hairpin bends make a mountain road less steep.

52436.q: What is another name for a hairpin bend?
52436.e: Hairpin bends are also called switchbacks, because the road almost turns back.
52436.m: A hairpin bend is also called a switchback.

52437.q: How should a car drive through a hairpin bend?
52437.e: In a hairpin bend you cannot see far and the bend is tight. That is why you must drive slowly.
52437.m: You drive slowly in hairpin bends.

52438.q: Seen from above, what shape does a pass road with many hairpin bends have?
52438.e: The road goes back and forth up the mountain. From above it looks like a zigzag or a snake.
52438.m: Seen from above, many bends look like a zigzag.

52439.q: What often stands at the edge of hairpin bends so that cars do not leave the road?
52439.e: Crash barriers or walls at the roadside stop vehicles if they go too wide on the bend.
52439.m: Crash barriers protect cars on tight bends.

52440.q: Who often has to swing out wide to get round a tight hairpin bend?
52440.e: Long vehicles such as PostBuses or coaches need a lot of space on tight bends. That is why they need the whole width of the road.
52440.m: Long buses need a lot of space on hairpin bends.

52441.q: Which cycle race sometimes goes over Swiss passes with hairpin bends?
52441.e: The Tour de Suisse is a cycle race through Switzerland. The professionals often ride over steep passes.
52441.m: The Tour de Suisse often goes over passes.

52442.q: In which year was the first railway tunnel through the Gotthard opened?
52442.e: The old Gotthard railway tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo was opened in 1882. At that time it was the longest tunnel in the world.
52442.m: Trains have run through the Gotthard since 1882.

52443.q: Which river rises in the Grimsel area and flows through the Haslital?
52443.e: The Aare rises at the Aare glaciers near the Grimsel. It flows through the Haslital into Lake Brienz.
52443.m: The Aare comes from the Grimsel.

52444.q: Between which two mountain ranges does the Swiss Plateau lie?
a: The Black Forest and the Alps
52444.e: The Swiss Plateau lies between the Jura in the north-west and the Alps in the south.
52444.m: The Swiss Plateau lies between the Jura and the Alps.

52445.q: Which motorway runs right across the Swiss Plateau from Geneva to St Gallen?
52445.e: The A1 connects many big cities on the Swiss Plateau, for example Lausanne, Bern and Zurich.
52445.m: The A1 runs right across the Swiss Plateau.

52446.q: What does the landscape on the Swiss Plateau usually look like?
52446.e: On the Swiss Plateau there are gentle hills, fields, forests, lakes and many towns.
52446.m: The Swiss Plateau is hilly and has many fields.

52447.q: Which big city lies on the Swiss Plateau?
52447.e: Zurich is the biggest city in Switzerland and lies on the Swiss Plateau. The other places are in the mountains.
52447.m: Zurich lies on the Swiss Plateau.

52448.q: Which river flows right across the Swiss Plateau and through Bern?
52448.e: The Aare flows through Bern, Solothurn and Aarau. It is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.
52448.m: The Aare flows through Bern and the Swiss Plateau.

52449.q: Why are there so many farms on the Swiss Plateau?
52449.e: On the Swiss Plateau the soil is fertile and the land is not so steep. That is why grain, potatoes and vegetables grow well there.
52449.m: The soil on the Swiss Plateau is fertile.

52450.q: Which big lake lies in the far south-west of Switzerland?
52450.e: Lake Geneva lies in the far south-west of Switzerland. It is the biggest lake that Switzerland has a share of.
52450.m: Lake Geneva lies in the south-west of Switzerland.

52451.q: Roughly how much of Switzerland's area is Swiss Plateau?
52451.e: The Swiss Plateau makes up about 30 per cent of Switzerland's area. That is roughly a third.
52451.m: The Swiss Plateau is about a third of Switzerland.

52452.q: In which part of Switzerland are the Jura Mountains?
52452.e: The Jura stretches across the north-west of Switzerland from Geneva to the area around Schaffhausen.
52452.m: The Jura lies in the north-west of Switzerland.

52453.q: Which rock is the Jura mainly made of?
52453.e: The Jura is mainly made of limestone. You often find fossilised shells and caves in it.
52453.m: The Jura is mainly made of limestone.

52454.q: Are the mountains in the Jura higher or lower than the Alps?
52454.e: The highest Jura peaks in Switzerland are only about 1700 metres high. In the Alps there are peaks over 4000 metres.
52454.m: The Jura mountains are lower than the Alps.

52455.q: Which craft has long been famous in the Jura?
52455.e: In the Jura, for example in La Chaux-de-Fonds, watches have been made for centuries.
52455.m: The Jura is famous for its watchmakers.

52456.q: Which Jura mountain above Lake Biel has a tall transmitter tower?
52456.e: The Chasseral is 1606 metres high. Next to the summit stands a transmitter tower 120 metres tall.
52456.m: There is a transmitter tower on the Chasseral.

52457.q: What is the huge rock basin in the Neuchâtel Jura called?
52457.e: The Creux du Van is a big rock basin with high, curved cliffs in the canton of Neuchâtel.
52457.m: The Creux du Van is a rock basin in the Jura.

52458.q: Which period of the dinosaurs is named after the Jura?
52458.e: The rocks in the Jura gave a period of Earth's history its name. Many dinosaurs lived in the Jurassic.
52458.m: The Jurassic is named after the Jura Mountains.

52459.q: Which big bird of prey also hunts marmots in the Alps?
52459.e: The golden eagle has very sharp eyes and strong talons. It is big and strong enough to hunt hares and marmots.
52459.m: The golden eagle hunts in the Alps.

52460.q: Which white flower with felty leaves grows high up in the Alps?
52460.e: Edelweiss grows on stony meadows in the mountains. It is protected and must not be picked.
52460.m: Edelweiss grows high up in the Alps.

52461.q: Which nimble animal with short, hook-shaped horns leaps over rocks?
52461.e: The chamois is very agile and leaps safely over steep rocks. Its horns are bent like a hook at the end.
52461.m: The chamois leaps safely over rocks.

52462.q: Which animal with long, curved horns climbs in the Alps?
52462.e: The ibex lives high up among the rocks. The males have long, curved horns.
52462.m: The ibex climbs among the rocks of the Alps.

52463.q: What is the way over a mountain from one valley to another called?
52463.e: A pass is the lowest point between two mountains. Roads lead over it from one valley to the next.
52463.m: A pass takes you from one valley to another.

a: Snow that slides down the slope
A storm on a mountain lake
A big rock in the river
52464.e: In an avalanche a lot of snow breaks loose and slides quickly down the mountain. Avalanches can be very dangerous.
52464.m: An avalanche is snow sliding down a mountain.

52465.q: Which two big rivers rise in the Swiss Alps?
52465.e: The Rhine and the Rhône have their sources in the Swiss Alps in the Gotthard area.
52465.m: The Rhine and the Rhône rise in the Alps.

52466.q: How does the temperature change when you climb a high mountain?
a: It gets colder first and then warmer
52466.e: For every 100 metres of height it gets on average just over half a degree colder. That is why there is often snow at the top.
52466.m: The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

a: Between the Swiss Plateau and the Alps
In the middle of the Jura
52467.e: The Prealps form the transition from the flat Swiss Plateau to the high Alps.
52467.m: The Prealps lie between the Swiss Plateau and the Alps.

52468.q: What is there usually none of in the Prealps?
52468.e: The Prealps are lower than the High Alps. That is why there are hardly any glaciers there, but many meadows and forests.
52468.m: There are hardly any glaciers in the Prealps.

52469.q: Which mountain near Lucerne is called the “Queen of the Mountains”?
52469.e: The Rigi lies between Lake Lucerne and Lake Zug. From the top there is a beautiful view.
52469.m: The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”.

52470.q: What do farmers do in summer with the grass on steep slopes in the Prealps?
a: They mow it and make hay
52470.e: The grass is mown and dried. The cows eat the hay in winter.
52470.m: Farmers make hay from the grass for the winter.

52471.q: What do farmers do with their cows in summer in the Prealps?
a: They drive them up to the alpine pasture
They keep them in the shed
They bring them down into the valley
They take them to the city
52471.e: In summer the farmers take the cows up to the alpine pasture. There they eat fresh grass.
52471.m: In summer the cows go up to the alpine pasture.

52472.q: Which railway was the first mountain railway in Europe, running up a mountain from 1871?
52472.e: The Vitznau-Rigi railway was opened in 1871. It was the first mountain railway in Europe.
52472.m: The Rigi Railway is the oldest mountain railway in Europe.

52473.q: Which Prealpine mountain rises in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg?
52473.e: The Moléson is a well-known viewpoint mountain in the Gruyère region. Gruyère cheese is made in this area.
52473.m: The Moléson is the local mountain of the Gruyère region.

52474.q: In which canton is the Engadine?
52474.e: The Engadine is a long high valley in the canton of the Grisons in the east of Switzerland.
52474.m: The Engadine is in the Grisons.

52475.q: Which river flows through the Engadine?
52475.e: In Romansh the Inn is called “En”. That is where the Engadine gets its name.
52475.m: The Inn flows through the Engadine.

52476.q: Which language do many people in the Engadine speak besides German?
52476.e: Romansh is one of the four national languages of Switzerland. It is still often spoken in the Engadine.
52476.m: Romansh is spoken in the Engadine.

52477.q: Which well-known holiday resort in the Engadine has hosted the Olympics twice?
52477.e: The Winter Olympics took place in St Moritz in 1928 and 1948.
52477.m: St Moritz has hosted the Olympics twice.

52478.q: What is the children's book about a boy from the Engadine and a bell called?
52478.e: Ursli wants to carry the biggest bell at the spring festival. The story takes place in Guarda.
52478.m: Ursli with his bell comes from the Engadine.

52479.q: Which festival do children in the Engadine celebrate with bells on 1 March?
52479.e: At Chalandamarz the children go through the village with bells and drive away the winter.
52479.m: At Chalandamarz the children ring the winter away.

52480.q: Which pastry with nuts is a speciality from the Engadine?
52480.e: The Engadine nut tart is filled with walnuts and caramel.
52480.m: The Engadine nut tart is filled with nuts.

52481.q: Which famous cross-country skiing race takes place in the Engadine every year?
52481.e: In the Engadine Ski Marathon thousands of people ski cross-country from Maloja to S-chanf.
52481.m: The Engadine Ski Marathon is a cross-country ski race.

52482.q: Where does the water of the Inn end up?
52482.e: The Inn flows into Austria and joins the Danube at Passau. The Danube flows into the Black Sea.
52482.m: The water of the Inn reaches the Black Sea.

52483.q: Which caves on Lake Thun are named after a monk who is said to have driven away a dragon?
52483.e: According to legend, the monk Beatus drove a dragon out of the cave. Today you can visit the stalactite cave.
52483.m: The St Beatus Caves lie on Lake Thun.

52484.q: Which viewpoint right above Interlaken can be reached by funicular?
52484.e: The Harder funicular runs from Interlaken up to Harder Kulm. From there you can see two lakes and many mountains.

52485.q: What is the open-air museum with old Swiss houses near Brienz called?
52485.e: At Ballenberg there are over a hundred old houses from all over Switzerland. You can see how people used to live.
52485.m: There are old Swiss houses at Ballenberg.

52486.q: What is the Lauterbrunnen valley especially known for?
52486.e: In the Lauterbrunnen valley many waterfalls plunge over steep cliffs, for example the Staubbach Falls.
52486.m: There are many waterfalls in the Lauterbrunnen valley.

52487.q: What can you see on the Schynige Platte near Interlaken?
52487.e: Hundreds of mountain plants grow in the alpine garden on the Schynige Platte. You go up on an old cog railway.
52487.m: There is an alpine garden on the Schynige Platte.

52488.q: Which canton does the Bernese Oberland belong to?
52488.e: The Bernese Oberland is the southern, mountainous part of the canton of Bern.
52488.m: The Bernese Oberland belongs to the canton of Bern.

52489.q: Which famous ski race takes place in Wengen every year?
52489.e: The best skiers in the world race on the Lauberhorn near Wengen. The downhill is said to be the longest in the World Cup.
52489.m: The Lauberhorn race takes place in Wengen.

52490.q: On which mountain above Mürren is there a revolving restaurant?
52490.e: The restaurant on the Schilthorn slowly turns in a circle. That way you can see all the mountains around while you eat.
52490.m: There is a revolving restaurant on the Schilthorn.

52491.q: Which pass connects Meiringen with the canton of Obwalden?
52491.e: Cars and trains travel over the Brünig Pass from the Bernese Oberland to Obwalden.
52491.m: The Brünig Pass leads from Meiringen to Obwalden.

52492.q: What do the cheesemakers in the Emmental make in big copper vats?
52492.e: The milk is heated in the copper vat and thickened. Big wheels of cheese are made from it.
52492.m: In the copper vat milk becomes cheese.

52493.q: What is the small house next to an Emmental farm, where the grandparents often live, called?
52493.e: When the young people take over the farm, the parents move into the Stöckli next to the big house.
52493.m: The grandparents often live in the Stöckli.

52494.q: What does the landscape in the Emmental look like?
52494.e: The Emmental is a hilly landscape with meadows, forests and scattered farms.
52494.m: There are lots of green hills in the Emmental.

52495.q: Which sport in sawdust is very popular in the Emmental?
52495.e: In Swiss wrestling (Schwingen) two men or women in special canvas shorts wrestle in sawdust. There are many well-known wrestlers in the Emmental.
52495.m: Swiss wrestling is very popular in the Emmental.

52496.q: What is typical of the old farmhouses in the Emmental?
52496.e: Emmental farmhouses have huge roofs that reach almost to the ground.

52497.q: What kind of bridges do you often see in the Emmental?
52497.e: Several old wooden bridges with a roof cross the Emme. This keeps the wood dry.
52497.m: There are covered wooden bridges in the Emmental.

52498.q: Which viewpoint mountain, about 1400 metres high, lies on the edge of the Emmental?
52498.e: The Napf is about 1400 metres high and lies on the border between the cantons of Bern and Lucerne. From the top you can see far across the hills.
52498.m: The Napf is a viewpoint mountain by the Emmental.

52499.q: What can you find in the streams around the Napf if you are lucky?
52499.e: There are tiny flakes of gold in the Napf streams. You can wash them out with a pan.
52499.m: There is gold in the Napf streams.

52500.q: Which glacier is the biggest in the Alps?
52500.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the whole of the Alps. It has more ice than any other Alpine glacier.
52500.m: The Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the Alps.

52501.q: In which canton is the Aletsch Glacier?
52501.e: The Aletsch Glacier flows down the south side of the Bernese Alps into Valais.
52501.m: The Aletsch Glacier is in Valais.

52502.q: Roughly how long is the Aletsch Glacier?
52502.e: The Aletsch Glacier is about 20 kilometres long. But because of the warmth it gets shorter every year.
52502.m: The Aletsch Glacier is about 20 kilometres long.

52503.q: What is happening to the Aletsch Glacier because it is getting warmer and warmer?
52503.e: Because it is getting warmer, more ice melts than new ice is added. That is why the Aletsch Glacier gets shorter every year.
52503.m: The Aletsch Glacier is getting shorter because of the warmth.

52504.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage Site does the Aletsch Glacier belong to?
52504.e: The Jungfrau-Aletsch area was listed in 2001 as the first natural World Heritage Site in the Alps.
52504.m: The Aletsch Glacier belongs to the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site.

52505.q: From which viewpoint mountain do you get a good view of the Aletsch Glacier?
52505.e: From the Eggishorn near Fiesch you can see far across the long river of ice.
52505.m: You can see the Aletsch Glacier from the Eggishorn.

52506.q: Does the ice of the Aletsch Glacier move?
a: Yes, it slowly flows down the valley
52506.e: Glacier ice is heavy and flows very slowly down the valley, at the Aletsch up to about 200 metres a year.
52506.m: Glacier ice slowly flows down the valley.

52507.q: Which very old trees grow in the Aletsch Forest above the glacier?
52507.e: In the Aletsch Forest there are Swiss stone pines that are several hundred years old. Swiss stone pines grow high up in the mountains.
52507.m: Ancient Swiss stone pines grow in the Aletsch Forest.

52508.q: Why are the glaciers in Switzerland melting?
a: It is getting warmer and warmer
52508.e: Because of climate change it is getting warmer. In summer more ice melts than new ice is added in winter.
52508.m: The glaciers are melting because it is getting warmer.

52509.q: Roughly how many glaciers are there in Switzerland?
52509.e: There are about 1400 glaciers in Switzerland. Many of them are very small.

52510.q: What is part of the ice at the Rhône Glacier covered with in summer?
52510.e: White sheets reflect the sunlight. This makes the ice near the ice grotto melt a little more slowly.
52510.m: White sheets protect the ice from the sun.

52511.q: What is often left behind when a glacier melts?
52511.e: The glacier leaves rubble behind. In hollows the meltwater collects to form new lakes.
52511.m: Where a glacier melts, stones and lakes are left behind.

52512.q: What is the meltwater from glaciers important for in summer?
52512.e: In hot summers meltwater fills the rivers. Without glaciers some streams then carry less water.
52512.m: Glaciers give water to the rivers in summer.

52513.q: Which glacier was given a farewell with a funeral ceremony in 2019?
52513.e: The Pizol Glacier in the canton of St Gallen had almost completely disappeared. So people held a funeral ceremony for it.
52513.m: The Pizol Glacier was given a farewell in 2019.

52514.q: On a glacier trail, how can you see where the ice used to be?
a: From signs with years on them
From colourful flags on the ice
52514.e: On the way to some glaciers, for example the Morteratsch Glacier, signs show where the ice used to be. The glacier has already retreated a long way.
52514.m: Signs show where the glacier used to be.

52515.q: In which year did the Swiss glaciers lose a particularly large amount of ice, about 6 per cent?
52515.e: The summer of 2022 was very hot and dry. The Swiss glaciers lost about 6 per cent of their ice.
52515.m: A particularly large amount of glacier ice melted in 2022.

52516.q: How many national parks are there in Switzerland?
52516.e: The Swiss National Park is the only national park in Switzerland.

52517.q: In which canton is the Swiss National Park?
52517.e: The national park lies in the east of Switzerland, in the Lower Engadine in the canton of the Grisons.
52517.m: The national park is in the Grisons.

52518.q: In which year was the Swiss National Park founded?
52518.e: The park was founded in 1914. It is the oldest national park in the Alps.
52518.m: The national park was founded in 1914.

52519.q: What are you not allowed to do in the national park?
52519.e: In the national park nature should remain undisturbed. That is why you must not pick anything and must stay on the paths.
52519.m: You do not pick flowers in the national park.

52520.q: Which big bird was released back into the wild in the national park?
52520.e: The bearded vulture had died out in the Alps. From 1991 young bearded vultures were released in the national park.
52520.m: Bearded vultures were released in the national park.

52521.q: Which big animal with antlers do you often see in the national park?
